articles.title: OpenAI creó un grupo asesor de matemáticos después de que su IA resolviera más de 100 problemas abiertos en un mes
articles.text:
OpenAI anunció la creación de un grupo asesor independiente de matemáticos, con sede en el Instituto de Estudios Avanzados de Princeton, después de revelar que un modelo interno resolvió más de 100 problemas matemáticos abiertos desde el 28 de agosto de 2026, además de una demostración disputada del problema Navier-Stokes, uno de los siete Problemas del Milenio.
El Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence surge como respuesta a una carta abierta firmada por veinticinco matemáticos ganadores de la Medalla Fields, que acusó a las empresas de inteligencia artificial de usar los problemas abiertos como vidriera competitiva y de dañar el trabajo intelectual genuino de la disciplina.
PUBLICIDAD
Una polémica que empezó con Navier-Stokes
La tensión se desató a comienzos de septiembre de 2026, cuando el matemático de la Universidad de Nueva York, Tristan Buckmaster publicó, junto al investigador de Anthropic Levent Alpöge, avances preliminares sobre el problema Navier-Stokes usando modelos de Codex y Claude.
Buckmaster denunció públicamente que un equipo paralelo de OpenAI se había enterado del progreso de su investigación antes de que fuera pública y utilizó una ventaja de cómputo para llegar primero a una demostración completa.
Según su propio relato, cuando pidió explicaciones sobre cuándo había comenzado OpenAI a trabajar en el problema, las respuestas de la compañía se volvieron cada vez más evasivas. Horas después de que Buckmaster hiciera pública su versión, OpenAI publicó una demostración completa del problema de existencia y suavidad de Navier-Stokes, atribuida a un modelo interno de próxima generación todavía sin nombre comercial definitivo.
PUBLICIDAD
OpenAI confirmó buena parte de la cronología: reconoció que su intento por resolver Navier-Stokes había comenzado el 1 de septiembre de 2026, después de escuchar rumores de que dos matemáticos habían avanzado usando inteligencia artificial. La compañía también admitió conversaciones con Buckmaster y Alpöge mientras ambos equipos avanzaban en paralelo sobre el mismo problema.
Más de cien problemas resueltos en un mes por OpenAI
El comunicado publicado por OpenAI precisó que, a partir del 28 de agosto de 2026, comenzó a entrenar un nuevo modelo interno que, además de resolver Navier-Stokes, terminó dando solución a más de 100 problemas abiertos de larga data distribuidos en la mayoría de las áreas de la matemática. La compañía describió el ritmo de esos resultados como algo que sorprendió a sus propios matemáticos internos.
PUBLICIDAD
Ese progreso se suma a un antecedente de agosto de este año, cuando OpenAI ya había publicado diez avances en matemática y ciencias de la computación teórica —entre ellos la construcción de un grupo no sófico, una pregunta abierta desde 1999— logrados por una versión interna del modelo que la empresa bautizó Astra. Todos esos resultados fueron formalizados en el asistente de demostración Lean, que verifica automáticamente que cada paso lógico de una prueba sea correcto.
La velocidad y escala de los nuevos hallazgos llevó a la compañía a reconocer, en el texto que anunció el grupo asesor, que la comunidad matemática necesita más tiempo y mecanismos para adaptarse. “Esto llevó a discusiones internas sobre la mejor manera de informar a la comunidad sobre el rápido progreso para preparar y adaptar el campo”, señaló OpenAI en su publicación oficial.
PUBLICIDAD
Nueve matemáticos con voz pero sin poder de veto
El nuevo grupo está integrado por nueve matemáticos de primer nivel: François Charles, Camillo De Lellis, Timothy Gowers, Martin Hairer, Nikhil Srivastava, Ulrike Tillmann, Ravi Vakil, Edward Witten y Melanie Matchett Wood, todos vinculados a instituciones como Princeton, Cambridge, Oxford, Stanford y Harvard. Solo uno de ellos, De Lellis, había firmado también la carta de los medallistas Fields.
Según el propio comunicado de OpenAI, el grupo funcionará de manera independiente: podrá dar consejos que la empresa no pidió, criticar públicamente su impacto en la matemática y decidir su propia composición, sin recibir pago por su tarea. Su función central será asesorar sobre cómo comunicar y revisar los resultados que vaya publicando la compañía, además de opinar sobre estándares académicos y profesionales de la investigación matemática.
PUBLICIDAD
Sin embargo, la propia OpenAI fue explícita sobre el límite de esa independencia: “el grupo no será responsable de asesorarnos sobre el ritmo de nuestro progreso interno en matemática”, aclaró la empresa en su publicación. El Instituto de Estudios Avanzados reforzó ese matiz en un comunicado propio, al señalar que asesorará pero no tendrá poder de decisión en ninguna empresa de inteligencia artificial, y que la responsabilidad de cada decisión seguirá recayendo en la compañía que la tome.
Ninguno de los más de 100 resultados anunciados fue publicado todavía con el detalle técnico que sí acompañó a los diez avances de agosto, que incluyeron manuscritos completos y certificados formales en Lean disponibles públicamente. Esa diferencia alimenta las dudas de parte de la comunidad matemática, que reclama poder revisar cada demostración de manera independiente antes de darla por válida.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué está en juego para la ciencia y la industria
El episodio expone una tensión de fondo entre la velocidad con la que los laboratorios de inteligencia artificial buscan demostrar avances científicos y los tiempos tradicionales de validación por pares que exige la matemática. Mientras un resultado formalizado en Lean elimina la duda sobre la consistencia lógica de una demostración, no garantiza que el problema haya sido interpretado correctamente ni reemplaza el juicio de especialistas sobre su relevancia real.
Para la comunidad académica de habla hispana, el caso también anticipa un dilema que empieza a discutirse en universidades de la región: qué reglas de atribución y verificación deberían regir cuando un sistema de inteligencia artificial produce resultados científicos originales, y qué rol les queda a los investigadores humanos en ese proceso.
PUBLICIDAD
La disputa con Buckmaster y Alpöge, sumada a la carta de los medallistas Fields, sugiere que otros laboratorios como Anthropic y Google DeepMind podrían verse presionados a adoptar mecanismos de supervisión similares antes de anunciar sus propios avances matemáticos. Por ahora, ninguno de esos dos competidores formó un organismo comparable al que OpenAI presentó esta semana.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Airbus va sécuriser les données de l'armée française pendant les 25 prochaines années, un contrat XXL
articles.text:
Airbus remporte un contrat de cybersécurité de 25 ans auprès du ministère des Armées. Baptisé PARACOM, il porte sur des passerelles chargées de sécuriser les échanges de données entre réseaux militaires classifiés et non protégés.
La Direction générale de l'armement (DGA) a confirmé ce mercredi 23 septembre avoir attribué le contrat PARACOM à Airbus Cybersecurity, la filiale d'Airbus dédiée à la sécurité informatique, au nez à la barbe de plusieurs de ses concurrents. D'une durée de 25 ans, ce contrat de cybersécurité englobe l'étude, la production et le maintien en condition opérationnelle de passerelles destinées aux réseaux du ministère des Armées. Ces équipements seront déployés aussi bien sur les sites du ministère que sur les théâtres d'opérations.
Airbus décroche PARACOM, le contrat qui doit blinder les réseaux de l'armée française
Au sein du ministère des Armées, les réseaux informatiques sont séparés selon la sensibilité des informations qu'ils transportent, du « secret » jusqu'au « non protégé ». Mais ces réseaux ont parfois besoin d'échanger des données. PARACOM se placera alors entre eux pour filtrer ce qui passe d'un côté à l'autre et sécuriser ces transferts. Une fois homologuées et certifiées, c'est-à-dire officiellement validées pour ces niveaux de sensibilité, ces passerelles seront déployées dans les armées et dans les directions et services du ministère. Elles deviendront alors un pilier de sa cybersécurité.
Airbus est une fois nouvelle récompensée pour son savoir-faire en la matière. « Depuis 2013, nous fournissons des passerelles de ce type pour les forces terrestres françaises », rappelle François Lombard, qui dirige l'activité Connected Intelligence d'Airbus Defence and Space, la branche défense et espace du groupe. Selon lui, PARACOM contribuera à renforcer « le bouclier numérique » des forces françaises.
Le contrat accompagnera ces passerelles tout au long de leur vie. Airbus devra d'abord les concevoir et en réaliser plusieurs prototypes, puis les produire. Il devra ensuite assurer leur maintien en condition opérationnelle, c'est-à-dire veiller à ce qu'elles restent fonctionnelles pendant toute la durée du contrat.
Du datacenter au sous-marin, une cybersécurité tout-terrain
PARACOM, qui sera installée dans les bâtiments du ministère ou envoyée sur les théâtres d'opérations, ne se contentera pas d'un seul costume. Airbus prévoit plusieurs versions. La première s'intégrera dans une baie de datacenter, qui accueillent les serveurs. Une autre prendra la forme d'un caisson autonome, déployable dans un poste de commandement, d'où les militaires dirigent les opérations. D'autres encore sont prévues pour des environnements tactiques plus contraints, où les conditions d'installation sont bien plus exigeantes, comme les drones, les sous-marins, les navires de surface, les avions, les hélicoptères, les blindés ou véhicules terrestres.
À mesure que les opérations militaires se numérisent, les données circulent davantage, et les menaces informatiques qui les visent aussi. Contrôler ces flux de données est donc devenu un enjeu majeur pour les armées. Pour Airbus, c'est aussi une vitrine. François Lombard met en avant l'expertise de ses équipes dans les échanges dits « multi-niveaux », entre réseaux de sensibilités différentes. Selon lui, elle renforce la position du groupe en tant qu'« acteur souverain de la cybersécurité en France ». Autrement dit, un acteur français capable de fournir ces technologies sensibles sans dépendre de l'étranger. Notons que le montant que du contrat n'a, sans surprise, pas été communiqué, tout comme le nombre de passerelles commandées, ni le calendrier de déploiement.

articles.title: The Eufy Omni E35 boasts huge suction power, good mopping performance, and self-cleaning
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Eufy Omni E35 is an excellent robotic vacuum cleaner and mop that gets the fundamentals right. Its 35,000 Pa of suction delivers fantastic results on carpet and hard floors alike, while the self-cleaning roller mop scrubs effectively — but not perfectly when stains are dried on — and stays remarkably clean after use. Meanwhile, the compact dock empties the dust bin, replenishes the water, then washes and dries the mop, making this robovac properly hands-off for weeks at a time. It is expensive though, and the lack of a mop-only function is frustrating. But good navigation, a polished app and impressive self-maintenance make the Omni E35 easy to recommend.
Pros
- +Fantastic vacuuming
- +Impressive mopping
- +Very effective self-cleaning
Cons
- -Relatively expensive
- -No mop-only mode
- -Small issues with phantom room mapping
Why you can trust TechRadar
Eufy Omni E35: two-minute review
The Eufy Omni E35 is a near-perfect robot vacuum cleaner and mop. It fits into the Eufy range below its flagship S series, but above the cheaper C and older X series. The headline figure of 35,000 Pa suction is seriously impressive, and so too is the E35’s ability to keep itself clean by cleverly preventing fine dust from blocking the filter.
The charge dock empties the dust bin, replenishes the mopping water tank, then washes and dries the mop with hot water and warm air, for truly hands-off cleaning. Navigation is also strong, the Eufy app works very well, and the E35’s overall cleaning performance fully justifies the four-figure price tag.
The E35 lacks the fragrance diffuser, water ozonator and more advanced, AI-powered navigation tech of the pricier Omni S2, but by cutting those Eufy has created a robovac that focuses on what really matters — cleaning your floors and, crucially, keeping itself clean too.
It’s the self-cleaning that impresses most here, with the mop still looking brand-new after weeks of use, the roller free from tangled hair, and the dust bin filter not caked in dust. Add that to the E35’s strong suction and pivoting mop that stretches into the edges of every room while pushing down to scrub stains and scraping itself clean as it goes, and this is truly a set-it-and-forget-it robovac.
Eufy Omni E35: price and availability
- List price: $1,299.99 / £999 (about AU$1,830)
- Launched: September 2026
The Omni E35 is the new flagship of Eufy’s E series of robotic vacuum cleaners. It sits above the E25 and E38, but below the company’s top-end S tier and overall flagship, the Omni S2.
At £999 (or $1,299.99 in the US; Australian price to be confirmed), the E35 is £100 more than the E28, but sits comfortably below the older £1,299 S1 and £1,599 S2.
Interestingly, the E35 has slightly more suction power than the range-topping S2, and features much of the same self-cleaning and anti-tangle tech. But it misses out on the S2’s fragrance system, water electrolysis function, and more advanced vision system — all of which helps explain the price difference, and also why the newer model’s base station is more compact.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Announced at the IFA technology trade show in September 2026, the Eufy Omni E35 is available now.
- Value for money score: 4 out of 5
Eufy Omni E35: specifications
| Feature | Specification | 
| Max suction | 35,000 Pa | 
| Robot diameter | 14.2 in (360 mm) | 
| Robot height | 4.6 in (116 mm) | 
| Dock dimensions | 14.6 x 17.6 x 16.2 in / 270 x 447 x 411 mm | 
| Dust bin volume (base) | 2.5 liters | 
| Water tank volume (base) | 2.5 liters clean / 2.4 liters dirty | 
| Base type | Charging self-emptying, refilling, hot-water mop washing, hot-water drying | 
| Max threshold clearance | 1.2 in (30 mm) | 
| Mop type | Self-cleaning roller | 
| Mop pad lifting | Automatic on carpet | 
| Max runtime | 180 minutes | 
Eufy Omni E35: design
- Charge station with dusty bag, water tanks, mop cleaning and drying function
- Self-cleaning roller mop with edge-cleaning design
- Dual detangling brushes
The Omni E35 continues Eufy’s trend of making its robotic vacuums more compact, while increasing performance. The robot itself is broadly similar to most other members of the Omni family — more on that in a moment — but the docking station is where a reduction in bulk is most obvious. It makes the X10 Pro, my go-to recommendation from just a couple of years ago, look ancient.
The E35 dock is shorter and sleeker, with a glossy plastic front, a neat bit of silver trim above the robot’s parking space, and a couple of discreet integrated handles for lifting out the clean and dirty water tanks. At about 16 inches (around 40cm) tall, and about the same depth front to back, including the robot when parked, the whole system is pleasingly compact. So much so, you’d be forgiven for wrongly thinking this is an entry-level robovac with limited performance.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Inside that compact dock there’s a charger and dust bag, two tanks for clean and dirty water, and a system that washes the mop with 60C (140F) hot water then dries it with 55C (131F) hot air. There’s also a compartment for installing Eufy’s own floor detergent (one bottle is included in the box), and Eufy says the system can operate entirely hands-free for up to 60 days. This will depend on the size of your home and how frequently you clean, of course, but it’s an impressive claim nonetheless.
The robot itself measures 4.6 in (116mm) tall and 14.2 in (360mm) in diameter, making it slightly larger in both directions than the Eufy S2, and fractionally taller than the Dyson Spot+Scrub AI. It’s also slightly taller than my trusty Eufy X10 Pro, and while the E35 managed to clean beneath all of my furniture, you’ll want to check it against yours to be sure it’ll fit.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Eufy claims a maximum threshold clearance of 1.2 inches (30.5mm), which isn’t as impressive as the Omni S2, but I’ve had no issues with it driving up from wooden floors onto carpeting.
A clever piece of design sees fine dust separated and ushered into the robot’s onboard bin before it reaches the filter. Eufy claims this ensures the E35 retains its headline 35,000 Pa suction power for longer, since the filter doesn’t get clogged up quite so quickly. After testing I found dust had started to settle in the filter, but this was easily cleaned and didn’t appear to affect performance. There’s also an anti-tangle comb to stop hair wrapping around the roller brush.
- Design score: 4.5 out of 5
Eufy Omni E35: performance
- Excellent vacuuming
- Very good mopping
- Fully cleans and dries itself reliably
Eufy’s E series of robotic vacuums has impressed for a few years now, so my expectations were high when the E35 arrived. Thankfully, the E35 delivered. The setup process will be familiar to anyone who has used a Eufy Omni, or really any robotic vacuum cleaner, before.
Assembly takes just a couple of minutes, then it’s just a case of filling the clean water tank, installing the included detergent bottle, switching it on and following the instructions of the Eufy app. The E35 then completed a mapping expedition, driving into every room and quickly using its vision system to map the walls, floors and doorways.
Furniture isn’t automatically added to the map, as it is with the pricier Omni S2, but I’ve never cared much for that feature and would rather see the floor plan unobscured.
As with all robotic vacuums, I had to manually adjust the E35’s map slightly, repositioning some walls and naming each of the rooms. It’s not really a failing of the vision system, just a part of the setup process. That said, the robot mistakenly added an enormous room to the sides of my kitchen and living room that doesn’t really exist. I imagine it saw through to the garden and decided that was part of the floor plan, but frustratingly phantom rooms can’t be deleted, so I binned the entire map and started again. The second map was created accurately, and remained so throughout the rest of my month-long test.
The headline figure for this robot is its 35,000 Pa of maximum suction power. This is actually 5,000 Pa more than the flagship Omni S2, and provides fantastic results on carpet and hard floors alike. Going back to my X10 Pro again – a vacuum that I awarded four stars just two years ago, and launched at £800 / $800 – and that manages just 8,000 Pa, a quarter of the new E35.
The result of all that power is deeply impressive cleaning performance. The vacuuming is especially good, with carpets visibly cleaner after using Max mode. It’s probably overkill for a little-and-often cleaning schedule, but if the battery can survive a full carpet vacuum in Max mode, why wouldn’t you use it?
I often left it in Max for the kitchen and living room, or switched down to the middling Turbo mode for bigger cleans in a bid to avoid charging mid-task. It’s also worth noting how the robot automatically increases suction when carpet or rugs are detected.
After a fortnight of regular use — and being impressed by the E35’s performance – I began TechRadar’s specific robovac tests. Vacuuming is first tested with a crumb mix made of flour and crushed biscuit spread across both carpet and hard floors, then oats are scattered across the same areas to test its ability to pick up larger debris.
The Omni E35’s quietest mode — which I recorded at just 60 decibels – was very fast, but left noticeable tracks of the crumb mix behind. The same happened when ramping up to Turbo mode (64 decibels) and switching to a more thorough clean. But, thankfully, the carpet was left absolutely flawless by using the ultra-powerful Max mode (67 decibels), along with the Deep intensity option and with two passes of the target area. This took longer, but the results absolutely justified the extra time and energy.
(While talking about noise levels, I recorded the dust bin emptying process at 85 dB from about two feet away.)
The oat test is usually more difficult, because robovacs tend to flick them across hard floors with their rotating side brushes. But the E35 performed surprisingly well, with Turbo mode paired with the Deep intensity and two passes being enough to completely clear the debris. The Max power option wasn’t required. Oats scattered on carpet were tackled even more successfully, as a single pass with the least power, least thorough setting did the job perfectly.
Moving to the mop, and the Omni E35 continues to impress. It’s a similar system to that of Eufy’s flagship Omni S2, with a roller that cleans itself during use, then is washed and dried when back at the docking station. Eufy claims its HydroJet 2.0 system removes 99.99 percent of bacteria “for a TÜV-certified baby-friendly clean” – in other words, it has been assessed and certified by a group of independent German testing organizations.
The 290 mm (11.4 inch) mop pushes down with 1.6 kg (3.53 lb) of pressure, so it isn’t merely wiping across the floor, but giving it a good scrub too, and is cleaned by a pair of scrapers eight times per second to stop dirt getting trapped in its fibers. The roller can slide outwards by 32 mm (1.26 inches), ensuring it cleans right up to the wall, while dirty water is moved away from the mop and into an onboard tank, ready to be deposited into the charge station.
Even without quantitative testing, I know the E35’s mop works extremely well, because the dirty water held in the charge station tank is properly filthy. As I found with the Eufy Omni S2, it’s worth emptying this tank quite frequently, because if you wait until it’s full you’ll be dealing with some seriously stinky water when you pour it down the sink.
During TechRadar’s standard mopping test – which involves a small amount of dried-on ketchup – the Omni E35 at first struggled to clean the stain from a wooden floor. But upping the water supply to 100 percent soon fixed this, and the ketchup was entirely lifted on the second pass.
Interestingly, the E35 does not have the ClearMind AI function of the pricier S2, which recognizes floor types, stains and different kinds of mess, then cleans appropriately. Instead, the E35 lets you decide what’s best – and, in my experience, that’s almost always a whole-room clean with the middle or most powerful suction, about 75 percent of the maximum water flow for mopping, the most intense cleaning pattern, and everything done twice.
The S2’s AI system is clever, and sees the robot work harder to clean messier areas, but the end result — at least on my carpets and wooden floors — was perfectly comparable between the two robots. It also lacks the S2’s water ozonization feature, but that’s by no means a dealbreaker.
Finally, I tested the E35’s obstacle avoidance tech by having it clean an area littered with a shoe, a sock and a USB cable. The robot performed perfectly, driving neatly around each object but not touching any of them. I was particularly impressed by its ability to dodge the USB cable, since this is something even high-end robovacs can struggle with. Eufy says the robot can recognize over 280 common household objects, and can navigate fine in darkness as well as daylight.
It isn’t perfect though. The E35 sometimes navigated too confidently, driving up and over obstacles that should be avoided. I have a vinyl record stand on the floor, the front of which stands about an inch off the ground; the E35 frequently drove up onto this, pushing some records around in the process.
- Performance score: 4.5 out of 5
Eufy Omni E35: app
- Straightforward mapping
- Good use of shortcuts
- Lacks a mop-only mode
The Omni E35 uses the same app as all other Eufy robotic vacuums, and it’s an app shared by the company’s home security products too. The app has matured nicely over the past few years into something that works very well, giving you access to just the right amount of customization without it feeling overwhelming.
The creation and editing of maps works well (albeit with the phantom room I mentioned earlier), and it’s easy to select the right parameters for each clean. Or, you can set up a clean (kitchen with intense mopping and two passes, for example) and save that as a commonly used chore. This can then be added to the home screen of the app, where it’s ready to activate with one tap.
It’s also possible to create a home screen widget, where a single tap fires up the E35 and sets it to work.
Other useful app settings include the child lock, which stops small people (and pets!) from pressing the robot’s two buttons, and off-peak charging, which you can program to coincide with cheaper overnight electricity rates. Since I have an electric car tariff, I set the Eufy to charge overnight when power is significantly cheaper.
All that’s missing is a mop-only mode. This is a little frustrating for Eufy to omit, since I’d prefer to have my robot tackle a dried-on hard floor stain with its mop first, rather than vacuum the floor. Ideally, the robot should approach such a stain in reverse, mop-first, rather than risk it transferring onto the brushes before applying water and detergent.
- App score: 4.5 out of 5
Should you buy the Eufy Omni E35?
| Eufy Omni E35 score card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
|---|---|---|
| Value | The Omni E35 feels like much better value than some of Eufy’s more expensive robotic vacuum cleaners, especially from its flagship S family. The E35 offers superb vacuuming and strong mopping performance, with smart navigation and a compact design at a more accessible price than models with superfluous bells and whistles. | 4.5 | 
| Design | Compact and relatively attractive, as far as robovacs go, the E35 benefits from a clever anti-tangle brush design, along with a high-performance mop that washes and dries itself. It cleans right into the corners of every room, but can’t raise itself up to clear raised rugs as well as the more expensive Omni S2. | 4.5/5 | 
| Performance | Its superb vacuuming performance is reason enough to buy this robovac. It really does leave your carpets spotless, while also mopping hard floors well, navigating reliably, and thoroughly cleaning itself after every use. It also works quickly, quietly, and reliably, not once getting stuck or lost during my testing. | 4.5/5 | 
| App | Eufy’s app continues to impress, with a clean interface that is easy to navigate. It offers just the right amount of functionality and customization without being overwhelming. Shortcuts and iOS widget functionality are welcome additions, along with a child lock and off-peak charging. | 4.5/5 | 
Buy it if
You want a hands-off robovac
Eufy says this robot can operate hands-free for up to 60 days – and even after that, you’ll likely only need to replenish the water and perhaps replace the dust bag. The self-cleaning really is that good.
I set up the Eufy Omni E35 in my own home and lived with it for a couple of weeks. During this time it was my only vacuum cleaner and mop, tackling every room of my home and cleaning up after an energetic puppy too.
After that fortnight, I conducted TechRadar’s standard robovac tests to analyze its suction, mopping and navigation skills, as well as monitoring how loud it is and checking the performance of its self-cleaning system.
You don’t need the flagship
Eufy’s Omni S2 is phenomenally good, but it’s also much more expensive than this model. Do you really need a fragrance diffuser and ozonated water? If not, save the money and buy this one instead.
You value mopping as much as vacuuming
If your floors are evenly split between hard floors and carpet, this robot could be perfect for you, since it manages both surfaces equally well.
Don't buy it if
You’re on a budget
Despite being much less expensive than Eufy’s top-end S2, the E35 is still a pricey robovac. If you’re on a tighter budget, consider a more affordable model with less powerful suction or a less comprehensive mopping and self-cleaning system.
You have large doorway thresholds or thick rugs
Although the E35’s ability to clear 1.2-inch thresholds is good, some models can climb higher. So if you have significant differences in floor height between rooms you might want to look elsewhere.

articles.title: Babbel's Lifetime Language Plan Is Now Available Through This Exclusive Offer
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 23rd 2026
	
	
	
	
Babbel's Lifetime Language Plan Is Now Available Through This Exclusive Offer
Sticking with a new language usually comes down to whether the lessons feel like an actual conversation or like homework, and most apps lean hard toward the second. Babbel takes the opposite approach with a lifetime subscription to all 14 languages, on sale for $159 with code LEARN (reg. $299).
Founded in 2007 as the first language-learning app of its kind, Babbel built its course library around human linguists and educators rather than gamified drills or AI-generated scripts, and the company now counts more than 1 million active subscribers and ranks among the world's most innovative companies in education. Seventy-three percent of users said they could hold a short, simple conversation in a new language within five hours of starting.Researchers at Yale University tested the method and found that participants saw 100% improvement in their oral proficiency within three months. Spanish, French, German, Italian, and 10 other languages fit into one account, split into 10- to 15-minute lessons that fit a commute without clearing a weekend for it.
Speech recognition checks pronunciation as you go, and personalized review sessions bring back material that needs reinforcement instead of repeating a fixed drill. Lessons download for offline use too, so a spotty connection does not stop a session in progress.
Babbel's own monthly plan totals $646.20 over three years, so even a single year of paying month-to-month costs more than this lifetime option.
Stop paying a language app every year for something you can own outright.
Through October 8 at 11:59 p.m. PT, use code LEARN to get Babbel's lifetime subscription to all 14 languages for $159 (reg. $299).

articles.title: New Linux Kernel Flaw Gives ARM64 KVM Guests Read-Write Access to Host Memory
articles.text:
A new flaw in the Linux kernel's KVM virtualization code for ARM64 processors can leave a freed piece of host memory exposed to a guest virtual machine on hosts with nested virtualization enabled.
The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-89775, allows a guest to read and write host kernel memory, and the researcher who found it says it can be used to escape the guest and run code on the host machine.
The affected code is part of the mainline Linux kernel for ARM64, and it is fixed in Linux 6.18.51, 7.2.5, and 7.3-rc1.
Nested virtualization allows a guest to run its own hypervisor, enabling it to host virtual machines. On ARM64, it is off by default. It is an experimental boot-time mode that needs Armv8.4 hardware with a feature called FEAT_NV2, so a plain ARM64 KVM host that never turns it on is outside the reported attack path.
The flaw sits in the part of KVM that handles nested virtualization on ARM64. When a guest arranges its memory in a certain way, a size calculation comes out as zero, and a step that should clear stale entries from the processor's address cache, a TLB invalidation, is skipped.
A page of host memory that has been freed then stays mapped and writable, and the guest can read and write it 64 bits at a time, with no hardware trap to hand control back to the host.
Hyunwoo Kim, the security researcher who reported the flaw and disclosed it on September 16, says a guest can use this to escape to the host, breaking out of its own virtual machine to run code on the underlying machine. No exploit code has been published, and there is no sign the flaw has been used in an attack.
The kernel's own record lists the affected code as present from Linux 6.16. But the author tagged the fix against a later change, and the maintainer who reviewed and tested it said the "missed invalidation only starts at v6.17." By that account, a host on 6.16 carries the code but not the behavior an attacker needs.
There is a second way to abuse the flaw. On systems where any user can open /dev/kvm, the device a program uses to create a virtual machine, a local user could build a guest and use the same bug to gain root, Kim says.
He points to Red Hat Enterprise Linux, where that device is open to all users by default. Red Hat lists its version 10 kernel as affected and versions 6 through 9 as not affected. This path still needs the host to have nested virtualization enabled.
Which Kernels Are Fixed
Upstream, the flaw is fixed in Linux 6.18.51, 7.2.5, and 7.3-rc1. Distributions are shipping the fix on their own schedules, and status differs by release.
| Kernel or distribution | Status as of September 22 | 
|---|---|
| Mainline Linux | Fixed in 6.18.51, 7.2.5, and 7.3-rc1 | 
| Red Hat Enterprise Linux | Version 10 kernel affected; versions 6 through 9 not affected | 
| Ubuntu | 26.04, including its AWS, Azure, and GCP kernels, vulnerable; 24.04 LTS general kernel not affected, though its newer hardware-enablement kernels (6.17, 7.0) are vulnerable | 
| Amazon Linux | AL2023 kernel6.18 package: fix pending; other Amazon Linux kernels not affected | 
| Debian | bookworm and trixie not affected (code not present); sid fixed in 7.2.6-1; forky vulnerable | 
For hosts that cannot yet be patched, Red Hat says no mitigation meets its criteria for a workaround. The one certain thing is scope: the attack only targets hosts with nested virtualization enabled, which is not the default on ARM64.
Vendors score the flaw from 7.8 to 9.3 out of 10. They agree the impact is high and the attack is local, meaning it cannot be launched over a network. The spread reflects how difficult each vendor thinks the flaw is to exploit, and Ubuntu, which shows the 9.3 figure, sets its own priority to medium.
As of September 22, the flaw was not in the U.S. CISA catalog of exploited vulnerabilities, and its predicted exploitation score was below 1%.
The disclosure raises the question of whether cloud tenants could use the flaw to break into a provider's machines. On the largest providers, the configuration it needs is not on offer: Amazon Web Services lists only Intel-based instances for nested virtualization, and Google Cloud excludes its ARM virtual machines from it.
That is not a clean bill of health for those platforms, but the specific path this flaw takes is not exposed in their standard ARM offerings.
CVE-2026-89775 is the fourth KVM guest-to-host escape Kim has disclosed this year. Two were in the x86 version of KVM: Januscape in July and Zapscape in August. The one it most resembles is ITScape, an ARM64 KVM escape he published in June, which he called the first such escape shown publicly on ARM64.

articles.title: Windows 11 : la mise à jour de septembre fait la part belle à l'Explorateur de fichiers, au Bluetooth et aux améliorations
articles.text:
Windows 11 : la mise à jour de septembre fait la part belle à l'Explorateur de fichiers, au Bluetooth et aux améliorations
Microsoft prépare le terrain à la prochaine grosse mise de Windows 11 avec une préversion riche en nouveautés et en améliorations, disponible dès à présent.
Alors que le dernier riche Patch Tuesday de Windows 11 n'a visiblement pas encore corrigé tous ses bugs de jeunesse, Microsoft travaille déjà sur le prochain. En témoigne la mise à disposition dans Windows Update pour les plus courageux et impatients de la préversion optionnelle de septembre (KB51224010). Les changements qui s'y trouvent seront normalement installés de manière moins facultative par la suite dans le prochain Patch Tuesday.
Il y a un Copilot dans l'avion
Comme souvent, la plupart des éléments évoqués ci-dessous seront déployés de manière graduelle. Ainsi, installer la mise à jour ne garantit pas l'arrivée immédiate d'un changement, qui peut être activé plusieurs jours ou semaines plus tard par Microsoft.
Pour commencer, l'Explorateur de fichiers profite de plusieurs nouveautés, parfois évoquées depuis un moment. On relèvera notamment que le panneau d'aperçu latéral propose un nouveau bouton pour afficher quand même un aperçu d'un fichier HTML téléchargé depuis le web. L'Accueil de l'Explorateur conserve quant à lui l'état des sections, étendues ou réduites, d'une session à une autre.
Comme déjà évoqué il y a quelques jours, via cette mise à jour Microsoft permet enfin de rendre la touche Copilot (un peu) personnalisable. Cette dernière peut être de nouveau utilisée comme une touche Ctrl Droit ou Menu Contextuel via les paramètres. Par ailleurs, de nouveaux gestes sont disponibles pour les pavés tactiles (touchpads) : le défilement à un seul doigt et le défilement automatique.
Des améliorations à tous les étages pour Windows 11
Via cette mise à jour, Windows 11 supporte également les émojis de la version 17.0, avec de nouveaux émojis et des refontes d'anciens. Du côté des Widgets, Microsoft ajoute un widget Astuces dédié à des conseils sur Windows 11.
Les utilisateurs de Bluetooth apprécieront également la présence de nombreux correctifs pour améliorer la fiabilité de l'expérience à la connexion et à l'utilisation. Du côté de l'accessibilité, en plus d'une loupe aux contrôles modernisés, une nouvelle option permet désormais d'ouvrir systématiquement les applications de manière maximisée.
Enfin, outre des correctifs à de nombreux niveaux, Microsoft a supprimé la fonctionnalité de transfert Windows Backup de PC à PC pour mettre davantage à profit la sauvegarde cloud via OneDrive. Par ailleurs, une nouvelle option dans les paramètres permet de sauvegarder les images de la pellicule photo dans OneDrive.

articles.title: Anthropic anuncia novo Claude Opus 5.5, com capacidade ainda maior • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Anthropic anuncia novo Claude Opus 5.5, com capacidade ainda maior
Modelo promete igualar desempenho do Mythos 5.1 para trabalhos de cibersegurança e biologia. Recursos de segurança também são reforçados.
A Anthropic revelou seu novo Claude Opus 5.5, o modelo de IA mais avançado da empresa até o momento. Ele alcança a capacidade de Mythos 5.1 e Fable 5.1 em atividades relacionadas a cibersegurança e biologia, garantindo também novas salvaguardas para mitigar casos de uso indevido.
Segundo a desenvolvedora, a IA é também mais rápida e assertiva, migrando códigos de 680 mil linhas em apenas um dia. Outra vantagem citada pela empresa é o custo, 40% inferior ao do Opus 5. Esse modelo é o mais recomendado da Anthropic para trabalhos aprofundados de programação, engenharia de software e automação.
Além do Opus 5.5, outras duas IAs devem ser atualizadas nas próximas semanas: Sonnet 5.5 e Haiku 5.5, voltados para maior velocidade e eficiência, respectivamente. O lançamento do novo modelo vem na sequência da polêmica envolvendo as denúncias de um funcionário da Anthropic e o posicionamento do próprio CEO, Dario Amodei, pedindo a diminuição no ritmo de desenvolvimento da IA.
Com a novidade, a Anthropic promete capacidade semelhante aos modelos mais avançados Mythos 5.1 e Fable 5.1 para assuntos relacionados a cibersegurança e biologia. Da mesma forma, mecanismos de defesa presentes no Fable aparecem no novo Opus 5.5, como o downgrade pontual para o Opus 4.8 e Opus 5 a depender da situação.
Segundo a Anthropic, a novidade alcançou as melhores notas em uma auditoria comportamental automatizada realizada internamente. Isso significa que o modelo tem menos chances de burlar salvaguardas em tentativas de uso indevido, além de ser mais resistente que seu antecessor Opus 5 a tentativas de prompt injection.
Em termos de performance, a empresa fala em um grande salto para trabalhos complexos. Segundo a Anthropic, de 40 repetições de processos de reparo de software, o novo Opus 5.5 resolveu 39 casos, ficando acima do Opus 5, que buscou alternativas menos eficientes. Também foi testada a qualidade da IA para desenvolver jogos do zero com um único prompt, com destaque para os resultados da nova inteligência em gráficos e acabamentos.
Da mesma forma, o “preço” para rodar o Opus 5.5 também se destaca, com 40% menos custo para trabalhos em geral. A Anthropic promete US$ 4 a US$ 20 (R$ 20 a 100, em conversão direta) para cada 1 milhão de tokens, um quinto da precificação do Opus 5 padrão. Já pensando em leituras de cache, relacionadas principalmente aos trabalhos agênticos, a empresa fala em US$ 0,20 (R$ 1) a cada milhão, valor 60% menor.
A Anthropic divulgou gráficos com vantagens frente ao mais recente GPT-6 Astra, da Open AI (aquele que decifrou uma antiga mensagem cifrada da Primeira Guerra Mundial), tanto em custo-benefício quanto em trabalhos de coding e pesquisa. A companhia também promete uma comunicação mais fluida e assertiva, com informações mais importantes vindo primeiro e um estilo de escrita mais fácil de entender.
A Anthropic já liberou o novo Opus 5.5 em sua plataforma, que pode ser ativado com o código “claude-opus-5-5”. Segundo a empresa, há um limite de 5 horas para usar o modelo, disponível nas assinaturas Pro, Max, Team e Enterprise. Esse tempo pode ser regulado pelos próprios usuários ao escolherem apenas tarefas específicas.

articles.title: Rocket Software brings governed AI agents to mainframe operations - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Rocket Software brings governed AI agents to mainframe operations
Rocket Software Inc. is expanding its Enterprise Virtual Assistant agentic artificial intelligence platform to help enterprises investigate and eventually automate operational work on mainframe systems while stopping short of giving AI agents unrestricted access to critical resources.
The company said today that the forthcoming EVA 2.0 will add PlanGuard, a security layer that evaluates an agent’s proposed action before execution. The platform targets organizations that want to apply generative AI to mainframe operations while retaining existing identity controls, policy enforcement and audit trails.
EVA can already conduct multistep investigations after a person submits a natural-language request. It selects connected tools and data sources, collects operational context, correlates evidence across systems and returns findings, recommendations and supporting evidence. The current emphasis is analysis rather than unsupervised system changes.
“Today, EVA can independently orchestrate complex investigations once a user initiates a request,” said Phil Buckellew, president of Rocket’s Infrastructure Modernization Business Unit. “Rather than requiring operators to manually navigate multiple consoles, dashboards, logs and reports, EVA brings those sources together and provides a unified, context-rich explanation of what is happening in the environment and why.”
Careful provisioning
PlanGuard is designed to mediate that transition. It operates first as a policy decision point, examining the caller, request, session, selected tool, environmental conditions and organizational rules when an action is proposed. It can permit or deny the action or require another approval. If it grants permission, it creates a temporary execution identity limited to the approved task and revokes it when the work is complete.
“This invocation-time approach is important for agentic AI because decisions can no longer rely solely on permissions granted during account provisioning,” Buckellew said. “Instead, PlanGuard evaluates the specific user, request, tool and operational context involved in each action before execution is allowed.”
Rocket said PlanGuard works with established mainframe security managers including RACF, ACF2 and Top Secret rather than replacing them. Customers can apply contextual and short-lived authorization while keeping their existing mainframe controls as the underlying enforcement framework.
The system also records who initiated a request, what an agent proposed, which policy was applied, whether approval was necessary, the identity used for execution and the resulting action. EVA adds a tamper-evident, hash-chained audit trail intended to make the agent’s reasoning and activity traceable to identifiable people.
Buckellew said the records are designed to support operational and regulatory review: “This creates a complete chain of evidence that allows operators, security teams and auditors to understand not only what occurred, but why it occurred, with which identity, and under which policy decision,” he said.
Time saved
Rocket is testing EVA with organizations in financial services, government, insurance, retail and telecommunications. It said pilot results show that the enhancement shortens investigations that traditionally require several specialists to search separate logs, reports and consoles.
Buckellew said an operations team at a large South American financial institution spent about three weeks investigating a production problem. After receiving the relevant System Management Facilities records and operational context, EVA identified a probable root cause and supporting evidence in less than a day.
In another pilot, a major retailer knew that a production CICS region had stopped after exhausting temporary storage resources but didn’t know the cause. EVA concluded that the event was a localized, application-driven issue rather than general system contention. It isolated the main source of activity, identified contributing systems and connected the failure to a workload pattern and likely application owner.
Buckellew said EVA’s role goes beyond displaying system data: “EVA is not simply surfacing metrics or dashboards,” he said. “It is correlating operational evidence, identifying likely causes, explaining its reasoning and helping teams move from knowing what happened to understanding why it happened.”
The platform combines live operational information with institutional knowledge embedded in workflows, policies, tool integrations and connected systems. Rocket said that this can extend scarce mainframe expertise to less-experienced employees while keeping recommendations aligned with changing applications and configurations.
EVA uses a consumption-based pricing model tied to expected users and usage volume. Customers can use their preferred large language model providers and retain control over those model costs. Rocket estimates that a typical deployment can generate a 3.2-times annual return on investment, including LLM expenses, through fewer specialist escalations, faster resolution of high-priority incidents and round-the-clock access to operational knowledge. That projection is Rocket’s analysis, not an independently verified result.
The broader test will be whether customers move beyond AI-assisted investigation to governed execution. PlanGuard supplies policy and identity controls, but organizations must still decide which actions agents may take, when people must approve them and how to validate conclusions before changes reach production.

articles.title: KDE Begins Drafting AI Guidelines: "Don't Be a Meat Proxy"
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 23rd 2026
	
									
	
	
	
KDE Begins Drafting AI Guidelines: "Don't Be a Meat Proxy"
Despite the immense popularity of LLMs and AI coding agents in software development, the open-source community seems to be quite divided on the topic at times. On the one hand, you have projects like GIMP banning AI from its codebase entirely, while other projects, like Nobara Linux and Omarchy, are very much all-in on AI coding. There is, however, a middle ground, like the Linux Kernel project, which allows AI-assisted and -generated code in the codebase, but all code requires human review and a proper merge request write-up that demonstrates an understanding of the actual code submitted. This appears to be where KDE Plasma will land as a project, if the recent proposed KDE LLM guidelines are anything to go by. 
The draft of KDE's LLM guidelines was submitted for discussion by project lead, Nate Graham, and it outlines rules that effectively summarized by the golden rule: "Don't be lazy." In the KDE LLM guidelines discussion post, the proposed draft explains that "contributions with obvious and lazy LLM usage may be ignored or closed," and that "nobody should know if you use an LLM," because the output should be indistinguishable from what you could produce yourself without an LLM. It also places rules on AI-generated text, forbidding AI-generated text for merge requests, commit messages, or replying to a question or comment. The current draft also seeks to prevent additional work being placed on maintainers by limiting vibe-coded changes to that maintainers are expected to clean up and implement—an issue faced by Godot maintainers not long ago.KDE will seemingly also expect developers to take responsibility for their LLM-generated code, with the draft guidelines specifically forbidding adding AI disclosures as a way to excuse low-quality work. The draft has yet to be finalized, and the discussion around the LLM guidelines is expected to continue in the upcoming days, after which a finalized version will be added to the KDE documentation. The full KDE LLM Guidelines follows:
LLM usage
		
		Source:
				KDE Invent			
	
	
	
		
	
		
The draft of KDE's LLM guidelines was submitted for discussion by project lead, Nate Graham, and it outlines rules that effectively summarized by the golden rule: "Don't be lazy." In the KDE LLM guidelines discussion post, the proposed draft explains that "contributions with obvious and lazy LLM usage may be ignored or closed," and that "nobody should know if you use an LLM," because the output should be indistinguishable from what you could produce yourself without an LLM. It also places rules on AI-generated text, forbidding AI-generated text for merge requests, commit messages, or replying to a question or comment. The current draft also seeks to prevent additional work being placed on maintainers by limiting vibe-coded changes to that maintainers are expected to clean up and implement—an issue faced by Godot maintainers not long ago.KDE will seemingly also expect developers to take responsibility for their LLM-generated code, with the draft guidelines specifically forbidding adding AI disclosures as a way to excuse low-quality work. The draft has yet to be finalized, and the discussion around the LLM guidelines is expected to continue in the upcoming days, after which a finalized version will be added to the KDE documentation. The full KDE LLM Guidelines follows:
LLM usage
The golden rule for LLM usage in KDE is Don't be lazy:
The result will be poor-quality work that eventually becomes someone else's problem.
- Don't try to use a tool to replace your own judgment, interpersonal communication, or learning process.
- Don't take unsustainable shortcuts.
- Don't avoid growing as a person.
Nobody in KDE should know if you use an LLM—not because you're concealing it, but because your usage of it produces output indistinguishable from what you could produce yourself. Contributions with obvious and lazy LLM usage may be ignored or closed.
Using an LLM to generate contributions
KDE follows a "human in the loop" principle: you must be making decisions and adjustments beyond mere prompting. The output must express your unique humanity in some way.
Don't be a "meat proxy". For example:
Using an LLM to generate text
- Don't submit "vibe-coded" changes you don't understand and couldn't make yourself.
- Don't submit throwaway LLM-created changes as a "first draft or proof-of-concept for maintainers to improve".
- Don't disclose LLM usage as a way of trying to excuse the potential errors or poor quality of a contribution that you haven't put much effort into.
- Don't add "Assisted-by: [some LLM]" tags to your commits; it's just free advertising for the LLM's provider.
Generally, don't.
What you are willing to write is generally the upper limit of what others are willing to read.
LLMs, on the other hand, often produce long, rambling, soulless, corporate-sounding nonsense that nobody wants to read; don't do it. This includes:
The one acceptable usage is to write text in your native language and then machine-translate it into English, with no stylistic or tonal changes.
- Don't use an LLM to "organize your thoughts" and copy-paste the output somewhere. Organize them yourself.
- Don't use an LLM to generate commit messages and merge request descriptions. Write them yourself.
- Don't use an LLM to generate a reply to someone's question or comment, then copy-paste that as if it were your response. Understand and reply yourself.
Other usage of LLMs
If you use an LLM to debug issues or find bugs, make sure its conclusion is correct.
If you use an LLM for research, or to replace reading API docs directly, verify the accuracy of what it told you.
8 Comments on KDE Begins Drafting AI Guidelines: "Don't Be a Meat Proxy"
An example is the Ghostty AGENTS.md, that includes:
It's a tool to assist, not a method to replace!
Though of course since food started "growing in supermarket" common sense has become so rare it's superpower...
I suspect this is also one the things in which Microslop has gone wrong and that they start actually looking at code only after problems appear.

articles.title: Attention, Muse, l'IA de Meta, peut être piratée par une simple commande sur votre Mac
articles.text:
Le chercheur en sécurité Patrick Wardle a découvert une faille zero-day dans Muse, l'assistant IA de Meta pour Mac. Une simple commande locale suffit à détourner l'agent pour intercepter la voix de l'utilisateur et prendre le contrôle de ses comptes connectés.
Muse, l'IA que Meta vient de lancer, n'est pas passée inaperçue et connait un succès fulgurant auprès du public et des investisseurs… mais aussi un blocage par Amazon pour des raisons de sécurité. Ars Technica détaille faille technique qui alimente ces inquiétudes.
Comment une commande de terminal peut voler la voix et le compte
Muse dicte les messages vocaux via un serveur de Meta, lequel se charge de les transcrire. Patrick Wardle, fondateur de la fondation Objective-See et spécialiste de la sécurité macOS, a découvert qu'une appli locale ou une simple commande de terminal peut changer l'adresse de ce serveur, sans demander la moindre autorisation sur macOS. Il suffit alors de rediriger ce trafic vers un serveur piégé pour récupérer à la fois les échanges vocaux et le jeton qui authentifie le compte Muse de la victime.
Avec ce jeton, l'attaquant hérite de toutes les autorisations accordées à Muse. Cela inclut lire les e-mails, gérer l'agenda, se connecter à WhatsApp ou aux réseaux sociaux, et parfois accéder aux fichiers, au micro, à la caméra ou à la localisation via les permissions macOS. Apple encadre normalement ce type d'accès pour bloquer les applications et commandes de terminal indésirables. Muse contourne cette protection en s'appuyant sur les autorisations déjà accordées par l'utilisateur.
Pour en arriver là, l'attaquant doit d'abord réussir à exécuter du code sur le Mac, via un malware, une application piégée ou de l'ingénierie sociale. Mais il n'a pas besoin de compromettre toute la machine. Une seule commande, obtenue par une technique de type ClickFix suffit. Wardle a réalisé plusieurs démonstrations de ce détournement avec l'écriture de fichiers sur le disque, la prise de photo à distance, le tout, sans le moindre signal visible pour l'utilisateur.
Alors si vous souhaitiez installer Muse… mieux vaut sans doute y réfléchir à deux fois. Plus généralement, mieux vaut limiter les connexions données d'emblée à un agent IA (messagerie, agenda, paiement, permissions système), les revoir régulièrement, et se méfier de toute demande d'autorisation inhabituelle. Reste à savoir si Meta corrigera ce problème. Garder son système à jour, utiliser un antivirus actif et ignorer les commandes trouvées sur un site ou dans un message non sollicité restent les bons réflexes face à ce genre de faille.

articles.title: SharePoint Flaw Initially Listed as Spoofing by Microsoft Enables Authenticated RCE
articles.text:
A SharePoint Server vulnerability that Microsoft initially classified as a spoofing flaw with a CVSS score of 6.5 actually enables authenticated remote code execution, according to full technical details published today by Viettel Cyber Security researcher Dinh Ho Anh Khoa.
The flaw, CVE-2026-65660, affects SharePoint Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition. Patches have been available since the August 11 security updates, and the National Vulnerability Database scores it 8.8.
Microsoft's advisory describes CVE-2026-65660 as allowing an authorized attacker to perform spoofing and assigns no impact to integrity or availability. The CVE record that Microsoft publishes separately, updated on September 11, titles the same flaw a remote code execution vulnerability and says it allows an authorized attacker to execute code.
Both records assign CWE-94, a code-injection weakness. Defenders who triaged CVE-2026-65660 based on the advisory saw a moderate spoofing flaw, not a code-execution vulnerability with a near-maximum score.
Khoa is the researcher who demonstrated the original ToolShell exploit chain against SharePoint at Pwn2Own Berlin in May 2025. That chain was later exploited by Chinese state-backed groups and triggered emergency patches from Microsoft.
The researcher has since disclosed several other SharePoint flaws, including CVE-2026-55040, an authentication bypass that attackers exploited shortly after its details became public in August.
The latest CVE-2026-65660 vulnerability sits in how SharePoint checks whether server-side controls are on the SafeControls list, a filter that prevents dangerous classes from loading. When the ToolPane component processes web-part markup, it reconstructs Register directives by writing attribute values between double quotes without escaping quotes inside them.
An attacker can inject additional directives through the unescaped quotes, registering arbitrary .NET classes after the type check runs but before the control is loaded.
With arbitrary class loading, the attacker uses XamlServices.Parse() to trigger code execution through deserialization. The writeup includes a working in-memory webshell payload that avoids the registry permission failures other deserialization methods encounter, Khoa said.
The researcher also demonstrated that the flaw can be chained with a separate, already-patched authentication bypass to reach pre-authentication remote code execution on servers configured to allow anonymous page access. Khoa says the bypass was fixed in a June 9 patch, and servers that applied the fix are not exposed to the pre-authentication path.
No exploitation of CVE-2026-65660 has been reported in the wild, and the flaw is not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Microsoft's advisory rates exploitation as unlikely, though the full exploit markup is now public. Khoa says he has used the exploit in penetration testing engagements.
The August 11 patch fixes the flaw and turns off the vulnerable function by default, according to the researcher.
Khoa says the flaw also affects SharePoint 2013, though Microsoft's advisory lists only 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition. SharePoint 2013 has been out of support since April 2023 and receives no security updates.

articles.title: Motorola mostra o Signature 27, com Snapdragon Extreme e câmera periscópica de 200 MP • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Motorola mostra o Signature 27, com Snapdragon Extreme e câmera periscópica de 200 MP
Modelo top de linha terá áudio da B&O e promessa de sete atualizações do sistema operacional.
A Motorola apresentou uma prévia do celular Motorola Signature 27, segunda geração da sua linha de celulares premium. O aparelho virá equipado com o novo chip Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, da Qualcomm, e terá uma câmera periscópica de 200 megapixels e áudio desenvolvido em parceria com a Bang & Olufsen. O preço no Brasil e a data de início das vendas são mantidos sob sigilo.
Com lançamento previsto para este ano, o aparelho foi revelado nesta terça-feira (22) durante o Snapdragon Summit. A fabricante também não divulgou a ficha técnica completa.
O Signature 27 está entre os primeiros celulares anunciados com o novo chip topo de linha da Qualcomm. Segundo a Motorola, o SoC permitirá recursos avançados de IA, melhorias de câmera e jogos mais responsivos. Para manter a temperatura sob controle, o aparelho contará com um novo sistema de refrigeração com metal líquido.
A empresa também promete sete atualizações do sistema operacional e até sete anos de atualizações de segurança. O modelo dá continuidade à família Signature, lançada no início de 2026. O número dele inaugura uma nova estratégia de identificação da fabricante: usar os dois últimos dígitos do ano seguinte nos aparelhos da linha.
A Motorola revelou parte do conjunto fotográfico do Signature 27. A câmera principal utilizará o sensor Sony LYTIA 910 de 50 MP, enquanto a teleobjetiva periscópica terá 200 MP. O aparelho também contará com um sistema de estabilização óptica de imagem (OIS) e recursos de IA para ajustar os tons de cor a partir da análise da cena antes e durante a gravação. Mais detalhes sobre o conjunto completo de câmeras serão divulgados posteriormente.
Outra novidade está no áudio: o Signature 27 será o primeiro smartphone da Motorola com sistema de áudio criado em parceria com a dinamarquesa Bang & Olufsen, conhecida por seus equipamentos premium. A fabricante tampouco detalhou as especificações dessa solução.
O smartphone também terá integração com o Google Gemini. Entre os recursos apresentados estão ferramentas para transformar comandos, fotos ou filmagens em vídeos e gerar músicas e trilhas sonoras.
No design, o Signature 27 terá estrutura de alumínio e será oferecido nas cores Pantone Coal Smoke (preto) e Capulet Olive (verde), ambas com acabamentos texturizados.

articles.title: Estos celulares se quedarán sin Netflix desde el jueves 30 de septiembre de 2026
articles.text:
Netflix dejará de estar disponible en una serie de celulares antiguos a partir del 30 de septiembre de 2026, según los requisitos técnicos de seguridad y actualización que exige la plataforma de streaming. La restricción alcanzará tanto a teléfonos con sistema Android como a modelos de iPhone que no admiten las versiones más recientes de sus sistemas operativos, además de una lista de televisores y reproductores multimedia.
El cambio será permanente en los dispositivos afectados: los usuarios no podrán abrir, descargar ni actualizar la aplicación desde el menú del equipo. La pérdida de acceso no dejará inutilizable el teléfono, aunque impedirá entrar al catálogo, reproducir contenido, descargar títulos o gestionar funciones asociadas a la cuenta.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué modelos de Android perderán la aplicación
La medida afectará a teléfonos Android comercializados entre 2011 y 2014 que no admiten versiones recientes del sistema operativo. Se trata de dispositivos que ya no pueden instalar los parches de seguridad ni los recursos que requieren las versiones actuales de la aplicación de Netflix.
Entre los modelos alcanzados figuran el Samsung Galaxy S3, el Galaxy Note 2 y el Galaxy Grand Prime. La lista también incluye al LG Optimus L5, el Optimus L7 y el LG G2, junto con varios equipos de Sony, como el Xperia Z, el Xperia Z1 y el Xperia E3.
Para verificar la versión instalada, es necesario ingresar a Configuración o Ajustes, buscar la opción “Acerca del teléfono” y seleccionar “Información del software”. Allí figura la versión de Android y, en la mayoría de los dispositivos, la fecha del último parche de seguridad disponible.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué iPhone quedarán sin acceso a Netflix
La restricción también incluirá a los modelos de Apple que no pueden instalar iOS 18.0 o una versión posterior. En ese grupo se encuentran los siguientes:
- iPhone X.
- iPhone 8.
- iPhone 8 Plus.
- iPhone 7.
- iPhone 7 Plus.
- iPhone 6s.
- iPhone 6s Plus.
- iPhone SE de primera generación.
- Modelos anteriores de la marca.
Qué televisores dejarán de tener la aplicación nativa
La lista de dispositivos afectados no se limita a los celulares. Los Samsung Smart TV fabricados antes de 2016, que utilizan el sistema operativo Orsay, perderán la aplicación nativa. Ese software antecedió al que la compañía incorporó en sus televisores más recientes.
En el caso de LG, quedarán fuera los televisores sin versiones modernas de webOS, entre ellos las series Nano LED LM9600 e Infinia LX9500, comercializadas antes de que la marca adoptara de forma extendida su sistema actual para pantallas inteligentes.
PUBLICIDAD
Los televisores Sony Bravia de las series KDL, XBR y W95, que funcionan con software propietario basado en Linux, también podrían perder el acceso. La situación es distinta para los modelos con Android TV, que cuentan con un ciclo de soporte más amplio y reciben versiones recientes del sistema.
La nómina incluye además televisores Panasonic VIERA de generaciones anteriores, entre ellos las familias VT50, AX900 y TC-P50VT25, que pertenecen a una etapa previa en el desarrollo de televisores conectados y ya no reciben mejoras compatibles con los requisitos actuales de Netflix.
Los reproductores Apple TV de primera, segunda y tercera generación también resultarán afectados. En estos casos, el acceso dependerá de la versión de tvOS que admita cada equipo y de su capacidad para recibir actualizaciones; los que no puedan actualizar el sistema perderán la aplicación nativa en la fecha prevista.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo saber si un dispositivo quedará sin Netflix
No es necesario contactar al soporte técnico para hacer una primera verificación. Existen tres indicios principales: la desaparición del ícono de Netflix, la imposibilidad de descargar o actualizar el servicio, o la aparición de una pantalla de error al iniciar sesión.
Conviene además revisar el modelo exacto y la versión de software desde el menú de configuración. Esa información suele figurar en los apartados “Acerca de”, “Soporte”, “Información del dispositivo” o “Actualización de software”, según cada fabricante.
La pérdida de la aplicación no implica que el televisor o el teléfono dejen de funcionar. En el caso de las pantallas, podrán seguir utilizándose con consolas, decodificadores, reproductores de video, computadoras y otros dispositivos conectados por HDMI. Chromecast, Fire TV y Roku aparecen como alternativas para instalar la aplicación de Netflix desde tiendas que todavía reciben actualizacione

articles.title: Disney+ va-t-il vraiment mettre des pubs partout ? La plateforme clarifie la situation
articles.text:
Disney+ va-t-il vraiment mettre des pubs partout ? La plateforme clarifie la situation
Suite à la grogne des abonnés après l'annonce de Disney+ que de la publicité pourrait à présent apparaître dans toutes ses offres, y compris premium, la plateforme de streaming a précisé ses propos et tenu à rassurer ses utilisateurs.
Le 18 septembre dernier, Disney+ prévenait ses utilisateurs français que ses conditions générales d'abonnement évoluaient. Parmi les modifications, la plateforme de streaming indiquait que toutes les offres pouvaient dorénavant inclure du contenu promotionnel et des publicités, y compris l'offre Premium.
Un changement de règles qui a naturellement courroucé ses abonnés, et qui oblige aujourd'hui la plateforme de streaming de Disney à apporter des précisions et à rassurer tant bien que mal ses utilisateurs.
Pas de "publicité traditionnelle" sur Disney+ Standard et Premium
Selon nos confrères américains du site The Desk, qui ont pu interroger deux sources internes de The Walt Disney Company, la société ne prévoit pas de mettre des publicités commerciales traditionnnels au sein des films et séries à la demande de sa plateforme.
Disney précise en effet que le terme utilisé de "publicité" visait simplement à s'assurer une plus grande marge de manœuvre pour intégrer des spots promotionnels pour ses autres films, émissions et programmes avant et après la diffusion de contenus sur Disney+, et non des spots publicitaires traditionnels, c'est-à-dire venant de produits ou de services de tiers.
Selon la firme, cela permettait aussi d'avoir une cohérence de ses conditions générales d'utilisation partout dans le monde, y compris dans des territoires où des spots promotionnels de ses propres programmes pouvaient être légalement considérés comme de la pub.
À ce titre, Disney+ renvoie ses utilisateurs vers son Centre d'Aide, où il est précisé que les personnes ayant souscrit un abonnement Disney+ Standard ou Disney+ Premium ne verront pas leur visionnage de films et de séries interrompu par des publicités.
Une rectification de communication bienvenue et rassurante, même s'il faudra toutefois s'habituer à du "contenu promotionnel limité" des produits Disney, quelle que soit son offre. Dans les faits, ce sera la même chose que les spots et courtes bandes-annonces des programmes Disney, comme le font déjà HBO Max ou Paramount+.
Il n'empêche, après l'augmentation relativement récente de ses tarifs et la perte de la qualité 4K pour l'offre Premium, la plateforme de streaming de Disney a tout de même dilué la qualité de son service depuis plusieurs années. Une pilule un peu dure à avaler malgré la diversificaton de son offre avec l'arrivée du sport, de l'espace Hulu et des programmes M6+.
Le salut de Disney+ viendra-t-il de la gratuité ? Alors qu'une offre Disney+ Gratuit est actuellement en train d'être testée au Brésil, et qu'elle devrait probablement arriver sous peu dans l'Hexagone, la plateforme de streaming semble se projeter sur le territoire de l'AVOD ("Advertising Video On Demand", ou "vidéo à la demande financée par la publicité"), au moment où ce type de plateformes financées par la publicité connaît un véritable essor, à l'instar des françaises TF1+, M6+ et France.tv.

articles.title: Ekai raises $1.7M to give enterprise AI agents verified business context - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Ekai raises $1.7M to give enterprise AI agents verified business context
Enterprise data startup Ekai Inc. today announced $1.7 million in new funding for software that builds the business context artificial intelligence agents need before they can be trusted with corporate data.
Ekai provides a platform that writes the semantic models and data transformation code AI tools rely on to read a company’s data warehouse correctly. Its starting point is the people who run the business. Domain experts define what a metric or term means, and Ekai treats those definitions as ground truth before converting them into machine-readable logic and validation rules. Nothing generated ships until it has been checked against the warehouse data, according to the company.
Starting with the experts is what the company calls forward-engineering. Much of the market, Ekai argues, works backward by inferring meaning from the business intelligence tools and queries a company already runs.
“Reverse-engineering from existing BI dashboards, query history, your dbt project, is asking the exhaust pipe what the engine was thinking,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Moatassim “Mo” Aidrus. “This is useful for documenting what you have, but it does nothing for what you need next.”
Co-founder and Chief AI Officer Hussnain Ahmed said the problem starts with the models. Foundation models know a term such as “active user” but have no idea what it means inside a particular company or where it lives in its data warehouse. Under Ekai’s approach, a definition like that is captured from the people who define the business and “owned by someone with their name on it.”
Ekai said that in early engagements, semantic modeling work that has historically taken teams three to six months was completed in as little as six hours. The company credits verification for the speed. When experts settle definitions up front, nobody has to guess what the data means, correct the guess and try again.
The context engineering conversation now running through AI infrastructure is mostly about how agents manage memory, retrieval and prompts in real time, and Ekai keeps some distance from it. The company says its work sits a layer below, on whether the business meaning an agent reasons over was ever verified in the first place and who signed off on each definition.
Boston early-stage investor Misneach led the pre-seed round, with participation from Cambridge AI venture fund and studio C10 Labs. Ekai said the money will accelerate product development and go-to-market operations and deepen its platform integrations.
Mark Coffey, co-founder and managing partner at Misneach, said Aidrus, Ahmed and third co-founder Tero Miikki each spent more than two decades in leadership roles at Accenture plc, Microsoft Corp. and UPM-Kymmene Oyj. That work put them in the room with chief technology and data officers trying to get AI into production. The founders “watched it go unsolved from the other side of the table,” Coffey said.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker To Get Easier Mode and PC Performance Boost in Update
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 23rd 2026
	
	
	
	
The Blood of Dawnwalker To Get Easier Mode and PC Performance Boost in Update
The Blood of Dawnwalker launched at the start of September with a strong start, selling over a million copies within the first week of launch. Following that success, it was confirmed that a sequel was already in the works, however, apparently one sticking point for many players was that the game didn't launch with enough difficulty options—especially not ones that make the gameplay more approachable. According to Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, game director for The Blood of Dawnwalker, in a recent interview with Eurogamer, an October update is en route to add a new difficulty mode. 
[Editor's note: Our in-depth handheld performance review of The Blood of Dawnwalker is now live]
We will introduce an additional difficulty level, but an easier one, because many people are asking for a more easy difficulty. The Story mode which we have right now will be a different difficulty—we will call it Demanding or something like this—and we will add a new Story mode which will be even easier for people who don't want to experience the combat, they just want to learn the story and go through the game without this gameplay challenge.
After the new difficulty mode is added, the game will have five difficulty settings in total: Story, the-mode-formerly-known-as-Story, Fair, Challenging, and Duelist. In addition to the new, easier story mode, Tomaszkiewicz also said that October's "big patch" will also fix a host of bugs, improve combat fluidity and intuitiveness, NPC responsiveness—specifically relating to wild animals, making them less of a threat when players are speeding past them—and performance on PC. 
Tomaszkiewicz also hinted at a New Game Plus mode and adding more enemies to the game in order to improve gameplay variety, although he was unable to outright confirm that these changes will be made or when they would potentially come to the game, with Tomaszkiewicz joking that "we will have the proper beats with our publishing team, and if I tell you more, they will kill me."
