articles.title: Amazon bloquea a Muse, la IA de Meta que puede realizar compras por internet sin supervisión humana
articles.text:
Amazon bloqueó el acceso de Muse, el nuevo agente de inteligencia artificial de Meta, a su plataforma de comercio electrónico después de determinar que el sistema podía realizar compras y acceder a información de las cuentas sin autorización de la compañía.
Amazon sostiene que Meta nunca solicitó permiso para que Muse utilizara su sitio web. La compañía también cuestiona que el agente no se identifique mientras navega por Amazon y afirma que puede acceder a páginas de cuentas e historiales de pedidos cuando el usuario se lo solicita.
PUBLICIDAD
Desde el domingo por la noche, quienes intentaban utilizar Muse para comprar en Amazon encontraban un mensaje que advertía que el acceso continuado de un agente de IA no autorizado infringía las condiciones de uso de la plataforma.
Amazon cuestiona cómo funciona Muse
El principal argumento de Amazon es que Muse opera como un tercero que accede a su plataforma sin que la empresa haya aceptado esa interacción. Según la compañía, esto puede generar riesgos relacionados con la privacidad, la seguridad y el manejo de información confidencial.
Amazon también afirmó que Muse aparentemente captura y almacena credenciales proporcionadas por los usuarios. Meta, sin embargo, sostiene que el agente no puede ver las contraseñas ni los métodos de pago. La empresa asegura que esas credenciales se almacenan de forma segura para que Muse pueda utilizarlas sin acceder directamente a ellas.
PUBLICIDAD
El problema está relacionado con la forma en que Meta diseñó el agente. Muse puede conectarse a servicios que cuentan con una API pública utilizando las credenciales entregadas por el usuario. Cuando un servicio no dispone de una API, Meta explica que Muse puede utilizarlo mediante un navegador, de una manera similar a como lo haría una persona.
Muse puede realizar compras y otras tareas
Meta presentó Muse el 8 de septiembre como un agente personal capaz de completar tareas de varios pasos. A diferencia de un chatbot tradicional, el sistema puede interactuar con servicios de correo electrónico, calendarios, restaurantes, pagos y plataformas de compras.
El agente está disponible de forma gratuita, con opciones de suscripción, y puede utilizarse en iOS, Android, WhatsApp y desde la web de Muse.
Meta afirma que Muse funciona dentro de una máquina virtual segura y que cuenta con su propio navegador. Además, el sistema consulta al usuario antes de realizar acciones consideradas delicadas, como enviar un correo electrónico o efectuar una compra. Un agente independiente denominado Sentinel debe aprobar todo lo que Muse envía a internet.
PUBLICIDAD
A pesar de estas medidas, Amazon considera que el hecho de que Muse pueda navegar por su plataforma sin identificarse plantea un problema diferente: el sitio no puede distinguir fácilmente entre una persona y un agente automatizado que está actuando en su nombre.
El conflicto llega después de otros enfrentamientos
La disputa con Meta forma parte de una estrategia más amplia de Amazon para limitar el acceso de agentes externos a su plataforma. Durante el último año, la compañía también ha tomado medidas contra agentes de compras desarrollados por otras empresas.
Uno de los casos más importantes involucra a Perplexity y su navegador Comet. Amazon obtuvo inicialmente una orden judicial preliminar, pero posteriormente un tribunal de apelaciones estadounidense determinó que, bajo la legislación federal contra el acceso no autorizado a sistemas informáticos, era el usuario y no necesariamente la empresa de IA quien accedía a los ordenadores de Amazon.
PUBLICIDAD
El fallo dejó abierta, no obstante, la posibilidad de que Amazon utilice argumentos contractuales y relacionados con sus condiciones de servicio. Precisamente ese es el lenguaje que aparece ahora en el mensaje mostrado a los usuarios de Muse.
Amazon y Meta también son socios comerciales
El enfrentamiento resulta especialmente significativo porque Amazon y Meta mantienen relaciones comerciales. Los usuarios pueden comprar productos de Amazon desde Facebook e Instagram desde 2023, mientras que Meta también mantiene un acuerdo con Amazon para utilizar sus chips Graviton en determinadas cargas de trabajo de inteligencia artificial.
Para Amazon, además, el control sobre su plataforma tiene una dimensión económica importante. La compañía obtuvo más de 68.000 millones de dólares en ingresos publicitarios durante el último año, un negocio estrechamente relacionado con el tráfico de usuarios y la exposición de productos patrocinados.
PUBLICIDAD
Amazon asegura que está conversando directamente con Meta y no ha confirmado si emprenderá acciones legales.
La carrera por controlar las compras con IA
Muse se ha convertido rápidamente en uno de los nuevos ejemplos de agentes capaces de ejecutar tareas en internet. Una semana después de su lanzamiento llegó al primer puesto entre las aplicaciones gratuitas de la App Store estadounidense, incluso por encima de ChatGPT.
Sus primeros usuarios han utilizado el agente para tareas como buscar descuentos, modificar pólizas de seguros y completar carritos de compra.
Amazon también desarrolla sus propios sistemas de compra asistida. En mayo lanzó Alexa for Shopping y cuenta con Buy for Me, una función capaz de buscar productos en sitios externos. La diferencia, según Amazon, es que su sistema se identifica ante las marcas y permite que estas decidan si quieren participar.

articles.title: Kantata debuts Agent Studio for building custom AI agents in plain language - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Kantata debuts Agent Studio for building custom AI agents in plain language
Professional services automation software company Kantata Inc. today unveiled Agent Studio, a tool that lets services firms build custom artificial intelligence agents by describing the job they want done in plain language.
The release goes after a problem Kantata says is building in the professional services automation market. Vendors are shipping narrow agents by the dozen, each scoped to a single job such as resourcing or risk reporting.
The company argues that every new one arrives as another silo to maintain. Kantata sells a single agent that it says carries context across the whole platform. That’s the Expertise Agent, which Kantata launched in June and calls the first AI superagent for professional services.
Agent Studio sits inside the Kantata Expertise Engine and works through conversation. A user describes the job, and the Expertise Agent assembles the new agent and refines it the same way, with every build and edit checked for correctly structured inputs and outputs before it is published.
Nobody has to fill in a form or write code. Once live, an agent can be triggered by a person or picked up automatically by a workflow on a single command.
The intended users are practice leads and delivery directors. Under Agent Studio a standard gets written down once, covering the format, the escalation rules and the outputs a recurring deliverable needs, then applied automatically rather than rebuilt by whoever happens to be staffed that week. Kantata calls the overhead it removes a “prompt tax,” the cycle of drafting and reformatting that a team repeats every time it re-explains the same job to an AI tool.
“When it comes to professional services, AI isn’t the differentiator — expertise is,” Chief Executive Michael Speranza said. “Any vendor can give a firm a tool to build AI agents. But if all you’re doing is automating processes, you’re just racing to the bottom and simply reducing costs, rather than developing differentiation.”
Chief Technology Officer Vikas Nehru put the case on governance grounds, calling an agent that improvises “a liability in a business where the same deliverable has to hold up in front of a client every time.”
Finnish invoice automation company Basware Oyj uses Kantata’s software in its own professional services operation. Mark Johnston, its chief customer officer, said he wants his services team with customers rather than “doing documentation, figuring out resourcing and entering their billable time,” and that Kantata lets the firm build agents to absorb that work.
The announcement cites Forrester Research Inc. on the wider point. Ted Schadler, a vice president and principal analyst at the firm, has written that the only durable route to business advantage now runs through putting a company’s own proprietary knowledge and expertise to work in AI models, apps and agents.
Agent Studio is available now and in use by customers, according to Kantata.
Kantata launched in 2022 following the December 2021 merger of Mavenlink and Kimble Applications, a deal Accel-KKR led, and the company says more than 1,500 organizations now run its software.

articles.title: AI data center boom hits growing resistance as $68 billion in US projects are blocked or delayed
articles.text:
A hot potato: Data center developers are facing stronger resistance as they try to add capacity for AI workloads across the United States. The pushback is delaying or blocking projects worth tens of billions of dollars and prompting states and local governments to scrutinize their power, water and land-use demands. As the AI buildout accelerates, community opposition is becoming a material obstacle to the industry's ability to add computing capacity at the pace it wants.
Local opposition blocked or delayed 45 data center projects valued at $68 billion during the second quarter, according to Data Center Watch, a research initiative from AI intelligence company 10a Labs. The affected projects accounted for more than half of the large-scale data center developments the group began tracking during the period.
The disputes are centered on the practical demands of AI infrastructure. New facilities require large amounts of electricity, water and land, and often need new transmission lines, substations or other utility upgrades. In some areas, residents are challenging individual projects. Elsewhere, local governments are considering moratoriums or new rules before developers submit permit applications.
Data Center Watch said it identified 843 groups opposing data center development in 49 states. Hawaii was the only state without a group on its list. The organization also said 30 statehouses introduced or adopted measures related to data center siting, electricity use or water consumption.
"New groups continue to emerge, opposition is appearing across a wide range of states and jurisdictions, and online petition signatures continue to grow," Miquel Vila, the group's lead analyst, told Bloomberg.
The second-quarter total was below the first quarter, when Data Center Watch counted 75 contested projects with an estimated value of about $130 billion. But the latest figures show that resistance is affecting a large share of proposed developments, not just a few high-profile projects.
For the technology industry, the issue is becoming a constraint on AI expansion. Companies including Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet are building more and more data centers to support training and inference workloads, which require significant amounts of electricity and cooling.
Developers have pursued several approaches to meet those needs, including larger grid connections, dedicated generation and on-site power systems. Those plans can create additional opposition, especially when they involve natural gas generation or major utility infrastructure.
Water use is another concern. Operators have promoted cooling systems designed to reduce consumption, including closed-loop designs. Critics, however, argue that even more efficient systems can place pressure on local supplies when deployed at the scale required for major AI campuses.
Opposition has also spread through online campaigns. One petition against a proposed Tennessee project drew more than 500,000 signatures on Change.org during the quarter, Data Center Watch said. The group said the petition represented more than one-third of all signatures collected on the platform during that period.
Data Center Watch is also seeing similar campaigns outside the United States. The group expanded its reporting this year to include opposition in Europe, Australia, South Africa and other regions. Those efforts focus on many of the same issues seen in the US, including project approvals, power demand and water use.
"As with many other trends, the US has generally been at the forefront, but the phenomenon is increasingly becoming global," Vila said. "We anticipate that this will just become more prominent as data center development expands across the globe."

articles.title: Nova função contra roubo de iPhone aparece no beta do iOS • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nova função contra roubo de iPhone aparece no beta do iOS
Chamada internamente de AutoLock, novidade deve bloquear celular ao detectar que foi puxado da mão do dono.
A Apple está preparando um novo recurso antifurto para o iPhone chamado internamente de AutoLock. A novidade já aparece no beta mais recente do iOS e tem como principal objetivo bloquear o celular em caso de roubo ou furto. Não custa lembrar: o Android já oferece tecnologia similar pelo menos desde 2025, e o Brasil foi o primeiro país a recebê-la.
No caso do iPhone, o software detecta quando o aparelho foi retirado de maneira brusca da mão do dono, além de levar em consideração a desconexão com outros dispositivos do usuário e o desbloqueio contínuo por um período extendido.
A identificação do novo recurso foi feita por meio de códigos analisados pelo site 9to5Mac. A maçã também deve incluir melhorias na segurança do iPhone para evitar falso positivo no desbloqueio por biometria, entre outras novidades.
Segundo o código analisado, o AutoLock vai usar os sensores do iPhone que já contabilizam passos e outros movimentos para identificar um possível roubo. Além do “puxão” e da aceleração característica, outras situações “suspeitas” serão analisadas para configurar roubo ou furto:
A partir disso, a ideia é que o iPhone bloqueie a tela para evitar acesso a informações sensíveis. Não foram revelados detalhes como o tempo máximo considerado para o desbloqueio ou para a perda de conexão.
A versão de teste foi liberada nesta segunda-feira (21) exclusivamente para desenvolvedores, que podem otimizar seus apps antes do lançamento. Vale ressaltar que o AutoLock não está ativo no beta, apesar de disponível no sistema. Portanto, a Apple pode não liberar o recurso já na versão final do iOS 27.2.
Além do AutoLock em si, há outros mecanismos previstos para o update. Formas de evitar problemas na identificação do FaceID devem ser incluídas no sistema, assim como ajustes para não acionar o bloqueio automático de forma errada.
Da mesma forma, algumas situações específicas podem derrubar o bloqueio, incluindo biometria e locais familiares. Essa identificação de segurança já está presente em serviços como o Proteção de Dispositivo Roubado, por exemplo, e deve entrar em uma espécie de “votação” onde o AutoLock solicita o bloqueio e o sistema aceita caso o celular esteja fora dessas condições.

articles.title: Google Meet intègre Quick notes pour résumer les réunions sur une seule page avec Gemini
articles.text:
Prendre des notes pendant une réunion de travail, ce n’est généralement pas quelque chose qui nous motive. Mais il faut bien que quelqu’un s’y colle. Ou pas. Depuis le développement des systèmes d’intelligence artificielle, ce n’est plus nécessaire.
L’application de visioconférence Google Meet, par exemple, permet de déléguer la prise de notes à l’IA Gemini. Et même pendant vos réunions physiques. La firme de Mountain View va plus loin en ajoutant une fonctionnalité qui devrait ravir bon nombre de professionnels.
iPhone 18 Pro Max à 199€ ! Obtenez 50€ de remise immédiate avec le code NEW50 et jusqu’à 150€ de bonus reprise. Associez-le à un forfait 250Go à 29,99€/mois pendant un an. Livraison offerte.
Gemini résume les notes de vos réunions Google Meet désormais
Recevoir plusieurs pages de notes sur la réunion qui vient de se terminer, c’est bien. Recevoir un résumé tenant sur une seule, c’est mieux. Voilà ce que permet « Quick notes », nouveauté annoncée par Google.
Son principe est simple : en plus des notes complètes, Gemini élabore un résumé tenant sur une seule page de Google Docs, avec une liste des points importants et éventuellement des tâches à accomplir.
    À lire aussi : 
    Google Meet simplifie la gestion de vos réunions grâce à sa nouvelle page d’accueil
Le texte prend place dans l’onglet principal du Docs généré à l’issue de la réunion. Un second onglet permet de voir l’ensemble des notes prises lors de cette dernière. Cerise sur le gâteau : le résumé peut être automatiquement envoyé par mail aux participants, sitôt la réunion terminée.
« Quick notes » ne nécessite pas d’activer un paramètre quelconque. Disponible depuis ce mardi 22 septembre, la fonction est automatiquement activée pour les abonnés à certaines formules Google Workspace (Business Standard et Plus, Enterprise Standard et Plus, Frontline Plus), ainsi que chez les particuliers disposant d’un abonnement Google AI Pro ou Ultra.
Google a également annoncé de nouveaux réglages permettant aux entreprises de mieux encadrer la prise de notes automatique par l’IA, par exemple en la réservant aux réunions d’au moins trois participants. Ces paramètres entrent en vigueur le 29 septembre.

articles.title: Review: Resident Evil might just be the best gaming adaptation yet
articles.text:
I was on the fence about going to see the latest Resident Evil reboot to review, given how uninspired the prior reboot attempt in 2021 turned out to be. But director Zach Cregger gave us last year’s phenomenal Weapons, and early word of mouth was extremely positive, so I took a chance. I’m glad I did, because the film is terrific. Cregger’s distinctive sensibility is just what the flagging franchise needed: a truly fresh take on a well-trodden fictional world that blends horror, humor, and some pretty over-the-top gore in just the right ratios. And you don’t need to be a Resident Evil franchise fan to enjoy it.
(Spoilers below, but we’ll give you a heads-up before any major reveals.)
When the first Resident Evil game debuted in 1996, it was an immediate commercial and critical success, spawning several sequel games, comics, novels, and a very lucrative film franchise directed by Paul W.S. Anderson and starring Milla Jovovich. Reviews were mixed, despite the films’ massive box office success. The first reboot, Welcome to Raccoon City (2021), was critically panned and had a disappointing box office, grossing just $42 million globally against its $25 million budget. The studio nixed its plans for a direct sequel, and a 2022 Netflix series was also canceled after a less-than-stellar first season.
Enter Cregger, who hadn’t seen any of the original films when he took on the project but was a huge fan of the games, especially Resident Evil 2. Cregger’s take is not a direct game adaptation, but an original story with original characters set in the same fictional universe. Cregger told the audience at CinemaCon earlier this year that his film would have “no narrative acrobatics, time jumps, or disorienting chapter things,” preferring his audience to be “locked in with a protagonist on a foot journey through a world hell-bent on destroying them.” Nor would it be like Weapons; Cregger’s Resident Evil vision, he said, is closer to Evil Dead II yet still “true to the spirit of the games.”

articles.title: NZXT Introduces the S5 RGB and S5 RGB Deluxe ATX Mid-Tower Cases

NZXT Introduces the S5 RGB and S5 RGB Deluxe ATX Mid-Tower Cases
NZXT, a leading brand in PC gaming components and prebuilt systems, today introduced the S5 RGB and S5 RGB Deluxe, two compact steel ATX mid-tower cases with panoramic dual tempered glass and RGB cooling pre-installed. Both models share one chassis, the same materials and the same clearances; the Deluxe adds two more RGB fan units, at the bottom and rear. The S5 RGB marks the return of the S series, the entry tier of NZXT's case lineup.
NZXT made the S5 RGB for the builder who wants a case that looks and feels genuinely well-made. A sturdy steel chassis carries tempered glass across the front and left side, with a steel mesh panel feeding the right-side intake and removable PVC mesh filters at the top and bottom. The single-frame 360 mm RGB reverse fan is pre-installed and turned toward the glass, presenting clean blades through the panel—the side intake filled and wired from the start, with the remaining mounts open for the build.
Johnny Hou, CEO of NZXT"Bringing the S series back is something we've wanted to do for a long time, and this is the moment builders need it most. We started with how the S5 RGB should feel in your hands and how it should look on your desk—solid steel and tempered glass, nothing hollow about it. Then we made sure it was a case anyone could actually put on their desk, whether the hardware going into it is entry-level or top of the line. articles.title: Bambu Lab R1 Review: This one stands alone
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
Great hardware combined with Bambu’s excellent software and smooth user interface puts this laser among the best. The 55W CO2 laser cutter and engraver makes quick work of wood, acrylic, glass, and more.
Pros
- +Easy to assemble
- +Simple to calibrate
- +Great camera accuracy
- +Smaller footprint than other lasers in its class
- +Bambu Suite software
- +Great price
Cons
- -Optional lens required for thicker material
- -Limited material presets listed
- -Loud fans
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Bambu Lab has swung for the fences with its second go at making a laser cutter, and this time, it knocked it out of the park. The Bambu Lab R1 is a standalone, 55W CO2 laser with a roomy 600 x 300 mm work area, a bird’s eye camera for remote positioning, and a well-designed software suite. Priced at $2,499, the laser is a steal compared to other CO2 lasers of the same size and caliber.
You might recall the company’s first laser, a 40w diode packaged inside the H2D, was met with skepticism. Though the company pitched the H2D as the ultimate mini manufacturing machine for makers, many people felt a laser was too dirty to house in the same box as an expensive Core XY printer. Bambu must be listening, because they took everything that was good about the H2D’s diode system and gave it a standalone case with a massive CO2 laser.
The R1 has the same simple unboxing and setup experience as a Bambu Lab printer, making it easy to get started without a ton of prior experience. The only thing it is currently lacking is a more comprehensive set of material presets. Bambu Suite really shines in a market where good hardware is often let down by bad software.
While the Bambu Lab R1 is not a small machine, it does have a smaller footprint than other lasers with a similar work area. It requires a stout work table – and two people to cart it into position – as the machine is over 70 pounds. In its base configuration the R1 has a work area of 600mm x 300mm. With the optional conveyor and riser base, that 300mm can be extended to 3000mm, or 9.8 feet. Of course, you’ll need a lot of space in front of and behind the machine to pull that off. Bambu Lab did a wonderful job putting all of the controls and frequently used ports near the front of the R1 since you won’t want to move it much unless you are lasering something large.
The only flaw I found was the need to manually change focus lenses to cut thicker material. The process to change lenses is tedious, with six screws needing to be removed and replaced with the new lens. The two screws for the toolhead cover are ridiculously small. This process is reminiscent of the early Bambu Lab printer nozzles that required the heater and thermistor to be detached, then reinstalled with thermal paste. Hopefully Bambu Lab will come up with a quick-release lens at some point in the future.
Specifications: Bambu Lab R1
| Machine Footprint | 940 x 560 x 200 mm (37 x 22 x 7.8 inches) | 
| Machine Weight | 33.5 kg (73.8 lbs) | 
| Engraving Size | 600 x 300 mm (23.6 x 11.8 inches) With Conveyor 600 x 3000 mm (23.6 x 118.1 inches) | 
| Material | Cuts wood, acrylic (incl. clear acrylic), leather, fabric, paper, EVA foam, and shell. | 
| Engraves | The above plus coated metal, glass, and ceramic | 
| Laser Type | CO2 | 
| Laser Power | 55W | 
| Laser Wave Length | 10600 nm | 
| Engraving Accuracy | 0.10 mm | 
| Cutting Platform | Metal slats and baseplate included | 
| Connectivity | USB, Wi-Fi | 
| Interface | Color touch screen | 
| MSRP | $2,499 | 
| Release Date | September 22, 2026 | 
Bambu Lab R1: Included in the Box
The Bambu Lab R1 arrives fully assembled with its accessory pack bundled inside the laser enclosure. Accessories include a tool kit, exhaust hose, ventilation fan, antifreeze, funnel, laser alignment sensor, calibration board, and a material pack of basswood plywood and clear acrylic. You will need to supply 1500ml of distilled water to dilute the antifreeze. For the review, we also received the medium and long focus lenses, the conveyor and the riser needed for its use, the auto fire extinguishing system, and a smoke purifier.
Design of the Bambu Lab R1
The Bambu Lab R1 is a beast of a machine, but a well-thought-out one. It’s more compact than other CO2 lasers with the same working area, despite this, weighing over 70lbs. It’s not an easy machine to move. Bambu Lab put all of the controls, ports, and the safety key thoughtfully within easy reach at the front of the machine. The color touchscreen and start button are on top of the machine.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The automatic fire extinguisher ports, USB-C, and safety key are located on the left side of the laser.
The emergency stop button is located on the right side of the laser.
Only the power switch, the exhaust fan, and the coolant filling point are located on the rear of the unit.
Unlike most other lasers, a CO2 laser has a large, glass, liquid-cooled laser tube at the rear of the unit. Antifreeze is mixed with distilled water for the coolant to prevent the glass tube from freezing should it be kept in a garage, basement or even if you lose power in your house during the winter.
The laser fires a beam which is directed to the tool head with mirrors.
On some lasers, calibrating these mirrors can be a chore. Bambu Lab developed a laser alignment sensor, which clips to the toolhead and allows the laser to align the mirrors itself in just about a minute.
The Bambu Lab R1 has an excellent positioning system. There is a bird's eye camera on the lid of the laser, which requires that the lid be up when measuring. This takes a little getting used to since I reflexively shut the lid of a laser when I walk away from it. There is a camera mounted on the toolhead as well as a distance-measuring laser, instead of a clunky mechanical probe. The R1 tracks the toolhead position with XY encoders. The system worked great out of the box with no camera calibration needed. The camera is listed as having a .2mm positioning accuracy.
The Bambu Lab R1 is rated to cut up to 18mm wood and 20mm acrylic but doing so requires changing the focus lens in the tool head and then doing a five minute vision accuracy calibration. To change lenses, you need to remove two extremely tiny 1.5mm screws from the toolhead cover and four screws from the focus lens. It would be nice if they could develop a quick release for the lens, since as it is, this is not a process I’d want to have to do frequently.
A built-in air assist works to keep charring down and keep the laser lens clear. It is not adjustable, being either on or off, and it's powerful enough to move lightweight objects if they are not stuck down.
Given its size, the R1 is not likely to be used anywhere other than a shop or workroom, which is great because this thing is loud. The cooling fans in the laser don’t ever stop, and they are pretty loud on their own. When the laser is activated, it sounds like a jet engine spooling up. Between the noise of the laser and the air purification, it’s the loudest laser I’ve reviewed.
Assembling the Bambu Lab R1
The Bambu Lab R1 is fully assembled out of the box. Setup requires removing the accessory box, removing a cage around the tool head, and removing two stops holding the XY carriage in place for shipping. At initial power up the printer walks you through these steps from the touch screen.
There is a short calibration routine that automatically calibrates the laser’s mirrors by clipping the laser alignment sensor to the toolhead. In no time at all, you are ready to go.
The riser base comes in four large assemblies that are screwed together. You need to remove the base plate from the laser before setting it atop the riser. A data cable runs from the laser to the riser base, and requires deft hands to attach. Rubber feet on the bottom of the main laser unit hold it the correct position
The laser is cooled with a mixture of distilled water and antifreeze, which is poured into the rear of the laser with an included funnel. Pay close attention to the instruction booklet when adding coolant. The instructions call for “preparing” 1500ml of distilled water, then adding antifreeze to an indicated level on the rear sight window. But what it means is to pour in the antifreeze, then add as much of the 1500ml of water as needed to hit the correct level. Getting this backward makes a bit of a mess. After mopping up, I added the correct amount of water and coolant to the laser. The coolant must be topped off after turning the laser on, so don’t move the laser into a position where you cannot access the coolant port until you do this.
Safety Precautions for the Bambu Lab R1
The Bambu Lab R1 is a fully enclosed and safe Class 1 laser by itself. When running with the riser base and conveyor, it moves to a Class 4 laser. Operating a Class 4 laser requires laser-safe glasses that are not provided with the laser. I was not able to see any leakage of laser light through the riser base, but it is unavoidable when running with the conveyor. Laser light can cause severe damage to eyes and skin, and care should be taken to keep small children and pets away while the laser is in use.
The R1 has a number of built-in safety features. There is an equipment key preinstalled on the left side of the laser. When not in use this key can be pulled to prevent unauthorized access. The laser will not operate with the enclosure’s lid up and will quickly pause the job if the lid is raised while in use. If there is a problem with the job, the machine can be stopped from the touch screen, and for major problems, there is a red kill switch on the right side of the machine, which will quickly cut power to the machine completely. The laser has flame sensors which will stop the job if they detect any issues. Bambu Lab provided its optional auto fire-extinguishing system for the review. This unit has a replaceable gas canister and plugs into the left side of the laser.
Even with a good air purifier, some materials should not be burned with a laser due to their chemical makeup. Dallas Maker Space has published a list of safe and hazardous materials to use with their laser. The list of no-nos includes some plastics like PVC, fiberglass, and certain types of foams.
Software for the Bambu Lab R1
Bambu Suite was developed to run the lasers on the H series and also handle the cutting function on H2 and A2 printers. It might be the easiest to use laser software I’ve seen. The laser is connected to Wi-Fi from the touchscreen, and Bambu Suite connects to it just like a 3D printer. You import whatever you want to cut or engrave, choose the process type, hit Prepare, then select Measure, line up your art with the material, and pick the material you are using. Finally, you press Make and off it goes.
The only thing that the software doesn’t have is a large list of default materials. The basics are there, but hopefully more will be added over time. As it is, a number of the projects I did required internet searches and guesswork to find material settings that worked.
Makerworld is accessible directly from Bambu Suite, and it has an expanding group of shared laser projects to help you get started.
Engraving / Cutting with the Bambu Lab R1
For the first job, we used the test file from Bambu Lab that includes line drawing, engraving, and cutting on 3 mm basswood plywood. The test file did not list the settings, but the overall job took under two minutes to complete and looks really good. The cuts show much less charring than you would see on a diode laser.
Next, I tried a really intricate butterfly decoration from PabloLab on Makerworld.com. Using the default material settings for 3mm basswood, 75% power at 30 mm/s, the cut was perfect. The butterfly and the interior cuts dropped out of the material with no weeding needed. I should point out I broke off one of her antennae in handling.
The Bambu Lab R1 is rated to cut up to 18mm black walnut and 20mm acrylic, but the thicker wood requires the optional medium or long focus lenses. I tested cutting on a piece of pine lumber that is 19.5mm thick but is much softer than black walnut. There was no material default for anything thicker than 3mm. The cut on the left used the long focus lens and did the best cut at the lowest power, using 80% power at 10mm/s and 4 passes. The cut in the middle used the medium focus lens at 85% power at 5 mm/s and required 5 passes. The short focus lens really did not totally punch through the bottom of the material. The cuts are charred due to using 100% power at 4 mm/s through multiple tries.
For cutting out stickers out of sheets of sticker paper, we used the material preset for 200g kraft paper, 45% power at 250mm/s. The cuts were perfect and only took a few seconds. With a jig mounted on the cutting plate, the results are repeatable page after page.
There was no material preset for PETG so with a little trial and error we stepped that down to 65% power at 35mm/s for 2mm PETG and 20% power at 20mm/s for 1mm PETG. With air assist, the results were terrific, with just a very little smoke cloudiness at the edges of the PETG cuts. At these speeds, the cuts all took less than a minute.
Where most lasers just pass right through clear materials, CO2 lasers run at a high enough frequency to cut and engrave them. Using the shape library in Bambu Suite for the designs, we cut a bunch of blanks for use with our UV printer out of clear PETG sheets and clear acrylic. The material settings in Bambu Suite were perfect for 3mm clear acrylic at 80% power at 10mm/s speed.
CO2 lasers can also engrave glass with no masking needed, though a thin smear of liquid soap is suggested to keep chipping down. There was no material preset for glass, so a quick internet search led to settings from a competitor’s 55-watt CO2 laser. Using 30% power and 250mm/s, with air assist on, the engraving took just seconds and looks excellent.
CO2 lasers can’t cut metal, but they do a good job engraving coated metal. The Bambu lab R1has a curved surface machining mode for curved surfaces like this flask and tumblers. The auto measure function creates a 3D map of the material’s surface and shows the engravable area. Using the settings for aluminum business cards, 70% power at 400mm/s, the job took less than a minute and looks sharp and clear.
Bottom Line
The Bambu Lab R1 is an impressive step into the laser market. Good hardware with even better software makes the R1 an excellent choice for makers and small businesses needing an easy-to-use CO2 laser. It’s simple enough for a beginner to use, leaving you with more time to focus on making art, not fussing over settings.
Retailing at $2,499, the R1 is more expensive than a hobby-level diode, but a downright bargain compared to the competition. If you’re serious about making cool things or running a small business, the price is worth it.
By combining a 55W CO2, a generous 600 x 300 mm work area, and automated mirror calibration, it delivers high-grade cutting performance through wood, acrylic, and glass with minimal charring. While the manual lens swap process is a minor hassle and the operational noise requires a dedicated workspace or shop environment, its performance outclasses most competitors in its price range.
If you’re not ready to invest in a professional-grade machine, check out the Creality Falcon A1 Pro, a very capable 20W for $1,099. If you’re thinking about engraving glass or handling materials without charring, the xTool F2 Ultra UV is a great “cold” laser that runs for $4,299. If you want to take your laser with you, a portable xTool F1 laser is a heck of a deal at $819.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: British Army spends £16 million on 1,000 small drones in bid to boost battlefield operations
articles.text:
The British Army is spending £16 million on 1,000 small drones in a bid to boost battlefield operations
Pocket spy drones are on the way
- Over 1,000 small drones are being added to the British Army’s modernized battlefield surveillance kit
- 245 FOXE-NATO drones from Evolve Dynamics in Hampshire, England, have been ordered by the Ministry of Defence (MoD), with a further 670 built by California-based Skydio
- A further £400 million investment in “long-endurance surveillance drones” has also been announced
The British government has announced spending on over 1,000 small surveillance drones for the British Army, as part of its Defence Investment Plan. This includes compact, lightweight devices assembled at UK-based Evolve Dynamics, designed for fast deployment.
Announcing the spending plans and investment, the UK’s Ministry of Defence has emphasized the use of what it terms Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) drones as a step forward in detecting emerging threats.
In addition, a huge £400 million is being invested in replacing the Watchkeeper Uncrewed Air System. This unmanned drone surveillance program has been in operation since 2014, and is being retired in 2027.
UK companies handling delivery
In total, 1,025 smaller drones are being procured in the £16 million deal, which involves deals with a trio of UK-based companies. Among these small and medium sized companies is Evolve Dynamics, a Hampshire-based company which is supplying the army with 245 FOXE-NATO drones. Weighing under 250g and equipped with infrared cameras for nighttime use, the FOXE-NATO drones are also designed for quick deployment from a backpack or pouch.
Meanwhile, Marlborough Communications Limited, in Surrey, England, is supplying the MoD with 670 Skydio X10 INTL drones, also capable of a fast deployment and speeds of up to 45 mpg. Skydio is a California-based company.
Finally, Exeter-based Brigantes Consulting and and Harmattan AI are delivering 110 SONORA drones. These are training devices, to prepare soldiers for using field-ready drones.
“Our soldiers deserve the best technology, and that’s what we’re delivering,” said Luke Pollard MP, the UK’s Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry.

“From small drones giving troops eyes on the enemy, to the AR5 offering commanders better intelligence over the battlefield, we’re transforming the Army’s ability to see, understand and act first.”
“This is defence procurement that backs British industry, creates skilled jobs and keeps our Armed Forces ahead of our adversaries.”
Long-endurance
Joining the smaller surveillance and training drone expenditure, the MoD has announced a £400 million spend on a fleet of Tekever AR5 surveillance drones (initially six, rising to 24 by 2029), designed and built for endurance. These craft have already seen action in Ukraine.
“We are proud to be delivering the AR5 to the British Army at this critical moment for national security,” said Tekever UK’s Managing Director Karl Brew. “This investment allows us to grow our UK operations, create hundreds of skilled jobs and bring cutting-edge surveillance technology, proven on the battlefield in Ukraine, into service with British forces.”
These units, capable of carrying up to 50kg of cameras and sensors, are being assembled at Swindon, UK, and the contract is expected to create 1,000 jobs at sites around the UK, including sites in the South West, Edinburgh, and London.

articles.title: Qualcomm reveals Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, its most powerful SoC ever [benchmark update]
articles.text:
Snapdragon flew me out to Hawaii to check out its latest chip, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and, for the first time ever, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, the company’s premier “extreme-levelled” mobile chipset.
We did live benchmarking with Geekbench 6 and saw a single-core score of 4,293 and a multi-core score of 12,924. We also used Geekbench 7 and had a single-core score of 3,608 and a multi-core score of 12,257.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series has a reengineered Qualcomm Hexagon NPU that allows the Elite Gen 6’s agentic AI features to comprehend personal context across devices; it also tries to anticipate your needs, learn and adapt over time, and auto-prompt photo editing. The Elite Extreme has more advanced agentic AI with deeper contextual understanding. Additionally, it has significantly enhanced on-device AI performance. Extreme is supposed to deliver agents faster, more personalized and more dependable.
Qualcomm says its Custom-built Oryon CPU offers industry-leading performance, with peak speeds up to 5.0GHz. Additionally, it says the CPU is fast, offering responsive experiences across play and creativity, and seamless multitasking throughout the day. The Elite Extreme has all of this plus “Snapdragon’s most powerful gaming, creation, and AI experiences.” Qualcomm also says it offers system-level contributions for an overall better-performing package. It also includes the VVC codec for more power-efficient videos.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6’s next-gen Adreno GPU sports faster, smoother gameplay with intelligent graphic enhancements, as well as responsive controls, fluid reactions, and a full suite of Snapdragon 8 Elite gaming experiences. The 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, on the other hand, sports AI-dedicated Adreno matrix cores and runs advanced models. Additionally, it features Adreno Neural Fusion for AI-driven super resolution and frame generation and even has 18MB of high-performance memory.
Additionally, the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 offers cinema-grade video with APV support, as well as 8K60 video capture and 4K240 ultra HD slow-motion.
And Qualcomm is already launching the first product with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6: the Motorola Signature 27.

articles.title: Discord's age verification era is upon us, despite community backlash | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Starting Wednesday, Discord, the community messaging platform, will roll out age verification measures to all users.
The rollout comes after the company initially delayed its age verification plans in February due to backlash from users concerned that biometric scans and ID checks could jeopardize their privacy. Those concerns weren’t unfounded; last year, a third-party vendor that works with Discord was breached, potentially exposing the data of 70,000 users’ data, including government ID photos and selfies used for identity verification.
“Age assurance draws strong opinions and skepticism, especially when it involves sharing biometric information or a form of ID,” Discord CTO Stanislav Vishnevskiy wrote in a blog post, published Tuesday. “At the same time, age assurance laws are expanding, and since my last post we’ve had to launch age assurance in other regions, including in Brazil and in Texas.”
However, Vishnevskiy says more than 90% of Discord users won’t have to verify their age. He explains that Discord will instead use existing account data to detect “signals,” like account tenure (how long an account has existed), device and activity data, and other usage patterns, to determine whether a user belongs in the adult, teen, or unconfirmed age group.
Discord says that it doesn’t estimate users’ ages based on message content, profile data, or demographic attributes.
“The way a typical 15-year-old uses Discord (including how many communities they’re a part of and how they interact with others) looks different in aggregate from how a typical 30-year-old uses Discord,” the company wrote in a separate, technical blog post, also published Tuesday. “Our [machine learning] model has learned these patterns to predict whether a given account likely belongs to an adult or a teen.”
This doesn’t mean that Discord is collecting new user data. It’s standard for social media companies to retain this kind of data on their customers, even though it might feel unsettling to see it spelled out so overtly.
Because local laws have required Discord to use age assurance technology in certain regions due to local law, the company was able to train its model on reliably confirmed data linking user behavior to age.
If Discord is not confident that a user is an adult, that user can still prove their age without a biometric or ID scan. They can appeal by sharing a credit card or age group data from their Apple App Store or Google Play Store account.
For confirmed adults, nothing about the platform will change. Teens accounts, however, will automatically be blocked from accessing age-restricted servers or channels. Message requests from people who aren’t their friends will go to a separate message requests inbox, and teens will get alerts when accepting friend requests from someone they don’t share mutual friends with.
As governments around the world continue passing age verification requirements in an attempt to protect children online, experts warn that these age checks can create a host of new privacy and security issues. That leaves platforms like Discord with a difficult choice: comply or risk sanctions.

articles.title: Des jeux PS5 tournent désormais sur Xbox Series X, merci l'émulation
articles.text:
L’émulation a toujours couru derrière les consoles avec une génération de retard, le temps que les machines soient comprises, disséquées et reproduites. La PS4 est désormais bien servie sur PC, mais la PS5 restait un chantier à peine ouvert, avec une poignée de projets balbutiants. L’un d’eux, l’émulateur Kyty, vient de faire un pas de côté aussi inattendu que spectaculaire : un port expérimental le fait fonctionner directement sur Xbox Series X et Series S, où il exécute ses premiers jeux PS5.
Quake II version PS5, sur la machine de Microsoft
La compatibilité se limiterait pour l’instant à une poignée de titres simples, avec des performances très en retrait (le mot « expérimental » est presque flatteur). Le premier jeu montré en fonctionnement est la version PS5 de Quake II, un classique de 1997 remis au goût du jour. Autant dire que personne n’annulera son achat de PS5 cette semaine.
 
Reste la démonstration technique : émuler une console récente revient à traduire un livre pendant qu’on le lit, phrase par phrase, sans jamais ralentir, et l’exercice pardonne peu. Le port profite néanmoins d’un terrain favorable, puisque la PS5 et la Series X partagent des architectures cousines signées AMD (processeur et puce graphique de la même famille), ce qui rend l’exploit un peu moins fou qu’il n’y paraît, mais pas moins intéressant techniquement : l’émulation n’intervient que sur les fonctions spécifiques à la PS5, le reste étant plutôt « traduit » (pensez à Proton sur SteamOS).
L’émulation PlayStation grignote du terrain
Sur PC, l’émulation PS4 a gagné une maturité telle que le jeu en ligne tourne désormais sans passer par les serveurs de Sony. Cet été, des jeux PS5 s’affichaient déjà, laborieusement, sur Steam Deck. La génération en cours n’attend donc plus la suivante pour être décortiquée : les barrières tombent pendant que les consoles sont encore en rayon.
Pour le joueur, rien d’utilisable à court terme : pas de catalogue, pas de stabilité, pas de promesse. Côté constructeurs, en revanche, l’exclusivité, argument commercial numéro un de cette génération, repose sur des murs que des bénévoles s’amusent désormais à escalader en public.

articles.title: Pokémon 30e anniversaire : les scalpers furieux, les cartes rares deviennent enfin plus accessibles
articles.text:
Les scalpeurs ont pris l'habitude de faire de beaux bénéfices avec la franchise Pokemon. Ce n'est pas le cas avec les 30 ans de la marque, ce qui a tendance à les contrarier.
Ces dernières années, les amoureux de Pokemon doivent faire face à un nouveau type d'intermédiaire : les « scalpers ». Ces derniers sont des particuliers qui essayent d'acheter le plus massivement possible les nouveaux produits de la franchise, et, en créant une pénurie artificielle, de se mettre dans la position de les revendre à un prix plus élevé. Mais la société Pokemon a peut-être trouvé une arme efficace contre ces derniers !
Un « taux de drop » exceptionnellement élevé pour les 30 ans de Pokemon
Le 16 septembre dernier, c'était la première vague des sorties spéciales pour les 30 ans de Pokemon. De quoi créer une folie sur le net, avec des gens prêts le premier jour à payer un produit deux, trois voire quatre fois son prix de magasin.
Mais avec les jours qui passent, on découvre que le « taux de drop », soit la probabilité d'obtenir une carte rare, a été nettement revu à la hausse par The Pokemon Company. Le prix des cartes les plus rares a ainsi suivi le mouvement, pour rapidement s'effondrer.
Les scalpeurs, qui piratent le marché pour vendre plus cher aux amoureux de la marque, se plaignent
Si l'on excepte ainsi les cartes Mew RGB, extraordinairement rares, et valorisées chacune à plusieurs milliers de dollars, presque l'ensemble des 15 cartes les plus rares sont actuellement valorisées à moins de 100 dollars l'unité. Les scalpeurs, qui ont mis énormément d'argent dans un stock dont la valeur se dévalue rapidement, se plaignent ainsi massivement sur internet - certain critiquant même The Pokemon Company de leur avoir fait un mauvais coup.
« Ça va être encore pire quand de plus en plus de gens commenceront à se débarrasser [de leur cartes]. Ça va être un véritable carnage » prédit ainsi un intervenant dans le subreddit consacré à l'investissement Pokemon. Du côté des réseaux, au contraire, beaucoup de fans célèbrent le désappointement des scalpeurs, et se moquent des messages où ces derniers se disent ruinés par le situation exceptionnelle de ces 30 ans. Alors, une bonne nouvelle pour le plus grand nombre ?

articles.title: 80 millions de dollars et un énorme changement, Eggers (Northman) va adapter Romeo et Juliette
articles.text:
Après les sorcières puritaines de The Witch, la folie maritime de The Lighthouse, la barbarie viking de The Northman, le sang frais de Nosferatu et en attendant les crocs de Werwulf, Robert Eggers s’attaque à ce que la littérature a produit de plus brutal : l’amour adolescent. Et pour s’offrir les services du cinéaste américain, Hollywood s’est livré une véritable guerre de tranchées.
A24, Sony et Warner Bros ont tous sorti le chéquier, mais c’est finalement Focus Features qui a raflé le morceau en posant près de 80 millions de dollars (environ 74 millions d’euros) sur la table. Un pactole monstre qui couvre à la fois la production et les cachets du réalisateur et des acteurs, pour ce qui sera le tout prochain film d’Eggers.
L’information a été révélée ce mardi 22 septembre 2026 par The Hollywood Reporter, qui a le premier rapporté le scoop. L’accord n’est d’ailleurs pas encore totalement bouclé : selon le magazine, Focus Features est sorti en tête des enchères, mais les contrats restent à finaliser.
Un choix créatif radical qui change tout pour Roméo et Juliette
Si le grand public s’attend à une relecture moderne ou à une énième adaptation académique, Eggers a déjà posé son énorme pavé dans la mare. Principal bouleversement par rapport aux adaptations habituelles : les acteurs joueront et s’exprimeront intégralement en vieil anglais.
Exit les tentatives de vulgarisation ou la modernisation pop des dialogues à la Baz Luhrmann (Romeo + Juliet en 1996) où les épées devenaient des pistolets. Fidèle à son obsession maladive pour la reconstitution historique, Eggers refuse de moderniser les dialogues pour les prémâcher au public contemporain.
Ce parti pris intransigeant transforme du tout au tout la proposition de casting : les agents de Los Angeles vont devoir dégoter de jeunes comédiens capables de déclamer des vers complexes dans une diction oubliée depuis des siècles, tout en conservant une intensité de jeu viscérale.
Au lieu d’un drame romantique fluide, le film s’annonce comme une plongée immersive, presque documentaire et poétique, dans la brutalité linguistique et sociale de l’Italie de la Renaissance.
La romance vue comme un pur film d’horreur
Voir le patron de l’horreur contemporaine récupérer l’histoire des Capulet et des Montaigu n’a rien d’un hasard. Décapée de son vernis à l’eau de rose, la pièce originale de Shakespeare est un concentré de violence pure : haine intergénérationnelle intestine, vendettas sanglantes dans les ruelles de Vérone, épidémie de peste en arrière-plan et trajectoire macabre de deux gamin(e)s poussés au suicide collectif par le fanatisme de leurs familles.
En imposant la langue originale brute au milieu de la violence du 16e siècle, Robert Eggers ne devrait pas nous raconter une gentille histoire de coup de foudre.

articles.title: DMI Finance secures Rs 1,455 Cr via listed NCDs to drive lending growth
articles.text:
DMI Finance secures Rs 1,455 Cr via listed NCDs to drive lending growth
DMI Finance has raised Rs 1,455 crore through an oversubscribed, secured NCD issuance to support its lending portfolio expansion and strengthen its debt capital base. The transaction saw broad participation from institutional investors and family offices.
Delhi-headquartered NBFC DMI Finance has raised Rs 1,455 crore by issuing secured, listed Non-Convertible Debentures (NCDs) on a private placement basis.
The issuance received aggregate bids of Rs 1,630 crore and saw participation from a diverse set of investors, including mutual funds, alternative investment funds (AIFs), primary dealers, corporates and family offices, according to a statement.
Morgan Stanley was consulted on the structuring of the issuance.
The NCDs are rated AA by ICRA and have a tenure ranging up to 36 months. The proceeds will be used to support the growth of DMI Finance’s lending portfolio and meet the company’s funding requirements.
“This transaction reflects the continued confidence of institutional investors in DMI Finance and our long-term growth strategy. As we scale our business, maintaining a diversified and resilient funding profile remains an important priority for us,” Shivashish Chatterjee, Co-founder & Managing Director, DMI Finance, said.
He added, “The capital raised will support our ability to meet the evolving credit needs of our customers while maintaining a disciplined approach to growth and risk management.”
The transaction is part of DMI Finance’s ongoing efforts to diversify its sources of funding and deepen its engagement with capital market investors. The company continues to access funding across banks, financial institutions and debt capital markets to support the growth of its lending business.
So far, DMI has raised a total of $734 million through seven funding rounds that include one Seed, five late-stage, and one debt rounds.

articles.title: La Broma Maestra de: Betty, La Fea usó un actor real como protagonista sin que él lo supiera y resultó un homenaje a la profesión actoral
articles.text:
Diego Caicedo, Julián Arango y Lorna Cepeda hablaron en exclusiva sobre La Broma Maestra de: Betty, La Fea de Prime Video, que está en tendencia en Google, ya que creó un concepto diferente de los protagonistas que se ven en plataformas streaming.
Convirtieron a un actor emergente en el protagonista involuntario de un montaje sin precedentes en las plataformas de streaming en latinoamericana: más de 80 personas detrás de cámaras, 30 cámaras ocultas y 14 actores expertos en improvisación trabajaron durante semanas para que Diego Caicedo creyera que participaba en un taller de actuación real.
PUBLICIDAD
El engaño que nadie vio venir: Diego Caicedo creía que era su segunda oportunidad
Diego Caicedo, actor emergente con trayectoria en teatro independiente y papeles secundarios, fue el centro de una operación de comedia en Colombia. Tras ser rechazado en un casting para Betty, La Fea: La Historia Continúa, recibió una invitación para participar en el llamado “Taller de Actores de Betty La Fea”. Lo que él interpretó como una segunda oportunidad era, en realidad, una producción diseñada con una sola función: hacerle creer que todo era real.
El elenco original de la serie, junto a 14 actores especializados en improvisación, construyó durante semanas un mundo falso alrededor de Caicedo. Cada situación (desde las incómodas hasta las absurdas) fue calculada para revelar quién era él cuando creía que nadie lo observaba. En palabras del propio actor, el proceso dejó una lección clara sobre lo que se necesita para sostenerse en esta profesión: “Sí o sí debes tener mucha disciplina y no ser orgulloso. Siento que debes tener mucha humildad para poder llegar a donde quieras, porque tienes que avanzar y para eso no puedes llegar con el ego por delante.”
PUBLICIDAD
Lorna Cepeda recuerda el embarazo que la alejó de un protagónico y cómo Betty, La Fea cambió su historia
En la entrevista exclusiva con Infobae, la actriz Lorna Cepeda, conectó la premisa de la serie con su propia experiencia al inicio de su carrera. En 1996, quedó seleccionada para un papel protagónico en La Viuda de Blanco, una de las producciones más importantes de la televisión colombiana de esa época. Un embarazo inesperado la obligó a renunciar al proyecto.
“Me sentí un poquito triste porque dije: ‘No puede ser, no fue el momento. ¿Hasta cuándo en la vida?’”, recordó. Sin embargo, tres años después llegó Betty, La Fea y con ella, uno de los capítulos más relevantes de su carrera. “Hay que confiar mucho. Eso te pasa en la vida: un montón de cosas, un montón de nos. Ni siquiera esos no hay que tomárselos personal”, afirmó la actriz, quien ve en La Broma Maestra un retrato fiel de lo que enfrenta cualquier actor en sus comienzos.
PUBLICIDAD
Julián Arango también fue el blanco de una broma en sus inicios: lo enviaron a buscar “el cajón de los suspiros”
Julián Arango, uno de los actores más reconocidos del elenco original de Betty, La Fea, reveló que él tampoco escapó a las bromas de set al inicio de su carrera. En sus primeros días en una producción televisiva, alguien lo envió a buscar por todo el estudio un inexistente “cajón de los suspiros”. Técnicos de luces, vestuario y producción lo pasaron de un departamento al otro hasta que el estudio entero estalló de risa.
“Todo el mundo muerto de la risa”, relató Arango entre carcajadas durante la entrevista. Cuando Infobae le preguntó cuándo se dio cuenta de que el cajón no existía, respondió: Cuando todos estallaron de la risa y lo señalaron así como: ‘¡Ja, ja, ja! Perdedor’.
PUBLICIDAD
La improvisación, el motor detrás de la serie: Colombia tiene un movimiento que Prime Video puso en el mapa
Uno de los ejes centrales de la conversación fue el rol de la improvisación en la formación actoral colombiana. La Broma Maestra de: Betty, La Fea se apoya íntegramente en actores especializados en esta disciplina y eso, según los protagonistas, no es casual: hay un movimiento de impro consolidado en Colombia que la producción visibiliza a escala global.
Para Arango, la serie es una demostración concreta de lo que puede lograr un actor entrenado en improvisación. “Ellos son expertos en improvisación y eso ahí lo demuestran en el set. Son tan buenos improvisadores que logran crear un producto tan bueno como este y engañar a alguien de esta manera”, señaló el actor, quien durante la grabación fue uno de los cómplices del montaje. Paz, por su parte, sostuvo que ningún actor puede prescindir de esa habilidad: “Un actor que no hace impro la tiene complicada, porque de eso se trata, sobre todo cuando uno hace teatro”.
PUBLICIDAD
Caicedo tomó la misma línea y amplió el alcance del argumento: “El impro siempre ha estado. Lo que pasa es que ahora se le da mucha más importancia. Tener a catorce pelados (jóvenes) improvisadores quiere decir que hay un movimiento grande y creo que esto va a ser muy importante para el impro en Colombia y en Latinoamérica”.
Los tres actores coinciden: detrás de un actor hay un trabajo que las redes sociales no muestran
El cierre de la entrevista derivó hacia un debate sobre la profesión actoral frente a la cultura de los seguidores y los likes. Los tres actores coincidieron en que La Broma Maestra funciona también como reivindicación del trabajo invisible que sostiene una carrera.
PUBLICIDAD
Ella fue directa al señalar el peso emocional que implica la formación actoral: “Detrás de un actor hay un proceso. No sé con qué lo equiparo de pronto con la medicina, que vienen cosas nuevas y los doctores siempre están actualizándose. Hay un trabajo enorme y también, un trabajo emocional bastante importante, porque eso juega mucho con tu forma de ser, con tus emociones y con tu ego”.
Caicedo, quien pasó de ser la víctima del engaño a protagonista de una producción global, cerró con una lectura que sintetiza el espíritu de la serie: “Me parece que La Broma Maestra es un homenaje a esta bella profesión. Creo que es muy chévere para el público que tenga la oportunidad de ver qué hay detrás de un actor, que es mucho más de lo que creen. La actuación tiene algo muy especial: la humanidad, las emociones. Es muy bonita esta profesión”.
PUBLICIDAD
Arango, por su parte, marcó la diferencia entre el arte de actuar y el oficio de crear contenido para redes: “La carrera actoral, el arte de ser actor, tiene un trabajo muy diferente al tema de crear algo en redes sociales. Esa formación tiene que tener un reconocimiento, así no tengan la mayor cantidad de cosas en redes, sino que cuando tú te pares a hacer el casting, el director sepa que eres capaz de hacer lo que él espera”.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Activision says the Call of Duty cheat economy is now a $8.5 billion industry
articles.text:
In context: Ahead of the much-awaited Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launch on October 22, Activision has published a detailed report on how the global video game cheat economy has evolved into a multi-billion-dollar business spanning subscription services, cheat reskins, illicit accounts, and spoofing hardware, supported by an organized network of hackers, resellers, and distributors.
The company also cited a recent study by threat intelligence firm Intorqa, which claims the cheat economy generates between $5.1 billion and $13.8 billion every year, with the median estimate being around $8.5 billion. The study claims that the cheat economy is made up of two revenue streams: subscription software and a wide network of supporting tools and services.
According to the research data, cheat subscriptions for just 15 popular titles generate around $3.5 billion per year, while account trading, boosting services, hardware ID spoofers, and other tools that are largely sold through organized distributor networks account for at least another $5 billion.
As part of its anti-cheat operations in collaboration with federal and local law enforcement agencies, Activision has reportedly disrupted 375 reseller operations, issued more than 80 cease-and-desist notices, and shut down 31 primary cheat vendors.
The company also recently released a video showing bodycam footage of an alleged Call of Duty cheat maker being served a cease-and-desist order at their Ohio residence.
 – Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) August 28, 2026
Due to the complexity, time, and cost involved in detecting and eliminating cheating in online multiplayer games, Activision says that its Ricochet Anti-Cheat technology does not try to catch one cheater at a time. Instead, it combines "detection, account security, TPM 2.0 enforcement, deep investigations, and legal action" to combat the cheating ecosystem.
The company added that it has adopted a multi-layered approach to counter cheating, whereby each layer targets one of the three pillars of the market: software- and hardware-based cheats, replacement accounts, and evasion tools such as spoofers. Activision is also working with law enforcement to dismantle distribution networks and catch the people operating them.
Explaining the scale and scope of the modern cheating economy, Activision noted that cheating tools include aimbots, wallhacks, rage cheats, unlock tools, DMA-based cheating hardware, and external devices designed to manipulate gameplay, such as Cronus, XIM, and Titan.
Account theft has also become big business, with one out of three gamers reporting that their accounts were hacked within the last two years. According to Activision, the ongoing bans on cheating accounts have created a massive demand for stolen accounts, aged accounts, Ranked Play-ready accounts, and boosting services.
Hardware-based spoofers, evasion tools, and related services are also being sold as part of a thriving online ecosystem helping cheaters evade bans. Activision says it is using "behavioral and technical detections" to thwart spoofers, adding that it issued more than 70,000 new hardware bans in August as part of its ongoing fight against this practice.

articles.title: Google's robotics unit Intrinsic open-sources its foundational infrastructure for intelligent robots - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google’s robotics unit Intrinsic open-sources its foundational infrastructure for intelligent robots
Intrinsic, the intelligent robotics software company owned by Google LLC’s parent Alphabet Inc., said today that it’s open-sourcing the core components of its industrial robotics platform.
Announced at ROSCon 2026 in Toronto today, the new offering is called Intrinsic Core, and its release under a permissive Apache 2.0 license is all about democratizing access to intelligent robotics, the company said. Founded in 2021, Intrinsic was incorporated into Google’s operations in February to accelerate the development of physical AI to push the envelope of artificial intelligence beyond digital applications and into real-world industrial environments.
Physical AI describes AI systems that use sensors, actuators, and control systems to perceive, reason, act and learn in real-world environments. It differs from pure software because it bridges the gap between bits and atoms – allowing autonomous machines such as robots, self-driving cars, drones and smart infrastructure to take action.
Though physical AI is interesting, its progress has long been stalled by the complexity of developing the underlying software and training the AI models that sit at the heart of intelligent robots. Google and Intrinsic both believe that progress can be accelerated with the availability of a reusable, foundational software layer that provides the basic infrastructure for physical AI, so that developers don’t have to rebuild everything from scratch for each new robot they create.
This is where Intrinsic Core should come in handy. It’s a preconfigured, Robot Operating System-compatible software environment designed to run on local hardware. It provides a number of reusable building blocks that developers can integrate with their physical robotics systems, providing them with the capabilities they need to operate in industrial environments.
These building blocks include Intrinsic Control, which is a hardware-agnostic real-time control framework capable of dynamically adapting a robot’s trajectory mid-movement, based on the feedback provided by its sensors. This will make it easier for developers to use various kinds of hardware, such as arms and grippers, without rewriting the underlying software and drivers for them each time, Intrinsic said.
Other components include Pose Estimation, a capability based on Nvidia Corp.’s FoundationPose that enables robots to dynamically detect and handle parts, removing the need for rigid, expensive physical fixtures. There’s also a motion planning capability that automates collision-avoidance path generation, eliminating the need for developers to program robots manually, joint by joint in a position-controlled way. And there’s a grasp planning function that allows various types of robotic grippers to automatically and dynamically adapt to the location and orientation of the objects they’re trying to grasp.
Intrinsic Core also provides simulation and calibration services that make it possible to simulate, visualize and troubleshoot robotics and calibrate their vision systems through a single interface. Finally, there are Intrinsic-ROS drivers, which make it easier for developers to integrate sensors with third-party grippers, 3D cameras and other hardware components.
To showcase how Intrinsic Core can aid robotics developers, the company has also released the Open Machine Tending Solution, which is a kind of open reference design for AI-powered CNC machine tending tasks. It supports modular customization for different hardware setups from major robotics manufacturers, including Universal Robots A/S and FANUC Corp.
Intrinsic said the Open Machine Tending Solution is designed to help accelerate automation in the machine building industry. The company said the U.S. and Europe are home to tens of thousands of shops that fabricate intricate parts for machines in a wide range of industries, yet only 8% of those shops use any form of automation at all due to the high costs and technical barriers of adoption. By providing a customizable starting point, Intrinsic believes, its reference design will pave the way for much smaller fabricators to automate lower-value tasks and accelerate automation.
More broadly, Intrinsic said it hopes to foster the growth of a much broader robotics developer ecosystem based on shared, open-source tools and accelerate the adoption of physical AI in various industries.

articles.title: Medo da IA no Brasil supera média global, diz pesquisa • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Medo da IA no Brasil supera média global, diz pesquisa
Pesquisa aponta 52% da população receosa com o futuro da tecnologia, mas um quarto da população nunca nem ouviu falar.
O futuro da inteligência artificial vem tirando o sono de mais da metade dos brasileiros. Pelo menos é o que aponta a pesquisa mais recente sobre o tema feita pela Pew Research Center. Os dados mostram um aumento na média global de pessoas preocupadas com os avanços da IA: em todo o mundo, 37% declararam ter mais receio que expectativa com a tecnologia. No Brasil, esse número sobe para 52%.
O medo dos mais jovens em relação à IA também vem numa crescente em países como Estados Unidos, Austrália, Japão e Brasil. Por aqui, já são 12% a mais de pessoas entre 18 e 34 anos levando preocupações com a IA em conta desde 2025. Mas, considerando um recorte global, a maior parte dos entrevistados (48%) nessa faixa etária vê a IA com certo equilíbrio.
Outro dado interessante é sobre as preocupações que relacionam IA à desigualdade social. Para 28% dos entrevistados, a tecnologia vai aumentar a diferença entre ricos e pobres. Aqui no Brasil, a maioria (30%) não vê dessa forma, enquanto 24% das pessoas acreditam que sim. A pesquisa foi realizada em 37 países de diferentes continentes entre março e junho.
Segundo os dados da Pew Research Center, o Brasil fica abaixo apenas de Austrália e Estados Unidos quando o assunto é preocupação com inteligência artificial. Além disso, é o país com menor percentual de pessoas animadas com o tema (8%), contrastando com os 52% que veem o assunto com receio.
Chama atenção também o fato de a preocupação ser mais comum entre pessoas acima dos 50 anos aqui no Brasil (58%), enquanto os jovens representam 44% desse recorte. Vale reforçar aqui que o Brasil está entre os seis países que registraram um aumento desse receio na faixa etária de 18 a 34 anos, saindo de 32% em 2025.
O impacto da inteligência artificial no mercado de trabalho é uma das principais preocupações atuais, sobretudo entre os jovens. Nos Estados Unidos, por exemplo, 74% das pessoas entre 18 e 34 anos acreditam em uma oferta menor de empregos relacionada ao crescimento da IA.
Vale lembrar que em maio deste ano algumas formaturas nos EUA tiveram vaias para executivos do mercado de tecnologia. Além disso, no último mês, uma pesquisa da CNBC junto ao Generation Labs apontou mais de 70% de desconfiança dos jovens em líderes da IA.
Aqui no Brasil, o percentual de pessoas preocupadas com os impactos da IA no mercado de trabalho chega a 42% em todas as faixas analisadas. Mas também há quem acredite num aumento de oportunidades com a tecnologia: 13% veem desta forma. Os países com maior índice de receio no tema são Austrália e Coreia do Sul, ambos om 76%, enquanto os EUA vêm logo atrás, com 71%.
Essa talvez seja a informação mais curiosa do levantamento feito pela Pew Research Center. Segundo os dados da pesquisa, são 27% dos brasileiros que afirmam nunca terem ouvido falar de IA. A maioria (42%) diz conhecer pouco do assunto, enquanto 31% dizem saber bastante sobre o tema. Nossos vizinhos da Argentina também têm um bom número de pessoas alheias à IA, com 30%.
Em relação à pesquisa feita em 2025, mais pessoas já ouviram falar ou leram sobre IA por aqui. O Brasil está entre os países em que esse percentual mais cresceu, subindo de 22% para os 31% registrados em 2026. Segundo os dados do estudo, o conhecimento sobre inteligência artificial é maior entre os países mais ricos – o que estaria relacionado à maior facilidade de acesso.

articles.title: Dacia et Renault électriques à prix cassé : les nouvelles batteries chinoises débarquent en Europe
articles.text:
CATL a annoncé ce mardi 22 septembre 2026, via un post sur LinkedIn, le lancement de la production d’essai sur son site de Debrecen, en Hongrie. Le fabricant chinois de batteries présente cette étape comme le signe que l’ensemble des préconditions réglementaires ont été remplies.
Dans les faits, seules les deux premières lignes de production de cellules sont pour l’instant activées, et uniquement à des fins de calibrage : il s’agit de régler les équipements et de valider les procédés avant d’envisager une production en série.
Le chiffre de 100 GWh, régulièrement mis en avant, correspond à la capacité totale visée une fois l’ensemble du site achevé. Pour l’heure, cette première phase plafonne à 34 GWh.
Derrière ces gigawattheures, il y a surtout un chèque colossal : environ 7,34 milliards d’euros engagés par CATL depuis l’annonce du projet, en 2022. C’est tout simplement le plus gros investissement industriel de l’histoire de la Hongrie, ce qui explique pourquoi Budapest a autant misé sur l’accueil des batteries chinoises… et pourquoi le moindre grain de sable prend une telle ampleur.
Un dossier sanitaire qui a pesé sur le calendrier
Ce démarrage intervient après plusieurs mois de blocage. Le bureau gouvernemental du comté de Hajdú-Bihar (là où se situe l’usine donc) avait ordonné la suspension temporaire de certaines zones de l’usine, invoquant « des risques d’exposition au nickel ayant touché 9 salariés ». CATL affirme avoir depuis mis en œuvre des mesures correctives, et les autorités locales ont validé la levée des réserves après plusieurs inspections successives.
Le contexte reste néanmoins assez trouble. Une amende d’environ 31 000 dollars (environ 27 000 euros) avait été infligée à l’entreprise pour des manquements assez mineurs sur le papier (une porte non verrouillée, une signalétique en chinois plutôt qu’en hongrois) alors que ce type d’écart donne d’ordinaire lieu à des sanctions symboliques, de l’ordre de 1 000 dollars (environ 870 euros).
Pour plusieurs médias, dont Caixin, ces contrôles tiennent davantage du signal politique que du dossier de sécurité, dans un pays où l’arrivée au pouvoir de Péter Magyar, en mai 2026, a rebattu les cartes pour les investisseurs chinois. Difficile, dans tous les cas, de ne pas y voir un moyen de retarder la production de CATL pour laisser du champ à la filière européenne. Sauf que le retard accumulé par l’Europe est tel qu’un décalage de quelques mois de l’usine hongroise n’y changera pas grand-chose.
Rappelons que Debrecen n’est pas un site neuf : l’assemblage de modules de batteries y est opérationnel depuis l’automne 2024, avec 537 000 unités produites à ce jour. La partie cellules, elle, démarre donc avec un temps de retard sur le calendrier industriel initial du groupe, sans que CATL ne communique de date précise pour le passage en production de série.
CATL n’est d’ailleurs pas un cas isolé. À Szeged, à l’autre bout du pays, BYD suit une trajectoire très proche : le constructeur chinois a lancé sa production pilote de voitures électriques le 30 avril 2026 et vise un vrai démarrage au quatrième trimestre 2026, avec là aussi plusieurs mois de décalage sur le plan initial. L’implantation industrielle chinoise en Hongrie avance, donc, mais rarement au rythme annoncé.
Quel intérêt pour les constructeurs et les automobilistes français ?
Sur le papier, ce site doit alimenter plusieurs constructeurs européens implantés en Hongrie. Des modèles comme la Renault Twingo électrique ou la Dacia Spring, tous deux positionnés sur des segments très sensibles au prix, pourraient bénéficier d’une bonification liée au score environnemental français, qui favorise les cellules assemblées en Union européenne.
Reste que cet avantage ne concernera, dans un premier temps, qu’une fraction limitée de la production (celle correspondant aux 34 GWh en cours de calibrage) et non les 100 GWh promis à terme. Selon nos informations, Renault s’est déjà positionné pour être parmi les premiers clients de cette usine, permettant à la Twingo de rapidement bénéficier d’un pack batterie fabriqué en Europe.
Renault a tout intérêt à proposer une batterie européenne pour sa Twingo E-Tech : cela lui permettrait de bénéficier du « coup de pouce CEE » (le dispositif qui a remplacé le bonus écologique, dont la bonification réservée aux véhicules à batterie européenne s’applique depuis octobre 2025), dont profitent déjà la R5, la Mégane et le Scénic.
Chaque marque fixe ses propres montants selon ses contrats avec les fournisseurs d’énergie, qui financent désormais le dispositif à la place de l’État ; Renault ajoute ainsi environ 1 440 euros à l’aide de base. L’aide minimale pour la Twingo passerait alors de 3 620 à 4 830 euros, et celle réservée aux ménages précaires grimperait de 5 740 à 8 240 euros, portant le prix de la citadine électrique à 11 250 euros pour les foyers les plus modestes, à grille tarifaire inchangée. La Dacia Spring passerait quant à elle sous les 10 000 euros avec cette batterie.
