articles.title: Toyota orders workers to train humanoid robots but says humans won't be replaced
articles.text:
Toyota workers are already helping to train humanoid robots as part of the automaker’s race to eventually deploy 400,000 factory robots—but a Toyota executive said the robotic push is not meant to directly replace humans.
Starting in 2028, the Toyota Motor group aims to start investing $6.42 billion every year in upgrading factories with the new robotic workforce, according to Nikkei Asia. The company wants to put 150,000 robots in its own automotive plants and deploy another 250,000 at group company facilities that produce various components and materials.
Toyota has already begun deploying some of its ELEY humanoid robots across assembly lines to learn from human workers. Nikkei Asia reported that workers are teaching the robots, which roll around on wheels, to perform tasks requiring precise hand movements by wearing “jigs” based on the humanoids’ fingers.
That naturally raises questions about the future of the Japan-based automaker’s human workforce, which has 18,000 veteran workers across 60 factories worldwide, including 11 US manufacturing plants. But Hiroki Nakajima, a Toyota executive vice president, told Nikkei Asia that the company aims for “a world where robots coexist with humans, rather than replacing them.”
It’s unclear how many robots Toyota has already deployed overall or how many of the new robots will be humanoids. But the automotive industry has been a leading adopter of industrial robots for decades, with such robots typically being robotic arms installed at workstations and mobile robots that move components or materials around.
China alone deployed 2 million industrial robots in 2024, with Japan coming in second at 450,500 robots, according to the International Federation of Robotics. The United States and South Korea ranked third and fourth with 34,200 robots and 30,600 robots, respectively.

articles.title: Beats Unveils Beats 360, Its First Customizable Over-Ear Headphone
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 22nd 2026
	
	
	
	
Beats Unveils Beats 360, Its First Customizable Over-Ear Headphone
Beats today unveils Beats 360, an all-new flagship over-ear headphone that introduces the brand's most personal listening experience yet. For the first time from Beats, interchangeable ear cushions and headband cushions let users customize their headphones with different colors and cushion types to match their style, activity, or mood.

Flagship Sound, Engineered for Everything

Beats 360 is the first over-ear Beats headphone with sweat and water resistance with an IPX4 rating. UltraPlush cushion kits are also available in Black and Cloud. Whether kept minimal or styled boldly, Beats 360 becomes a distinctive personal statement.
Seamless Connectivity Across Apple and Android Platforms
Beats 360 is powered by a custom Beats chip for seamless integration across both Apple and Android ecosystems, and features industry-leading Class 1 Bluetooth 5.3 for extended connectivity range.
Apple users get one-touch pairing, always-on Hey Siri, Automatic Switching between devices, Audio Sharing, FaceTime with Spatial Audio, Personalized Spatial Audio with dynamic head tracking, and Find My with network location support. Easy-to-use controls are positioned intuitively on the back of each earcup. The right earcup features a tactile volume rocker and a play/pause button for music playback and calls, while the left earcup has a power button and a dedicated listening mode button.

During calls, a dedicated beam-forming voice microphone works alongside feed-forward mics to focus on the user's voice and help reduce environmental noise, while the system dynamically leverages additional microphones when they provide a stronger signal, optimizing call clarity in real time.
Power That Lasts All Day
Beats 360 delivers up to 32 hours of battery life with Adaptive EQ when ANC and Transparency mode are off, and up to 32 hours with ANC and Personalized Spatial Audio on. Thanks to Fast Fuel, a five-minute charge provides up to 1 hour of playback via USB-C charging.

This marks the highest amount of recycled plastic ever used in a Beats product. Additionally, Beats 360 utilizes 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets and meets U.S. Department of Energy requirements for battery charger systems. articles.title: Glorious GMMK Eternal Review: Fits anywhere, sounds great
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The GMMK Eternal isn't the most exciting keyboard, but it sounds good and takes up very little space.
Pros
- +Compact size that's not overly cramped
- +Excellent sound-damping
- +$100
Cons
- -OEM profile keycaps
- -Generic-looking
- -ABS keycaps in OEM profile
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Something, something, going back to your roots. I guess that's what Glorious is doing (or, thinks it's doing) with the GMMK Eternal — its new wired mechanical gaming keyboard.
The GMMK Eternal is, at a glance, pretty basic: it's wired, it has regular mechanical (not magnetic) switches and a standard 1,000 Hz polling rate. It comes with bright backlighting, double-shot ABS keycaps, and some gamer-friendly features such as multiple onboard profiles and macro-recording via Glorious Core. It also has a hot-swappable PCB and three layers of sound-dampening material in the case — it's not supposed to be a revolution, but it is a pretty solid option if you're looking for something compact and relatively budget-friendly. The GMMK Eternal is available now in black, with GMMK's Fox MX linear switches, for $99.99.
Design and Construction of the GMMK Eternal
The GMMK Eternal is a wired mechanical gaming keyboard with a compact 96-percent layout — it has a full function row, arrow keys, and a 10-key numberpad, but everything is squashed together (and it ditches most of the navigation keys), so it takes up significantly less space than a full-size keyboard but has almost as many keys. It sports a fairly simple, minimalist overall design — edge-to-edge keys with virtually no bezel, black anodized aluminum top plate over a black ABS plastic bottom case, and no obvious branding on the top or sides.
The keyboard measures approximately 14.6 inches (372mm) wide by 4.8 inches (122mm) deep, and is 1.7 inches (44mm) thick at its thickest point (including the keycaps). That's significantly smaller than a full-size keyboard, and is even small by 96-percent keyboard standards — perhaps my favorite 96-percent keyboard, the Asus ROG Strix Scope II 96 Wireless, is slightly larger than the GMMK Eternal at 14.84 x 5.16 inches (377 x 131mm), though at 1.57 inches (40mm) thick, it's slightly lower-profile. This is because the GMMK Eternal has double-shot ABS keycaps with shine-through legends in an OEM profile (the ROG Strix Scope II 96 Wireless comes with keycaps in a mid-height profile that's very close to the Cherry profile).
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
While the GMMK Eternal is pretty compact, even by 96-percent keyboard standards, you won't feel too cramped for space. There's enough room to leave some separation between the alphanumeric keys and the arrow keys (though not much), and there's enough room in the top row that the Function keys are grouped into visibly distinct groups of four. There are five navigation keys next to the Function row and above the numberpad: PrintScreen, Delete, Insert, Page Up, and Page Down. So you really shouldn't miss too much about your full-size board once you get used to the numberpad being right on top of you.
The GMMK Eternal has some weight to it, but it's not too hefty: it weighs in at just under two pounds (1.94 lbs / 879 g), which is about what we'd expect for a board of this size and construction. For comparison, the wired Corsair Vanguard Pro 96 weighs about 2.2 pounds (998g), while the wireless Asus ROG Strix Morph 96 Wireless weighs just under 2.5 pounds (2.48 lbs / 1,125 g). The GMMK Eternal is heavy enough that it shouldn't move around on your desk too much during heavy gaming sessions, but it's not so heavy that it would be difficult to travel with.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The bottom of the keyboard is where you'll finally see Glorious' branding. The Glorious name is stamped across the back, debossed with a shiny finish. There are also a couple strips of anti-slip rubber, as well as two sets of plastic flip-out feet for adjusting the keyboard's angle. The GMMK Eternal is a wired keyboard, and it has one USB-C port in the center of the board.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The GMMK Eternal comes with just two accessories in the box: a 6-foot (1.8m) rubber-coated USB-C to USB-A cable and a 2-in-1 combination keycap and switch puller.
Specs
| Size | 96% | 
| Number of keys | 99 | 
| Switches | Glorious Fox Switches | 
| Backlighting | Yes | 
| Onboard Storage | Yes (3 profiles) | 
| Dedicated Media Keys | No | 
| Game Mode | Yes / No | 
| Additional Ports | 0 | 
| Connectivity | Wired (USB-C) | 
| Cable | 6ft. / 1.8m USB-C to USB-A | 
| Keycaps | double-shot ABS | 
| Construction | Anodized aluminum top plate ABS bottom case | 
| Software | Glorious Core | 
| Dimensions (LxWxH) | 14.6 x 4.8 x 1.7" / 372 x 122 x 44mm | 
| Weight | 1.94lbs / 879g | 
| MSRP / Price at Time of Review | $99.99 | 
| Release Date | Sept. 8, 2026 | 
Typing and Gaming Experience on the GMMK Eternal
The GMMK Eternal is a mechanical gaming keyboard with a hot-swappable PCB that takes both 3- and 5-pin switches. It comes pre-built with Glorious' Fox switches, which are pre-lubed linear switches with an actuation force of 55g — a little heavier than your average linear switch, but I kind of liked the extra force. The switches are otherwise typical linear switches, with smooth, stable keypresses that have no tactile bump or audible click. They're rated for 50 million clicks.
The keyboard features three layers of sound-dampening material in the case: a molded silicone layer and two layers of PU foam around the PCB, for a "deeper, more satisfying thock." And I'll admit that I was pretty impressed with how the GMMK Eternal sounded out of the box — especially for a sub-$100 keyboard from a mainstream gaming company. There was a small amount of rattle as I typed, but the case, at least, was solid and ping-less, and bottoming out did give a deeper sound (if not quite a "thock").
The GMMK Eternal comes with double-shot ABS keycaps in an OEM profile, which is the standard, medium-height profile you'll find on most mainstream gaming keyboards. The keycaps have lightly cupped, textured tops with shine-through legends and secondary legends printed on the sides in white. While I usually prefer lower-profile keycaps, I didn't mind these — the keyboard is fairly compact and low-profile to begin with, so I didn't find the standard height OEM profile to be uncomfortable (nor did I feel like I needed a wrist rest).
The GMMK Eternal is a solid option for both typing and gaming — I didn't have any issues with accuracy, speed, or response time in my testing, minus the normal learning curve of getting used to having the arrow keys right on top of the alphanumeric keys.
Features and Software of the GMMK Eternal
The GMMK Eternal is configurable with Glorious' universal peripheral software, Glorious Core, which I don't have any real problems with, save for the fact that it requires a restart upon install. The keyboard has onboard storage, and you can set up up to three profiles in Glorious Core to save directly to the hardware.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
You can use Glorious Core to adjust the keyboard's settings, including polling rate, input latency, and lighting standby timer, as well as switching between Windows and Mac modes. This isn't a magnetic switch keyboard, so there's not much else to set up in terms of performance. You can also remap keys — up to two layers deep, and the software has a built-in macro recorder and manager.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
You can also customize the keyboard's lighting, which looks great — the board features bright RGB backlighting with a north-facing PCB, and the board's otherwise boring design really lets the lighting shine. There are 17 different lighting presets in Glorious Core, and you can also customize the lighting for each key individually (if you want).
The Bottom Line
The Glorious GMMK Eternal isn't the most exciting keyboard on the market, especially not for gaming. It's a wired keyboard with mechanical switches and a standard 1,000 Hz polling rate, so it's not trying to be the fastest, lowest-latency, RapidTrigger-enabled keyboard that will launch you into a pro-eSports career. Instead, it's a simple, compact keyboard that offers a very solid typing and gaming experience with hot-swappable switches and pretty RGB lighting for the relatively budget-friendly price of $100. While you can definitely find keyboards for less than $100, you probably won't find one that sounds and feels better than the GMMK Eternal.
Sarah Jacobsson Purewal is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware covering peripherals, software, and custom builds. You can find more of her work in PCWorld, Macworld, TechHive, CNET, Gizmodo, Tom's Guide, PC Gamer, Men's Health, Men's Fitness, SHAPE, Cosmopolitan, and just about everywhere else.

articles.title: Chinese EV maker Geely promises a 4-minute EV charge with its ridiculous new 2.2MW charger — looks like BYD has competition when it comes to speed
articles.text:
A full EV charging session in 4 minutes? There's a new challenger to BYD in the MegaWatt charging game
Monster 2.2MW charging speeds promised by Chinese brand Geely
- Geely plans to unveil new charging technology this week
- The system will draw 2.2 MegaWatts of power during use
- Charging sessions could take as little as four minutes
The Geely Group has taken to Chinese social media site Weibo to tease its next generation of charging technology, which the company says can fill batteries in around four minutes.
The news arrives along with details of a new Geely Galaxy E5, an all-electric premium SUV that is due for launch in China this year and is reportedly the first model that will able to use this new, ultra-fast charging technology.
Delivering a staggering peak power of 2.2MW, the next-generation "AI-powered" charging system is claimed to be able to deliver a full charging session in four minutes.
However, there’s no mention of whether that’s the standard 10-80% state of charge or something else entirely.
According to China EV Home, the Galaxy E5 uses an 800V architecture and Geely’s next-generation Aegis Short Blade battery, which will be available in 61.52kWh and 70.01kWh capacities.
The batteries offer CLTC-rated ranges of 550 km (around 341 miles) and 635 km (395 miles) respectively, but it is the ultra-fast charging that will likely hog the headlines.
While there are very few details (Geely will hold an event imminently to unveil more), the AI involvement is reportedly to do with thermal control, which allows such a mammoth rate of charge without damaging battery cells.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Geely says its packs can last 3,500 charge-discharge cycles "with limited degradation”.
Analysis: China continues to push speed
The EV dream has always been to recharge in the sort of time it takes to refuel a petrol or diesel counterpart, as this would arguably break down one of the biggest barriers to ownership: range anxiety.
Those with little experience of electric vehicles worry about becoming stranded when batteries run out of charge, only to be faced with an hour or more wait to get back on the road.
However, most people that have owned a modern EV will likely argue that this isn’t really the case any more, but China continues to develop charging technology that prioritizes speed an convenience.
BYD has demonstrated its 1.5MW Flash chargers both in China and in Europe, where they are capable of brimming batteries in under 10 minutes.
Unfortunately, the only vehicles compatible with the tech (in Europe at least) happen to be some of the most expensive in the BYD stable.
Zeekr has also been pushing its own 1.2MW chargers in China, which are also capable of lighting-fast top-up times.
While it’s easy to see this as simple one-upmanship, China’s charging infrastructure needs to grow at a rapid rate to serve the more than 110 million EVs predicted to be on the roads by 2030.
This will mean installing more than 40 million charging points and approximately 300,000 high-power charging facilities to deal with the demand.
Having this mix of high and lower powered charging is the only way to meet all the needs of drivers, where high power and speed is essential in places like motorway service stations along busy travel corridors, while cheaper, lower-powered options benefit those charging curbside over night, for example.
Unlike many other nations, which have been comparatively slow to adopt electrification and the surrounding infrastructure, China appears to be exploring all avenues.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Leon has been navigating a world where automotive and tech collide for almost 20 years, reporting on everything from in-car entertainment to robotised manufacturing plants. Currently, EVs are the focus of his attentions, but give it a few years and it will be electric vertical take-off and landing craft. Outside of work hours, he can be found tinkering with distinctly analogue motorcycles, because electric motors are no replacement for an old Honda inline four.

articles.title: ANC für unter 100 Euro: Diese In-Ears schlagen die neuen Airpods 5 im Preisvergleich
articles.text:
Die Airpods 5 sind da: Drei Alternativen die günstiger sind – und noch mehr können
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Apple hat kürzlich die neue Generation seiner In-Ear-Kopfhörer vorgestellt. Die Airpods 5 sind in zwei Versionen erhältlich. Laut Apple wurde bei beiden die ANC-Funktion deutlich verbessert. Adaptive Audio soll automatisch zwischen ANC und Transparenzmodus wechseln, was zum Beispiel bei einer wichtigen Durchsage am Bahnhof nützlich sein kann. Die neue Version ist zudem mit der Siri-KI sowie Echtzeit-Übersetzungen ausgestattet. Für eine bessere Haltbarkeit sorgt ein Upgrade auf Staub- und Wasserschutz nach IP67.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Apple hat auch bei der Akkulaufzeit nachgebessert: Das Einstiegsmodell soll mit aktiviertem ANC bis zu vier Stunden durchhalten, zusammen mit dem Case sind laut Apple bis zu 22 Stunden Wiedergabezeit möglich. Beim teureren Modell gibt Apple eine Akkulaufzeit von bis zu fünf Stunden mit aktiviertem ANC an. Letzteres bietet außerdem die Möglichkeit, die Lautstärke direkt am Stiel der In-Ears zu regeln. Das Case lässt sich bei diesem Modell auch kabellos aufladen. Der Preis liegt bei 169 Euro. Das günstigere Modell, das über USB-C geladen wird, kostet 149 Euro.
Soundcore Liberty 5: Der Preis-Leistungs-Sieger von Anker
Wem das zu teuer ist, für den gibt es diverse günstigere Alternativen. Das beste Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis bieten die Soundcore Liberty 5 von Anker mit ANC-3.0-Technologie: Eine spezielle Akustikkammer erfasst und unterdrückt menschliche Stimmen effektiv, während sich ein adaptiver Algorithmus alle 0,3 Sekunden anpasst. Das ist besonders praktisch in dynamischen Umgebungen wie zum Beispiel im Zug oder im Café. Dank Wollpapier-Treibern, LDAC und Hi-Res Audio liefern die In-Ears laut Hersteller satte, ausgewogene Klangnuancen. Sechs Mikrofone und eine KI-Geräuschunterdrückung sollen auch bei Wind für klare Gespräche sorgen.
Über ein Bedienfeld am Stiel lassen sich Mikrofon, Anrufe und Lautstärke regeln. Bei Apple bietet dies nur die teurere Variante der Airpods 5. Die Soundcore Liberty 5 lassen sich per USB-C oder kabellos laden. Im Normalmodus sollen sie bis zu zwölf Stunden durchhalten, mit Case sogar bis zu 48 Stunden. Bei aktiviertem ANC sind es acht beziehungsweise 32 Stunden. Zehn Minuten Schnellladen liefern laut Hersteller weitere fünf Stunden Power. Die Kopfhörer sind in den Farben Schwarz, Weiß, Rosa und Blau erhältlich und werden mit sechs Silikon-Aufsatzgrößen für die optimale Passform geliefert. Der reguläre Preis liegt bei 99,99 Euro, aktuell ist das Modell aber schon ab 69 Euro erhältlich.
Freebuds 6i: ANC-In-Ears von Huawei für unter 60 Euro
Noch günstiger sind die Freebuds 6i von Huawei. Die intelligente dynamische ANC-3.0-Technologie soll Geräuschunterdrückungsparameter in Echtzeit modellieren. Sie überwachen Umgebungsgeräusche alle 2,6 Mikrosekunden und passen die Parameter innerhalb von etwa einer Sekunde an. Für ablenkungsfreie Telefonate sorgen drei Mikrofone, die im Verbund mit einem Deep-Neural-Network-Algorithmus Stimmen von Störgeräuschen unterscheiden und diese unterdrücken. Die 11-mm-Treiber erzeugen laut Hersteller satte Bässe.
Ohne Case halten die Freebuds 6i Herstellerangaben zufolge bis zu acht Stunden durch, mit vollständig geladenem Case sogar bis zu 35 Stunden. Schon zehn Minuten Aufladen sollen für vier weitere Stunden Wiedergabezeit reichen. Dank der IP54-Zertifizierung sind die Kopfhörer gegen Staub und Wasser geschützt und somit auch für Outdoor-Aktivitäten geeignet. Nutzer:innen können die In-Ears von Huawei zudem mit zwei Geräten gleichzeitig verbinden und sogar nahtlos zwischen iOS und Android wechseln, ohne die Verbindung neu koppeln zu müssen. Die Freebuds 6i sind in den Farben Schwarz, Weiß und Lila zum Preis von 59,99 Euro erhältlich.
Nothing Ear 3: ANC-Kopfhörer mit individuellem Sound-Profil
Eine weitere Alternative ist die dritte Generation der kabellosen Kopfhörer von Nothing Ear. Sie sind mit Adaptive Active Noise Cancellation ausgestattet und prüfen alle 600 Millisekunden die Umgebung, um die Geräuschunterdrückung in Echtzeit um bis zu 45 Dezibel anzupassen. Im Transparenzmodus können Nutzer:innen Umgebungsgeräusche wahrnehmen, ohne die In-Ears herauszunehmen. Als High-Res-zertifizierte Bluetooth-Kopfhörer mit LDAC-Technologie liefern sie laut Hersteller verlustfreien Sound. Der 12-mm-Treiber sorgt für kraftvollen Klang mit stärkeren Bässen und klareren Höhen. Ein Hörtest in der App erstellt zudem ein individuelles Sound-Profil.
Die dritte Generation der Nothing Ear lassen sich entweder per USB-C oder kabellos laden. Eine vollständige Aufladung dauert etwa 5,5 Stunden. Mit einer Akkuladung sollen die In-Ears bis zu 5,5 Stunden mit ANC oder bis zu 11 Stunden ohne ANC durchhalten. Zusammen mit dem Case sind laut Herstellerangaben bis zu 38 Stunden möglich. Dank Schnellladefunktion sollen schon zehn Minuten für bis zu zehn Stunden Wiedergabe auszeichnen. Die weichen Silikonaufsätze sollen ganztägigen Tragekomfort bieten. Zudem sind die Nothing-Ear-Kopfhörer IP54-zertifiziert. Beim Hersteller startet der Preis bei 149 Euro, bei Media Markt sind die In-Ears aber aktuell schon für 117,99 Euro zu haben.

articles.title: Motorola unveils Signature 27 first with Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme
articles.text:
Today at the Snapdragon Summit, which Qualcomm flew me out to, Motorola unveiled the first handset with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 mobile platform: the Signature 27. Firstly, we’re waiting to hear if the Signature 27 is coming to Canada, but the Motorola press release says it’s a North American release, so I wouldn’t be shocked if it shows up in the North.
Last year’s Motorola Signature wasn’t available in Canada, but we’ll keep our hopes up. Considering the jump from 2025’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 to the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, this handset is definitely getting a bump in performance compared to its predecessor. Motorola has also announced that it’s partnered with Bang & Olufsen to power the device’s sound.
The Signature 27 features a Motorola ArcticMesh cooling system, which uses a new diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal, copper mesh and a redesigned 3D vapour chamber to help with heating during sustained use.
Additionally, you’ll get a 50MP Sony Lytia 910 primary shooter and a 200MP periscope telephoto lens. And the device has Motorola’s Video Enhancement Engine, which uses AI to create a real-time intelligence layer that adjusts colour tones by analyzing the scene during and even before recording.
Of course, since it’s Motorola, the company has launched the device in two Pantone finishes: Coal Smoke, with a woven texture for better grip strength and durability. And Pantone Capulet Green with a brushed look that looks incredibly nice.
We’re waiting to learn a lot more about the Signature 27, including pricing and availability.

articles.title: Founder Summit’s agenda revealed | TechCrunch
articles.text:
On November 4, TechCrunch’s Founder Summit will bring a vital one-day crash course on startup building to Boston’s SoWa Power Station. Founders shouldn’t have to learn the hardest lessons the hardest way, and this event is designed to make the challenges of starting a company easier and the highs that much greater.
Instead of months of trial and error, you get direct access to the investors and founders who’ve already made the calls you’re now facing. We’re talking everything from fundraising and hiring to AI strategy, and topping your category.
Don’t take our word for it. Explore the full agenda of speakers and sessions we have planned for Founder Summit below, and lock in your spot at the event. All tickets are available for the lowest prices you’ll see, so now’s the best time to act.
The official TechCrunch Founder Summit agenda reveal
Without further ado, here’s the official agenda. Get to know each session and speaker on the event agenda page.
The New Rules of Raising Capital
Fundraising has never been easy, but the playbook keeps changing. Brian Devaney, partner at Underscore, will break down what investors are looking for now, how founders can stand out in a crowded market, and where founders often lose leverage without realizing it. Expect a candid look at today’s fundraising environment, from first checks to term sheets, and the mistakes that can make or break a round.
The CEO Job Never Gets Easier
The title may stay the same, but the job changes with each stage of a company’s growth. HubSpot co-founder and Sequoia partner Brian Halligan will share the lessons he’s learned from building and advising startups through rapid growth, tough decisions, and constant reinvention.
This session explores how founders can evolve as CEOs, avoid common leadership pitfalls, and build companies that can thrive well beyond the early days.
Built for AI From Day One
Adding AI features is one thing. Building an AI-native company is something else entirely. Lior Div, co-founder and CEO of 7AI, will explore what changes when AI becomes the foundation of a startup rather than a product enhancement. From team structure and product development to operations and go-to-market strategy, this session examines what founders should rethink when building in the AI era.
Not Every Dollar Is Equal
Raising capital is often framed as a milestone, but choosing the right investors can shape a company’s future long after the money arrives. After raising an $11 million round for Cogent Security, co-founder and CEO Vineet Edupuganti learned firsthand what separates helpful partners from costly distractions. This session explores how founders should evaluate investors, navigate trade-offs, and think beyond valuation when building their cap table.
How to Spot the ‘King of the Hill’ Company — Hidden Signals That Define Category Winners
Innovation is needed to solve the world’s biggest challenges, but only certain companies can realistically become category-defining winners at industrial scale. In this session, TDK Ventures investment director Tina Tosukhowong unpacks the firm’s “King of the Hill” framework: the disciplined process that the best investors use to evaluate companies based on economics, scalability, and commercial timing.
Through real-world examples, including Tina’s exploration of fission and fusion, attendees will learn actionable frameworks for evaluating startup readiness, mapping competitive landscapes, and identifying when timing, talent, and technology align.
Your Company Is Who You Hire
Early hiring decisions can define a startup’s culture, speed, and ability to execute. Melissa Taunton, partner at NEA, will share lessons from working with founders as they build teams through periods of rapid growth and uncertainty.
From identifying the right early hires to avoiding common recruiting mistakes, this session explores how founders can build organizations that are resilient, adaptable, and prepared for what comes next.
The Boston Founder Playbook
Silicon Valley gets the headlines, but Chase Garbarino has been quietly building category-defining companies from Boston for over a decade. As co-founder and CEO of HqO, he has raised $200 million from investors and scaled to 30+ countries without ever needing to change geographies.
He’ll break down the real advantages and disadvantages of building where the startup playbook wasn’t written, and what every founder outside a major hub should know.
Finding Product Market Fit Before You Scale
Every founder wants product-market fit, but knowing when you’ve actually found it is far more complicated. Kent Bennett, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, will unpack how founders can validate demand, build an MVP that answers the right questions, and avoid scaling before the fundamentals are in place.
This session explores the signals that matter, the metrics that mislead, and the decisions that separate enduring companies from expensive experiments.
What happens beyond Founder Summit’s sessions
The programming is a huge part of TechCrunch Founder Summit’s value, but it’s not the whole deal. You’ll also get the chance to mix and mingle with founders working through the same fundraising decisions and the same hiring calls as you, and then network with those who have already lived through those experiences. Or better yet … those who have funded those who have gone through the startup wringer.
A day filled with discussions turns into months of action at TechCrunch Founder Summit, and we’re eager for you to join us and the rest of the Boston startup community on November 4. Register now to secure your ticket savings and join the ultimate founder’s bootcamp.

articles.title: Les « conséquences sociales majeures » du rachat de SFR : Bouygues, Orange et Free traînés en justice
articles.text:
Le Comité social et économique (CSE) de SFR, soit les représentants du personnel de l’opérateur au carré rouge, attaque en justice Bouygues, Orange et le groupe Iliad (Free), comme le rapporte L’Informé. Cette action s’inscrit dans le cadre du rachat de SFR, conclu en juin dernier, et porte sur le sort des employés de SFR.
Les représentants du personnel de SFR s’attaquent à Bouygues, Orange et Iliad
Pour rappel, le consortium Bouygues, Orange et Iliad assure qu’il garantira l’emploi des 8 000 salariés de SFR jusqu’en 2029. Bouygues Telecom, qui récupérera les activités liées aux entreprises, doit reprendre 2 300 salariés. Orange, de son côté, accueillera entre 250 et 300 employés, tandis que Free, qui héritera de la marque RED by SFR, n’en reprendra que 54. Au total, moins de 3 000 des quelque 8 000 salariés actuellement employés par SFR conserveront donc un emploi après 2029. Plus de 5 000 personnes restent ainsi dans l’incertitude quant à leur avenir professionnel.
C’est précisément sur ce point que porte l’action menée en justice par le CSE. Cette dernière reproche au consortium un manque de transparence sur le découpage de SFR et de laisser ainsi plus de 5 000 employés dans l’incertitude. Le CSE demande par ailleurs un accès à plusieurs documents et informations concernant la vente de SFR, tout en exigeant une pénalité de 10 000 euros par jour si cette demande n’est pas respectée. De son côté, la direction d’Altice France a assuré avoir transmis aux syndicats « l’information la plus complète, c’est-à-dire celle disponible et dans le respect des principes élémentaires du droit de la concurrence ».
Les craintes grandissent et les actions se multiplient
Toujours selon L’Informé, les représentants du personnel de SFR font état de « conséquences sociales majeures », ainsi que d’un « impact psychosocial sans commune mesure ». Il faut dire que le sort de 5 000 salariés de SFR est bel et bien plus qu’incertain. Au moment du rachat de SFR, le consortium avait adopté un ton résolument rassurant en affirmant notamment que « l’opération envisagée a pour ambition d’être durablement créatrice de valeur pour l’ensemble des parties prenantes — clients, salariés, partenaires […] ». Entre-temps, des rumeurs de synergies ont circulé et l’État se serait dit non compétent sur ce dossier, selon Olivier Louise, secrétaire général de la CFTC Bouygues Telecom.
En parallèle de l’action menée en justice contre le consortium Bouygues, Orange et Iliad, le CSE a également engagé des poursuites contre la direction d’Altice France, la maison mère de SFR. Par ailleurs, les salariés de SFR seront en grève l’après-midi du jeudi 24 septembre.

articles.title: Brahma AI raises $150M led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management
articles.text:
Brahma AI raises $150M led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management
Brahma AI is expanding beyond its existing media and entertainment focus into sports, healthcare, and advertising, while developing new AI applications.
Enterprise AI company Brahma AI has raised $150 million in a funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management, as it looks to expand its AI platform across media and entertainment, sports, healthcare, and advertising.
Multiples invested $100 million through the issuance of preferred shares, while Brahma AI has received a further $100 million in investor interest.
The company works with global customers such as Warner Bros, the NBA, and Mayo Clinic. Its strategic distribution partners include Google, Hakuhodo, and DNEG.
Founded and led by Prabhu Narasimhan, Brahma AI brings together technology and capabilities developed across DNEG, Metaphysic, and Prime Focus Technologies. Narasimhan serves as Founder and CEO, while Jo Plaete, Co-founder and CTO, heads the company's technology and R&D division.
The company's AI-native platform comprises Brahma AI Core and Brahma AI Studio. Its technology combines enterprise content intelligence and management with AI creation capabilities spanning visual AI, digital humans, voice, and multilingual performance.
"Brahma AI is reimagining the content supply chain in the age of AI. Our investment is anchored in the belief that every enterprise is becoming a content enterprise. Multiples Private Equity will be an active partner as the company navigates the next phase of growth through investments in R&D, global market expansion, and talent & process build-out,” said Renuka Ramnath, Founder, MD & CEO of Multiples.
Brahma AI plans to expand its technology into new use cases and is working towards interactive digital humans. The company is also developing its platform to be model agnostic, while focusing on security, authenticity, and provenance.
“We are close to launching interactive digital humans, we are building Brahma AI to be model agnostic, and we are taking our technology into entirely new use cases. And security, authenticity and provenance are such an important part of what we are building," said Prabhu Narasimhan, Founder & CEO of Brahma AI.

articles.title: La carrera de la IA está entrando en otra fase: tras Opus 5.5, OpenAI juega una baza clave con GPT-6 Sol y Luna
articles.text:
Podemos medir parte del ritmo actual de la inteligencia artificial en horas. Anthropic acababa de presentar Claude Opus 5.5 cuando, apenas 90 unos después, OpenAI anunció dos nuevos integrantes de su familia GPT-6: Sol y Luna. Es otra fotografía de una carrera que ha cambiado muchísimo desde el lanzamiento de ChatGPT en noviembre de 2022. Hemos pasado de sorprendernos porque un chatbot pudiera mantener una conversación a trabajar con modelos capaces de programar, utilizar herramientas y afrontar tareas profesionales cada vez más complejas. Y ahora empieza a importar tanto lo que pueden hacer como lo que cuesta utilizarlos.
Dentro de esa nueva generación, los dos modelos ocupan escalones distintos. Astra continúa siendo, según la propia OpenAI, su opción más capaz para los trabajos más exigentes; Sol busca cubrir tareas complejas, especialmente programación y trabajo profesional, mientras que Luna está orientado a operaciones de gran volumen y objetivo bien definido, como resumir documentos, extraer información o responder consultas rápidas. La compañía cifra en un 50% la reducción de los precios de API de ambos frente a los precios promocionales de GPT-5.6 Sol y Luna, aunque las tarifas concretas varían según el modelo y si hablamos de entrada o salida.
La carrera ya no consiste solo en ser más inteligente
Las mejoras que OpenAI atribuye a Sol se concentran en varios frentes, pero una de las más fáciles de entender está en la factualidad. En una evaluación interna construida a partir de conversaciones reales en las que los usuarios habían señalado errores, GPT-6 Sol cometió aproximadamente la mitad de fallos que GPT-5.6 Sol. La propia compañía advierte de que estas conversaciones fueron seleccionadas precisamente porque habían provocado errores y no representan el uso habitual. OpenAI también asegura avances claros en programación: en FrontierCode, una prueba que valora si los cambios generados están listos para integrarse en código real, Sol mejora de forma sustancial frente a su predecesor. Astra, en cualquier caso, sigue siendo el modelo más capaz de la familia.
La segunda parte de la ecuación aparece cuando bajamos esas mejoras a la factura. Frente a los precios promocionales de GPT-5.6 Sol, el nuevo Sol pasa de 4 a 2 dólares por millón de tokens de entrada y de 20 a 10 dólares en salida. Luna baja de 0,20 a 0,10 dólares en entrada y de 1,20 a 0,50 dólares en salida respecto a GPT-5.6 Luna. OpenAI atribuye parte de ese abaratamiento a mejoras en inferencia y caché. Y aquí importa algo más que la tarifa por token: si un agente necesita encadenar numerosas llamadas para completar una tarea, el coste acumulado termina siendo una variable fundamental.
El movimiento de Anthropic ayuda a entender que esta presión por hacer más con menos no afecta únicamente a OpenAI. Claude Opus 5.5 llegó apenas unos minutos antes que Sol y Luna, y la compañía liderada por Dario Amodei asegura que ofrece un rendimiento comparable al de Fable 5.1 con un coste operativo un 40% inferior al de Opus 5. Son comparaciones publicadas por las propias compañías, con pruebas y configuraciones distintas, lo que dificulta identificar claramente cuál de los nuevos modelos sale mejor parado. Sí apuntan, en cambio, a una tendencia más amplia: capacidad y coste empiezan a competir en la misma conversación, incluso entre algunos de los sistemas más avanzados.
La llegada, además, empieza desde este mismo 22 de septiembre. GPT-6 Sol y Luna están disponibles en ChatGPT Work y Codex para usuarios Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise y Edu, mientras que Luna también puede utilizarse en la aplicación de escritorio con cuentas Free y Go; ambos modelos llegan igualmente a la API. OpenAI prevé extenderlos de forma gradual a ChatGPT a lo largo del día.

articles.title: La UE limitará el uso de agua y energía tras el uso excesivo en los centros de datos
articles.text:
La Unión Europea prepara nuevas reglas para controlar el consumo de energía y agua de los centros de datos, cuya expansión está aumentando la presión sobre las redes eléctricas y los recursos hídricos del bloque.
Bruselas presentó un nuevo sistema de calificación que permitirá comparar la sostenibilidad de estas instalaciones y anunció que en 2027 establecerá estándares mínimos de rendimiento que podrían limitar el funcionamiento y construcción de nuevos centros de datos poco eficientes.
PUBLICIDAD
La medida llega mientras Europa busca aumentar su capacidad de infraestructura para inteligencia artificial (IA), computación en la nube y otros servicios digitales. La Comisión Europea pretende triplicar la capacidad de los centros de datos del bloque hasta 2035, pero también reconoce que este crecimiento tiene un costo energético y ambiental cada vez mayor.
Los centros de datos tendrán una etiqueta de sostenibilidad
A partir del 21 de septiembre, los centros de datos de la UE con más de 500 kilovatios de capacidad instalada que presenten los informes exigidos por las normas comunitarias podrán recibir una etiqueta electrónica de sostenibilidad.
El objetivo es hacer más transparente el consumo de estos establecimientos y facilitar la comparación entre instalaciones. La etiqueta tendrá en cuenta aspectos como la eficiencia energética, el uso de agua y el origen de la electricidad utilizada.
PUBLICIDAD
La Comisión Europea considera que esta información podría ayudar a los gobiernos a diseñar políticas más eficientes y a empresas y organizaciones a elegir servicios digitales con un menor impacto ambiental.
Sin embargo, el sistema todavía no establece un límite máximo de consumo. Las restricciones más estrictas llegarán posteriormente.
Bruselas espera fijar límites en 2027
La Comisión prevé presentar en 2027 normas mínimas de rendimiento para los centros de datos. Estas establecerán determinados niveles de eficiencia que deberán cumplir las nuevas instalaciones y podrían impedir la construcción de centros que no alcancen esos estándares.
Por ahora, Bruselas mantiene un periodo de transición para recopilar información y mejorar el cumplimiento de las obligaciones existentes.
Los centros de datos de más de 500 kW ya deben presentar información desde 2023, aunque la Comisión reconoce que una parte importante de las instalaciones todavía no cumple completamente con esta obligación. Según un funcionario comunitario, el porcentaje de centros declarados ha aumentado progresivamente y podría superar el 50%.
PUBLICIDAD
La aplicación de estas normas corresponde principalmente a los Estados miembros, por lo que el nivel de cumplimiento puede variar entre países.
La IA aumenta la demanda de electricidad
El problema está directamente relacionado con el crecimiento de la inteligencia artificial. Los modelos de IA necesitan grandes cantidades de capacidad informática, y esa infraestructura funciona principalmente en centros de datos que requieren electricidad de manera constante.
En 2024, los centros de datos europeos consumieron 68 teravatios hora (TWh) de electricidad. La UE calcula que esa cifra llegará a 114 TWh en 2030, cuando podría representar el 3,2% del consumo eléctrico del bloque, frente al 2,5% actual.
Además de electricidad, estas instalaciones pueden necesitar grandes cantidades de agua para sus sistemas de refrigeración. Su expansión también genera preocupación en comunidades locales debido a la presión que puede ejercer sobre las redes eléctricas y los recursos disponibles.
PUBLICIDAD
Microsoft ya interviene en las nuevas reglas
Mientras Bruselas desarrolla el marco de sostenibilidad, las grandes empresas tecnológicas están intentando participar en la definición de los criterios.
Microsoft expresó en julio de 2026 su respaldo al uso de indicadores relacionados con energía limpia y eficiencia energética e hídrica. Al mismo tiempo, solicitó cambios en algunos de los rangos de eficiencia hídrica previstos para la nueva etiqueta.
La participación de las grandes tecnológicas ha generado críticas de organizaciones como Corporate Europe Observatory, que cuestiona el grado de influencia de estas empresas en la elaboración de las normas.
Uno de los puntos de discusión es la cantidad de información que será pública. Críticos de la propuesta sostienen que las reglas de confidencialidad podrían dificultar la verificación independiente de algunos datos incluidos en las etiquetas.
PUBLICIDAD
Europa busca crecer en IA sin aumentar la presión energética
La UE se enfrenta así a un doble objetivo: ampliar rápidamente su infraestructura tecnológica para competir en inteligencia artificial y, al mismo tiempo, controlar el impacto energético y ambiental de esa expansión.
Bruselas también estudia otras alternativas. Entre ellas está convertir los centros de datos en participantes más activos de la red eléctrica mediante mecanismos de flexibilidad y aprovechar el calor residual generado por sus instalaciones, que potencialmente podría utilizarse para suministrar calefacción a hasta cuatro millones de hogares europeos.
La nueva etiqueta será el primer paso de un proceso que podría terminar en requisitos obligatorios de eficiencia para las futuras instalaciones. Con ello, la UE busca que el crecimiento de la infraestructura necesaria para la IA no se traduzca en un aumento sin control del consumo de agua y electricidad.

articles.title: Okta adds AI agent runtime gateway, forms Blueprint Alliance with AWS and CrowdStrike - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Okta adds AI agent runtime gateway, forms Blueprint Alliance with AWS and CrowdStrike
Identity and access management company Okta Inc. used the opening day of its Oktane conference in Las Vegas today to announce runtime enforcement and a wider kill switch for its Okta for AI Agents platform.
Okta also joined 11 other vendors, among them Amazon Web Services Inc., CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. and Google Cloud, in forming the Blueprint Alliance. The group is reworking the agent security framework Okta first published in March into an open, multivendor reference architecture.
The product additions are aimed at agents that end up with more access than anyone intended. An employee who links an AI assistant to everyday tools can give it a path into sensitive systems without realizing it, Okta said. If that person later leaves, nothing stops the agent from running on in the background, ungoverned.
“The challenge businesses face is the same access that makes agents powerful also makes them dangerous,” said Ric Smith, president of products and technology at Okta.
The runtime piece is Agent Gateway, which sits in the execution path between an agent and the tools it calls, enforcing policy and logging each interaction as it happens. Okta’s existing visibility comes from agent events captured in its System Log, which customers stream to security information and event management systems for review after the fact.
The gateway is also where the kill switch is headed. Administrators can already deactivate an agent from the admin console, which blocks new sessions. Once an agent routed through the gateway is deactivated there, Okta plans for every active token it holds to be revoked and every session in flight shut down.
Discovery now extends to employee laptops and desktops. Okta can already register known agents directly or import them from platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Salesforce Agentforce, and shadow agents working through the browser get picked up too. A new feature, Shadow AI Agent Discovery for Endpoints, looks for unmanaged agents running on those machines.
Once an agent is on the books, the remaining additions govern what it connects to, whether that’s an app, a Model Context Protocol server or another agent. Agent SSO brings Cross App Access, which Okta debuted in June 2025, to all of its single sign-on customers so they can swap non-expiring keys for short-lived tokens tied to an identity.
Rules on which agents may call which other agents come through Agent-to-Agent Connections, with each handoff recorded in an auditable chain. Resource Access Certifications review agent connections over time to catch standing or excessive permissions. For administrators who would rather see the map, Configuration Designer draws agent-to-resource connections visually.
The Blueprint Alliance takes the framework behind those products outside Okta. Founding members also include Databricks Inc., Docker Inc., Lovable Labs Inc., Proofpoint Inc., Salesforce Inc. and ServiceNow Inc. Wiz Inc. has a seat of its own alongside Google Cloud, six months after Google closed its $32 billion purchase of the company. Zscaler Inc. is the 12th member.
“No single technology or vendor can secure the agentic era alone,” said Daniel Bernard, chief business officer at CrowdStrike.
Research from Gartner Inc. cited by the alliance predicts that the average global Fortune 500 enterprise will have more than 150,000 agents in use by 2028. Only 13% of organizations think they have the right AI agent governance in place, Gartner said in the same release.
The March version of the blueprint was built around questions about where agents run, what they can reach and what they do. The alliance’s version adds how an enterprise should respond when an agent is compromised, with containment through token revocation, session termination or network quarantine and a staged, auditable path for restoring it afterward. Members have agreed on principles that include treating every agent as a first-class identity and scoping its access to the task at hand.
Beyond the principles, members are already testing interoperability across open standards, including MCP, the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework and the Shared Signals Framework. The goal is for a threat signal raised by one member’s runtime monitor to trigger action across every connected control plane. Joint test results and reference integrations will be published on a regular basis.
GE Appliances and the nonprofit World Central Kitchen are serving as strategic advisers. Brian Stoll, chief technology officer at World Central Kitchen, said the organization is using agentic technology to support disaster response and needs governance “as dynamic as the agents themselves.” Taking part in the alliance, he added, might also bring “a better night’s rest for the CTO.”
Of the new Okta features, Agent SSO, Agent-to-Agent Connections and Resource Access Certifications are generally available today. Agent Gateway and Shadow AI Agent Discovery for Endpoints are planned for general availability in the third quarter, followed by Configuration Designer and the gateway kill switch in the fourth. More alliance members are expected to join over time.

articles.title: British Columbia says OpenAI could have stopped a school shooting, and is suing over it
articles.text:
What just happened? OpenAI and Sam Altman are being sued by British Columbia over claims that the company could have prevented a mass shooting in the Canadian province. The lawsuit alleges that OpenAI failed to inform authorities about the shooter's violent ChatGPT conversations.
The suit, which was filed in San Francisco federal court, accuses OpenAI accuses OpenAI of designing an unsafe product and acting negligently. It seeks damages to fund recovery efforts in the province following the shooting at a school in Tumbler Ridge in February.
The British Columbia government seeks financial compensation from the tech giant for past and future expenses related to emergency response and community recovery. It also asks the court to require the company to change how it detects and responds to user conversations involving threats of violence.
Nine people, most of whom were children, were killed in the school shooting. The shooter killed her mother and half-brother at their home before going to the secondary school, where she killed five children aged 12 and 13 and an educational assistant. She then died by suicide.
The shooter, eighteen-year-old former pupil Jesse Van Rootselaar, had previously been flagged by OpenAI's safety team for her conversations about gun violence but OpenAI never alerted police because the conversations did not meet the threshold for legal referral.
The suit claims that the shooting would have been averted if the company had followed its human reviewers' advice to notify the Royal Canadian Mounted Police about Rootselaar's activities.
Altman apologized in April for OpenAI's failure to contact police at the time. The lawsuit says that while he promised reforms, the company never followed through, despite efforts from British Columbia's attorney general to engage.
The school where the shooting occurred is now being demolished, while the province has had to cover the cost of a replacement school, mental health support, and other expenses stemming from the attack.
Van Rootselaar's actions were first flagged by OpenAI in June 2025. The lawsuit alleges that members of OpenAI's safety team urged the company to contact police, but Altman and other senior executives rejected the recommendation. It cites OpenAI whistleblowers who spoke to The Wall Street Journal after the shooting. Her account was deactivated, but she opened a new account and continued using the AI to plan her attack.
This isn't the first time OpenAI has faced legal action connected to a mass shooting. In June, Florida sued OpenAI and Altman, alleging that ChatGPT had contributed to real-world harms, including the 2025 Florida State University shooting. The lawsuit followed a criminal investigation launched by Florida's attorney general into OpenAI and ChatGPT over the incident. That probe was later expanded after prosecutors alleged that a suspect in the murders of two University of South Florida students had also used ChatGPT before the killings.

articles.title: IT mistake erases 11 years of viewing history for hospitals’ maternity records
articles.text:
A “human error” in the IT department led to Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (NUH) losing data from maternity records over an 11-year span.
The data loss occurred on August 18, the English hospitals announced in a blog post on Monday spotted by The Register. The blog said the problem is “the result of human error” during routine technical work while “creating a copy of a radiotherapy database for reporting purposes.”
The post reads:
The process used a set of pre-written computer instructions that had previously been used for a different hospital system. A setting that should have been changed before the process was run was missed. As a result, the process was carried out on a maternity database instead of the radiotherapy database, causing the maternity records database to be overwritten.
The overwritten database held data from NUH’s previous maternity database, which included maternity records for women and babies who received care from NUH from September 2011 to November 2022.
NUH has been unable to retrieve some of the data, the blog said:
… we have not been able to restore the complete history showing who viewed maternity records during this period. As a result, in most cases, we may be unable to confirm whether a maternity record was viewed by a particular person between September 2011 and November 2022.
NUH said that it escalated the problem “within minutes of being identified” and “worked with external specialists and reviewed other sources of information to recover as much data as possible.” It was able to restore patient care-related data, including “notes, observations, test results, and other information recorded as part of a person’s care.”

articles.title: Diablo 5 veut vous redonner un sentiment de surpuissance, contrairement à Diablo 4
articles.text:
Plus on entend Blizzard parler de Diablo 5, plus on se dit que Diablo 4 constitue un aveu d’échec. L’ambition initiale derrière le hack’n’slash paru en 2023 était d’en faire un jeu-service pensé pour durer de longues années. Les plans ont changé, matérialisés par l’envie de faire revenir Diablo en personne. Pour ce faire, une simple extension de Diablo 4 n’aurait pas suffi.
Diablo 5 va aussi permettre à Blizzard de repenser certains systèmes de sa saga, en lien avec ce que désirent vraiment les fans. Des évolutions et changements qui ne sauraient se satisfaire d’une mise à jour, même immense, de Diablo 4. L’un des chantiers évoqués par le studio concerne la progression, qui devrait davantage se rapprocher de celle de Diablo 2, découvre-t-on dans un article paru ce mardi 22 septembre sur PC Gamer.
Une progression repensée pour Diablo 5
Dans les jeux Diablo, la progression est une part importante de l’expérience. On va dans une zone, on tue des ennemis, on gagne des niveaux, on ramasse des nouvelles pièces d’équipement, on devient plus puissant. Et ainsi de suite. Ce sentiment de supériorité est néanmoins inhibé dans Diablo 3 et Diablo 4, qui ajustent le niveau des monstres en permanence afin de garantir une dose suffisante de challenge. Ce n’était pas le cas dans Diablo 2, dont les différents environnements ont chacun un palier de difficulté.
Blizzard a semble-t-il envie que l’on ressente un sentiment de surpuissance dans Diablo 5.
C’est ce que sous-entend le directeur Joe Shely, cité par PC Gamer : « Diablo est un jeu qui consiste à faire monter votre personnage en puissance. […] vous avez rempli la barre d’expérience, vous devenez plus fort, vous devriez vous sentir fantastique, une vague de lumière émane de vous, une horde de monstres meurt. »
Sauf qu’il y a un problème, avec l’ajustement automatique du niveau des monstres que le jeu vous oppose, au fil de votre progression. Si ceux-ci deviennent plus forts en même temps que le joueur, cette impression de puissance se retrouve diminuée ou nullifiée. C’est le problème du level scaling, pensé pour maintenir du défi en permanence.
L’intéressé explique que ce mécanisme « peut entraver ce sentiment, qui est pourtant fondamental dans le jeu, et c’est pourquoi c’est une question très importante. C’est la raison pour laquelle nous allons adopter une approche un peu différente sur ce point dans Diablo 5 ». Toute la question est de savoir comment.
Joe Shely ne rentre pas dans les détails, étant donné que Diablo 5 n’est pas attendu avant 2029. On imagine que les développeurs réfléchissent encore à la bonne manière de faire. Peut-être la réponse se trouve-t-elle dans un système hybride, avec des ennemis qui pourraient adapter leur niveau jusqu’à un certain point en fonction de l’endroit où ils se trouvent. Avec une telle structure, on conserverait un défi suffisant, tout en garantissant les moments de surpuissance espérés.
Pour rappel, Diablo 5 reviendra à un modèle procédural – — autre élément repris de Diablo 2.
La progression n’est qu’un des chantiers hérités de Diablo 2. Blizzard a aussi confirmé le retour d’un système de butin à l’ancienne — mots runiques, sets d’équipement et objets soumis à des seuils de statistiques — ainsi qu’un casting de classes étoffé, avec le retour du Chasseur de démons et du Moine, tous deux absents de Diablo 4.

articles.title: Snorkel AI triples valuation to $3.5B as demand for AI training data booms | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Snorkel AI, a startup that helps AI labs and corporations build training datasets and simulated environments, has raised a $350 million Series E at a $3.5 billion valuation.
The new round, which was led by Insight Partners and S32, valued the seven-year-old startup at nearly triple the $1.3 billion valuation it garnered when it raised $100 million in a Series D 17 months ago. Existing investors, including Addition, Lightspeed, Greylock, GV, and Wells Fargo, also participated in the round.
While Snorkel originally provided software for data-labeling automation, it shifted last year to providing customers with completed datasets, an offering it calls data-as-a-service. Rather than operating purely as a human expert marketplace, Snorkel relies on a hybrid approach, using its software and models to generate data synthetically alongside subject matter experts.
Snorkel says its current annualized revenue run rate now stands at $375 million, an eighteenfold increase over the last 12 months. That growth is fueled by AI labs’ insatiable appetite for high-end training data.
Other data companies positioning themselves as AI data labs have seen a similar explosion in growth. Mercor’s gross annualized revenue has climbed to $2 billion, Handshake hit the $1 billion milestone earlier this year, and TechCrunch reported that Micro1 has scaled to $500 million. Since these companies pay out roughly 60% to 70% of their top-line income directly to the domain specialists doing the work, it’s important to note that their actual net annual revenue is substantially lower than those headline gross figures.
Given that Snorkel sells reinforcement learning (RL) environments and complete datasets rather than human labor, payments to its human experts are accounted for in its cost of goods sold rather than headline-generating annualized revenue numbers, according to the company.
Snorkel launched commercially in 2019 following four years of research by co-founder and CEO Alex Ratner and his team at a Stanford AI lab.

articles.title: TerraMaster Announces New U-725 Rackmount NAS Series for Enterprise Storage
articles.text:

TerraMaster Announces New U-725 Rackmount NAS Series for Enterprise Storage
TerraMaster, a professional brand specializing in innovative storage products, today announced the launch of four new enterprise rackmount storage servers: the U8-725, U12-725, U12-725 Plus and U16-725 Plus. Designed for medium and large businesses, creative studios, virtualization environments, surveillance deployments and AI-driven workloads, the new lineup combines high-performance processing, flexible storage expansion, high-speed networking and integrated data protection to provide a scalable platform for demanding business environments.
Powered by TerraMaster's TOS 7 AI-native operating system, the new servers are designed to support multiple business-critical workloads from a single platform, including enterprise file services, media collaboration, virtualization, centralized surveillance storage, AI dataset access, backup and disaster recovery. The Ux-725 series is built around Intel Xeon D processors and features ECC memory, NVMe SSD cache acceleration and high-bandwidth networking to provide responsive performance for business applications, virtual machines and large file transfers.The U12-725, is powered by an Intel Xeon D-2712T processor with 16 GB of ECC DDR4 memory, expandable up to 1 TB, allowing organizations to increase available system resources as workloads and business requirements grow. High-speed networking is also built into the platform, with the U12-725 offering up to 50 Gbps of combined network bandwidth through four 10GbE SFP+ ports and two 5GbE RJ45 ports. Support for link aggregation enables businesses to combine network connections to eliminate the implication that link aggregation boosts bandwidth to reach the 50 Gbps bandwidth
The new rackmount servers are also designed to support virtualized environments and AI-focused workloads, providing the storage performance and expansion flexibility required for demanding data applications. Multiple PCIe expansion slots allow organizations to add high-speed networking cards, RAID controllers, AI acceleration hardware and other expansion devices as infrastructure requirements evolve.
Storage capacity can similarly be scaled to suit different environments. The U8-725, U12-725, U12-725 Plus and U16-725 Plus combine multiple drive bays with NVMe cache slots and expansion capabilities, providing businesses with a flexible storage platform that can grow alongside their data requirements. The U12-725 supports up to 12 drive bays, while the larger U16-725 Plus provides 16-bay capacity for organizations managing substantial volumes of business data.Data protection is supported through TerraMaster BBS (Business Backup Suite), which provides a centralized platform for backup, synchronization, snapshots and disaster recovery. The solution enables businesses to protect data across PCs, servers, virtual machines and network storage environments without additional software licensing costs. Built-in snapshot functionality, remote replication and data recovery tools further help protect critical information against accidental deletion, hardware failure and ransomware threats.
All four systems run TerraMaster's latest TOS 7 operating system, bringing together file sharing and collaboration, multi-user access management, virtualization support, centralized backup, cloud synchronization, remote access and monitoring, snapshot protection and AI-ready data management. Together, these capabilities are designed to provide businesses with a single platform for managing, accessing and protecting data across a range of demanding applications.

articles.title: Which DJI Mic should I buy? These are the key differences you need to know
articles.text:
Which DJI Mic should I buy? These are the key differences you need to know
A handy overview of DJI's excellent microphone lineup
DJI built its name on drones, but nowadays it has firmly established itself in multiple other content creator gadget markets too. That includes mics. The brand makes a selection of microphones, including two models released this year. Our testers have been extremely impressed with all of them — so much so, we awarded every single one a perfect five stars in their respective reviews.
If you're a content creator looking to upgrade your audio so it's just as good as your video, how do you choose between them? There's no dud option here, but certain models will be better than others depending on your needs. Below, you'll find an overview of the brand, links to find out more about each one, and a handy specs comparison table. Here's everything you need to know about DJI's microphone range.
DJI mic range
There are two main microphone lines: Mic and Mic Mini. The former is more pro-friendly, larger and higher specced (details vary by model, but expect superior audio quality, more adaptable noise cancelling and features like timecode and built-in storage). The latter is more compact and lightweight — although note the main Mic models aren't exactly bulky — and an excellent entry-level choice.
Scroll down for more details, and tap the View details button for a summary of each model, plus a link to read the full reviews.
In the main range the Mic 2 (launched 2024) and Mic 3 (launched 2025) are still widely available. In the Mini range, it's the Mic Mini (launched 2024), Mic Mini 2 and Mic Mini 2S (both released 2026). We awarded every single one of them a perfect five stars in our reviews, so you can expect a very capable mic no matter which one you go for.
Broadly speaking, within each lineup it's the newer the model, the more advanced the specs — although the gaps between some generations are bigger than others. The Mini 2S came out more recently than the Mini 2, and offers a number of upgrades over that model, most notable of which is internal recording.
For each model, you can also choose from various bundles of transmitters (TX), receivers (RX) and charge cases. These elements can, broadly speaking, also be purchased individually.

articles.title: Xbox keeps cutting with 268 more layoffs, hands Halo to Activision
articles.text:
The Xbox bloodbath continues with another round of layoffs and an internal shuffle that puts the next Halo game in Activision’s hands.
In a public staff memo titled “Continuing our reset,” Xbox’s executive vice president and chief content officer Matt Booty outlined the changes. These include the elimination of 268 roles across Halo Studios and other first-party studios, Xbox Game Studios management, and the “central functions” team.
Next, Booty detailed how Xbox is reorganizing its studios. First, Activision will expand to include World’s Edge and Rare, as well as developing the next Halo title. Booty said development would be “led by a new, purpose-built team that is separate from ongoing development and plans for Call of Duty.” Meanwhile, a small team at Halo Studios will continue to support the current, in-market games.
Similarly, Bethesda will expand to include Obsidian, with Booty noting the studio will continue current projects like Grounded and the new Fallout game in collaboration with Bethesda Game Studios.
King, the developers behind Candy Crush, will expand to include Microsoft Casual Games.
Wrapping up the reorganizations, Booty said Playground and Turn 10 will merge into one studio focused on the Forza and Fable franchises.
Finally, Booty shared an update on Xbox’s studio divestitures, noting that Undead Labs transitioned “on similar terms” to Double Fine and award-winning Canadian developers Compulsion Games, but will still release State of Decay III day one on Game Pass.
However, Booty said that two agreements for Ninja Theory fell through, and Xbox will “begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while continuing to explore other paths forward.” Xbox also expects consultations with Arkane to continue through the end of the year.
The new round of layoffs and restructuring comes as part of the 3,200 total cuts Xbox detailed back in July. At the time, Xbox said it was cutting 1,600 employees immediately and another 1,600 over the next 12 months. In other words, there are more cuts to come, which makes Booty’s sign-off about looking ahead to “one of the strongest game lineups in our history” feel particularly tone deaf.
Amid the cuts, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma keeps talking about growing Microsoft’s gaming division with goals of reaching 500 million people every day by 2030 — nearly five times what Sharma says Xbox currently reaches. But it’s not clear how the company could do that when it continues gutting studios and laying off the people who would make the games Xbox needs to hit those kinds of numbers.

articles.title: ¿Son realmente hermanos Matthew McConaughey y Woody Harrelson?: "Encontraron algunas pistas"
articles.text:
Una de las leyendas más divertidas de todo Hollywood es la que asegura que Matthew McConaughey y Woody Harrelson son hermanos. Ambos actores comparten una fuerte amistad desde hace muchos años. Protagonistas de la primera temporada de True Detective, ahora vuelven a trabajar juntos en una serie, Brothers. Una comedia para Apple TV en la que precisamente indagan en esa posibilidad de que sean hermanos.
Y con motivo del estreno de Brothers, en Hipertextual hemos podido estar con Matthew McConaughey y Woody Harrelson durante un encuentro con la prensa. En él, nos han explicado la verdadera historia sobre su posible relación sanguínea. Y lo cierto es que el relato solo alimenta aún más las teorías.
"Mi familia estaba de vacaciones con la familia de Woody por enésima vez. Estábamos en Grecia. Mis hijos siempre le llamaban tío Woody y sus hijos me llaman tío Matthew, y así. Y una noche estábamos allí sentados con nuestras familias juntas. Probablemente ya pasada la medianoche. Todo el mundo estaba de buen humor y un poco animado", comienza a relatar McConaughey.
"Y, de repente, de la nada, mi madre dice: «Oh, yo 'conocí'... a tu padre, Woody». Y esa pausa, esos puntos suspensivos, bastaron para que incluso mi hijo de seis años dijera: «Oh, creo que sé lo que eso puede significar». La insinuación que hay detrás es... ¡bum!, los niños se pusieron a dar vueltas diciendo: «Lo sabía. Sois parientes». Y Woody también dijo: «Lo sabía»", continúa. Y es que, para Harrelson, la historia es totalmente verídica.
"Mientras tanto, yo estoy a un lado riéndome y diciendo: «Sí, claro, claro, claro». Pero la semilla de la historia ya estaba plantada y se lanzaron a ello. Empezaron a encontrar algunas pistas que, cronológicamente, hacían posible que se hubieran liado, porque habría sido durante el segundo divorcio de mis padres. Ella habría estado libre para irse de juerga al oeste de Texas con alguien. Así que él cree totalmente que es verdad. Yo no", reconoce McConaughey.
"No hay ninguna duda", se une Woody Harrelson, asegurando que él y Matthew McConaughey son hermanos de mismo padre y distinta madre. "Una gran duda. No es verdad", lo niega el segundo. "Absolutamente cierto. Al 100 %", insiste Harrelson. "Así es como empezó todo. Eso fue hace ocho año y dijimos: «Oye, hagamos una comedia familiar sobre ello»", concluye McConaughey sobre el germen de la nueva serie Brothers.
Evidentemente, ante esta posibilidad, lo primero que se viene a la mente es hacer un test de ADN para descubrir si realmente comparten genes. Pero la situación no es tan sencilla. "Podríamos hacernos una prueba de ADN, como llevo diciendo desde hace tiempo. Pero él no quiere porque no quiere confirmar el hecho de que su padre era simplemente un hombre muy majo, no su padre biológico. Big Jim era más bien un amigo, en realidad", lo explica Woody Harrelson entre risas.
"«Ese hombre que pensabas que era tu padre era, en realidad, simplemente un hombre encantador en tu vida, Matthew»", se une a la broma el propio McConaughey entre carcajadas. "Por desgracia, nunca conoció a su verdadero padre biológico, pero le habría caído bien. Tienen muchas cosas en común", vuelve a asegurar Harrelson. En cualquier caso, parece que por ahora McConaughey no está por la labor de descubrir si de verdad es hermano de su amigo o si todo queda en leyenda.
Brothers ya está disponible en Apple TV.

articles.title: ‘We’ll be the first to mine Bitcoin in space’ says Nvidia-backed startup —Starcloud will fire up its ASICs after its second spacecraft reaches orbit later this year
articles.text:
‘We’ll be the first to mine Bitcoin in space’ says Nvidia-backed startup —Starcloud will fire up its ASICs after its second spacecraft reaches orbit later this year
Almost constant solar energy plus ASIC price per KW are the most compelling aspects of the plan.
An Nvidia-backed startup plans to establish a Bitcoin mining operation in space before the year is out. Starcloud will fire up its cryptocurrency mining ASICs after its second spacecraft reaches orbit later this year. “We’ll be the first to mine Bitcoin in space,” claimed Starcloud CEO Philip Johnston in a recent interview with Documenting Bitcoin.
Starcloud was founded in 2024 with the headlining goal of moving data centers to space. “As launch costs fall, data centers in space will leverage continuous solar energy and radiative cooling, rapidly scaling to gigawatts while avoiding permitting constraints on Earth,” reads its mission statement. The firm spells out its proposition in far greater detail in a white paper on its website, highlighting the appeal of training AI in space. However, the ample supply of solar energy is also great for cryptomining.
So, when Starcloud-2 reaches orbit, it will be tasked with raising some crypto-cash. In the embedded interview segment, Johnston said: “We’ll have some Bitcoin mining ASICs on the second spacecraft launching later this year.” At the time of writing 1BTC is worth roughly $86,000, quite a way down from highs several months ago.
Starcloud-2 is just the second of four currently planned satellite launches from the startup. It is framed as the company's first commercial mission, and like the prior satellite, will feature a GPU cluster. Interestingly, the official Starcloud-2 project page doesn’t mention Bitcoin mining or ASICs, so Johnston’s reveal is quite eyebrow-raising. Moreover, for something that seems a bit like an afterthought, “Potentially it [Bitcoin mining] is one of the most compelling use cases of space compute,” the Starcloud CEO told Documenting Bitcoin.
Johnson provided some financial insight into why there is now a Bitcoin side gig or pivot being considered. He cited the lower costs of ASICs vs. GPUs: they are about 30x cheaper than GPUs per kilowatt, he told the host. A specific example given was a 1KW Nvidia B200 chip at $30,000 vs. a 1KW ASIC at $1,000. Solving the energy supply situation in space for GPUs, or for ASICs, isn’t relevant to the business, said Johnson. We wonder what Nvidia will think about that.
While the availability of near-uninterrupted solar power is a big attraction of space-based compute, there are downsides. For example, satellites aren’t easy to service, and convection cooling doesn’t work in a vacuum. Commercial space-based data centers are so new that some of the problems and solutions will only become entirely clear after pioneering deployments like the Starcloud-2.
