articles.title: Thunderobot dévoile un laptop Ryzen AI Max+ 395 avec 85 Go de cache IA sur SSD
articles.text:
On connaissait surtout Thunderobot pour ses PC portables gaming, le voilà qui dégaine désormais l’AI Master M7000, une station de travail mobile dévolue au calcul local de (très) grands modèles de langage, rendu possible par une configuration SSD pas encore si courante.
Les PC portables se démarquent rarement par le choix de leur SSD. C’est pourtant le cas du nouveau Thunderobot AI Master M7000. Lancé en Chine à un tarif avoisinant les 3300 euros une fois conversion faite, ce nouveau modèle de 16 pouces s’appuie sur un SSD M.2 hybride mêlant 768 Go de stockage « classique » et 85 Go de cache consacré à l’IA locale.
Une machine Strix Halo plutôt commune…
De prime abord, l’AI Master M7000 s’appuie sur une configuration « Strix Halo » désormais courante sur le segment des stations de travail mobiles dédiées au calcul local de grands modèles de langage. On y retrouve un Ryzen AI Max+395 couplé à 64 Go de mémoire vive unifiée LPDDR5x. Le lancement de cette puce mobile (que nous avions testé sur une tablette gaming) remonte au début d’année 2025 mais sa diffusion à grande échelle se fait sur le tard… Parallèlement aux nouveaux SoC « Gorgon Halo » comme le puissant AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 495 Pro installé sur un nombre croissant de mini-PC.
Quoi qu’il en soit, le Ryzen AI Max+395 est tenu en respect, sur la machine qui nous intéresse aujourd'hui, par un système de dissipation à triple caloduc et double ventilateur, plutôt classique sur les modèles gaming. Ce dispositif permet de dissiper jusqu’à 160 W, note Thunderobot, qui évoque aussi la présence d’un écran QHD+ / 165 Hz et 100 % sRGB sur l’appareil. Une dalle IPS qui n’a rien de spectaculaire au regard du prix salé de l’AI Master M7000.
L'engin s’appuie pour le reste sur une batterie de 99 Wh et s’en tient à un châssis de 2,45 kg, dans la moyenne pour ce segment. On y trouve enfin un port USB-C à 40 Gbps, une sortie HDMI 2.1, une prise Ethernet, un port OCuLink (pour la connexion d’une carte graphique externe), ainsi qu’un lecteur de cartes SD.
… à un gros détail près
Comme évoqué plus haut, sa caractéristique la plus intéressante touche à la question du SSD, basé sur la technologie hybride aiDAPTIV+ de Phison. Elle permet dans le cas présent de loger, sur une seule et même barrette M.2, 768 Go d’espace de stockage « classique » et 85 Go de mémoire cache dévolue à l’IA.
Ces 85 Go de cache n’ont évidemment pas pour vocation de remplacer la mémoire unifiée du SoC, mais de servir comme un espace de stockage temporaire pour certains workloads. Cette approche hybride leur permet en effet de conserver une partie de leurs données actives sur le SSD, soulageant ainsi la RAM lorsque cette dernière est saturée.
De quoi permettre au Thunderobot AI Master M7000 de jouer localement avec des LLM qui seraient normalement au-dessus de ses moyens en RAM. C’est le cas de GPT-OSS-120B, par exemple. Thunderobot explique d’ailleurs que d’autres modèles MoE à 120 milliards de paramètres peuvent être gérés efficacement, toujours en local, grâce à ces 85 Go de mémoire cache. Et comme le souligne VideoCardz, Phison avait quant à lui démontré l’efficacité de son concept en faisant tourner GPT-OSS-120B sur un PC portable Panther Lake limité à 32 Go de mémoire vive.

articles.title: Claude's merged chat and Cowork vs. ChatGPT's Work mode: ChatGPT is faster, Claude is more thorough
articles.text:
Claude’s merged chat and Cowork vs. ChatGPT’s Work mode: ChatGPT is faster, Claude is more thorough
When Anthropic merged Claude chat and Cowork into a single interface last week, it removed an increasingly irrelevant decision users had to make about which mode to choose.
Now, to use both tools, just ask a question, then hand off a multi-step task in the same thread, and Claude routes it. Anthropic made this update because it says customers often struggled to choose the right tab for the right task, so the merged app now routes each request itself instead of asking you to pick a mode — for now, the unified experience is rolling out to Pro and Max subscribers first, with free and team tiers to follow.
But this isn’t new. OpenAI has offered the same promise since earlier this summer. OpenAI introduced Work mode alongside Chat on July 9, then phased out the older, separate Agent mode the following month. Work mode is a sandboxed environment with a browser, code execution, and file output, sitting next to a Chat toggle in the same window — though reviewers note it can’t yet hand a live, logged-in browser session back to the user mid-task the way Agent mode could, e.g., for logins or payments. OpenAI built Work mode on its Codex coding agent after OpenAI reported that roughly a fifth of Codex’s 5 million weekly users were non-developers — a share it said was growing three times faster than developers.
As OpenAI and Anthropic get closer to feature parity, accuracy, reliability, and token usage matter even more. What better way to find out which tool is better than to run head-to-head tests?
The tests
I ran three tests, covering different areas of real developer work.
- API research -Look up four real developer APIs and tabulate their documented rate limits, whether a free tier exists, and the current version identifier. I checked the answers against the vendors’ docs the same day.
- Build from a spec – Write a small command-line duration parser from a spec with strict edge cases. I ran each app’s code against a hidden 16-case test suite.
- The handoff – Ask which of two stack traces indicates a race condition, then in the same thread hand off a real job: pull a log file from Google Drive, compute latency percentiles and error rates per endpoint, and deliver a spreadsheet with a chart. I generated the log data, so I knew every number in advance.
I recorded token cost and time in each test and included the prompts for anyone interested in replicating this work.
API research
The prompt:
Research the current public documentation for these four developer APIs and build me a table with one row per API and these columns: documented rate limit for authenticated requests, whether a free tier exists (yes/no), and the current API version identifier or date shown in the docs. APIs: GitHub REST API, Stripe API, Twilio Messaging API, OpenAI API. Cite the documentation page you used for each row.
Both Claude and ChatGPT answered correctly on the twelve graded fields, but Claude was more thorough. It included GitHub’s separate limit for Actions tokens, Twilio’s queue window, and OpenAI’s tier thresholds, plus a note about one page it couldn’t reach.
ChatGPT, in Work mode, finished in 1 minute 17 seconds and wrote 649 output tokens. Claude took 1 minute 44 seconds and wrote 1,042 tokens, read eight pages, listed nine sources, and offered to export the table as a spreadsheet. Claude wrote nearly double the tokens and took longer, but in this case, it’s warranted because of the added detail.
Build from a spec
The prompt:
Build the command-line tool described in the spec below. Deliver a single file named durparse.py that follows every rule. Test it yourself before returning it. Show the complete final code in your reply. (Followed by the spec: a duration parser with units d/h/m/s, largest first, one of each, decimals allowed, bare numbers are seconds, everything else returns None.)
Both apps returned a durparse.py file that passed all 16 hidden tests, including the traps. The traps included units out of order, a repeated unit, a trailing number with no unit, and negative values. The 517-token spec went to both. ChatGPT finished in 1 minute 17 seconds on 769 output tokens. Claude took 1 minute 45 seconds and 989 output tokens. Claude reported running 35 of its own test cases before returning the file. Both delivered a download and showed the code in the reply.
The code came out nearly identical, both using exact-precision arithmetic and a fixed-order regex. Claude flagged a judgment call the spec never settles on: that rounding 0.5 seconds up is a choice and Python’s built-in round would go the other way. ChatGPT reported only that its tests passed. Once again, Claude was just a little more thorough.
The handoff
The prompt:
Which of these two stack traces points to a race condition, and in one sentence why? (with the two traces) Then: Now take the file api_logs.csv from my Google Drive (columns: time, endpoint, status, latency_ms) and produce a downloadable spreadsheet with one row per endpoint showing request count, p50, p95, and p99 latency in milliseconds, and error rate as the percentage of requests with status 500 or above. Add a bar chart of p95 latency by endpoint. Also show the table in your reply.
I started each thread in plain chat with the stack-trace question, 135 tokens. Both answered correctly in seconds: Trace B, the dictionary that changed size during iteration. ChatGPT spent about 10 seconds and 48 output tokens. Claude spent 118 in about 25 seconds, adding a caveat that the same error can happen without threads if the loop body edits the dictionary itself. Then, without switching modes, I handed off the log analysis.
Claude pulled the file, computed the table, and built an .xlsx with a p95 bar chart in about 4 minutes on 319 output tokens. ChatGPT produced the same spreadsheet and chart in 28 seconds, using 467 output tokens. All 30 numbers matched my ground truth on both sides. Claude also named its percentile method (linear interpolation) and noted the numbers would match if I recomputed them in Google Sheets. ChatGPT gave the same correct table but didn’t provide as much detail as Claude did.
Results
| The test | ChatGPT (Work mode) | Claude (merged app) | 
| API research | 12/12, 1:17, 125 in / 649 out | 12/12, 1:44, 125 in / 1,042 out | 
| Build from spec | 16/16 tests, 1:17, 517 in / 769 out | 16/16 tests, 1:45, 517 in / 989 out | 
| Handoff, question | Correct, ~10 s, 135 in / 48 out | Correct, ~25 s, 135 in / 118 out | 
| Handoff, task | 30/30, 28 s active, 133 in / 467 out | 30/30, ~4 min, 133 in / 319 out | 
| Total tokens (visible) | 910 in / 1,933 out | 910 in / 2,468 out | 
Both Claude and ChatGPT were equally accurate. Every field, every test case, every number matched on both sides, and both cited real documentation.
The differences are in speed and answer detail. ChatGPT was faster on every task and produced 1,933 visible output tokens, compared with Claude’s 2,468. Some of Claude’s extra output was filler, but not all of it. It added context the prompts didn’t ask for, named the percentile method behind its numbers, and flagged two judgment calls the specs left open. ChatGPT gave the same right answers but with less context.
What do I think?
I’d pick Claude, and here’s the reasoning. On time, ChatGPT won every task, but the gaps were seconds on the short tasks (1:17 vs 1:44, 1:17 vs 1:45), not a noticeable difference. On tokens, ChatGPT used about 22% less output than Claude, which is positive, but not when you consider how important detail/context is.
On detail, Claude provided more meaningful detail on all three tests. This included the extra API context, the rounding judgment call, and the percentile method. In today’s world, where AI can fabricate, detail matters.

articles.title: Shuffling the deck chairs: Xbox continues its "reset" with dramatic restructuring
articles.text:
When Xbox announced sweeping layoffs in July as part of a brutal “reset” for the gaming brand, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said part of the pre-existing problem in the gaming unit was “teams, studios, and functions [that] often operate independently, [making it] harder to work toward a shared goal.” Today, the company announced a radical restructuring of its internal studios that is seemingly designed to reduce that “independence” for the teams behind some of gaming’s biggest franchises.
The biggest apparent change is for the Halo franchise, which will now be under the remit of Call of Duty maker Activision. Halo Studios (formerly 343 Industries), which recently released Halo: Campaign Evolved, will remain as just a “small team” to support the player community, Microsoft said, with the remaining staffing roles eliminated as part of 268 newly announced layoffs.
“For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place,” Activision President Rob Kostich said in a statement provided to Kotaku. “It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community.”
Activision, which Microsoft officially purchased just under three years ago, will now also take control of venerable studio Rare (Sea of Thieves) and the Age of Empires stewards at World’s Edge.

articles.title: Pourquoi le toit solaire à prix d'or d'Elon Musk s'est transformé en fiasco
articles.text:
Il semblerait que ce soit la fin pour les tuiles solaires Solar Roof de Tesla, dix ans après leur apparition. Aucune annonce officielle n’a été faite, mais le site spécialisé Electrek a rapporté le 20 août 2026 que Tesla avait prévenu ses installateurs certifiés que les tuiles n’étaient plus disponibles à la commande
Une source proche du programme évoquant un produit jugé « pas économiquement viable ». Les pages qui lui étaient consacrées ont été discrètement redirigées vers les autres solutions énergétiques de la marque.
Des ventes très loin des ambitions initiales
Peut-être trop ambitieux, Tesla n’est jamais parvenu à atteindre ses objectifs de ventes pour ses tuiles solaires. En 2019, l’entreprise annonçait vouloir atteindre un rythme de 1 000 installations par semaine, mais les résultats ont finalement été très loin de ces prévisions.
En 2022, selon TechCrunch, Tesla installait seulement entre 20 et 40 systèmes par semaine, soit à peine 4 % de l’objectif initial. D’après un rapport du cabinet d’analyse Wood Mackenzie, le toit solaire de Tesla ne représentait que 0,17 % de la capacité solaire résidentielle installée cette année-là.
Le chiffre qui résume tout l’échec tient en un nombre : selon le cabinet Wood Mackenzie, Tesla n’a posé qu’environ 3 000 toits solaires aux États-Unis entre 2016 et début 2023, pour une capacité totale de près de 30 mégawatts. En clair, un produit pensé pour équiper un millier de foyers chaque semaine en aura installé à peine 3 000 en sept ans.
Ces faibles volumes empêchaient surtout Tesla de produire à plus grande échelle et de faire suffisamment baisser ses coûts de production. Contrairement aux panneaux photovoltaïques classiques fabriqués dans des formats standards, le Solar Roof repose sur des composants spécifiques intégrés directement à la toiture. Tesla devait donc investir dans des équipements adaptés à leur fabrication.
Or, lorsque les volumes produits restent faibles, les coûts unitaires deviennent logiquement plus élevés. L’entreprise se retrouvait ainsi dans un cercle vicieux : les coûts de production élevés entraînaient des prix élevés, qui freinaient ensuite les ventes. Un problème d’autant plus difficile à surmonter que dans le même temps, le prix des panneaux photovoltaïques conventionnels chutait fortement.
Le Solar Roof était, certes, présenté comme une solution haut de gamme, mais certains devis atteignaient tout de même des montants exorbitants. Des clients ont rapporté avoir reçu des devis pouvant aller jusqu’à 200 000 dollars (environ 185 000 euros) pour l’installation d’un toit solaire.
Une technologie encore confrontée à des problèmes techniques
Au fil des installations, des clients ont également rapporté plusieurs problèmes techniques. Certains propriétaires ont notamment évoqué une déformation des tuiles sous l’effet de la chaleur.
Les panneaux photovoltaïques classiques sont généralement installés quelques centimètres au-dessus de la toiture, ce qui laisse un espace permettant à l’air de circuler sous les modules et de favoriser leur refroidissement. Les tuiles solaires, en revanche, sont directement intégrées à la couverture du bâtiment. L’espace disponible pour la circulation de l’air est donc beaucoup plus limité.
Cette configuration peut favoriser l’accumulation de chaleur, entraînant la dilatation des matériaux qui entourent les cellules photovoltaïques. Cela pourrait contribuer à certaines déformations rapportées par des propriétaires.
D’autres clients ont également signalé une production d’électricité inférieure à leurs prévisions. La température pourrait aussi être l’un des facteurs en cause, même si elle ne permet pas à elle seule d’expliquer tous les cas de sous-production rapportés.
Tesla ne renonce pas pour autant à l’énergie solaire. Après cet échec du Solar Roof, l’entreprise continue de commercialiser des panneaux photovoltaïques classiques. Elle reste également présente sur le marché du stockage d’énergie, avec ses batteries Megapack destinées aux installations à grande échelle et ses systèmes résidentiels Powerwall, qui sont désormais proposés à la location au Texas.
Pour les quelque 3 000 foyers déjà équipés, l’arrêt ne change rien dans l’immédiat : Tesla assure qu’il honorera la garantie de 25 ans des installations existantes et continuera de fournir des pièces de rechange, la couverture se transmettant même en cas de revente du logement. La vraie inconnue porte sur le long terme, car plusieurs installateurs certifiés doutent de la disponibilité des pièces et redoutent des coûts de réparation élevés pour un produit désormais abandonné.

articles.title: Vast Data launches confidential computing service for sensitive workloads - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Vast Data launches confidential computing service for sensitive workloads
Vast Data Inc. today introduced DataEnclave, a confidential computing environment designed to let companies run advanced artificial intelligence models against sensitive data without exposing either the data or the model’s intellectual property.
DataEnclave is a new capability within the Vast DataEngine and broader Vast AI Operating System that uses Nvidia Corp.’s confidential computing technology to create hardware-isolated environments in which proprietary models and enterprise data can be decrypted and processed securely.
The technology targets financial institutions, healthcare providers, government agencies and other organizations that cannot move regulated or sensitive information to externally hosted AI services. It also addresses model developers’ reluctance to distribute proprietary model weights into infrastructure they do not control.
“Model weights are fast becoming the most valuable intellectual property in the world,” said Jeff Denworth (pictured), Vast Data’s co-founder. “Base weights define the value of frontier models, while fine-tuned weights will increasingly represent the proprietary intelligence of AI-driven enterprises.”
DataEnclave uses trusted execution environments spanning central processing units and graphics processing units. It encrypts guest memory, graphics processing unit memory and NVLink traffic while isolating active models and data from administrators, infrastructure operators and other tenants.
A cryptographic attestation process verifies the hardware, software and governing policies before models or data are decrypted. Enterprises and model developers retain control of their respective encryption keys through integrations with their own key management systems.
“Up until now, there hasn’t been a great solution for ensuring that the memory space that people do this computing in is equally protected,” Denworth said. “Once you get to the final computing destination, is that environment safe enough to actually decrypt the world’s most sensitive data?”
Flexible deployment
DataEnclave can be deployed in customer data centers, AI clouds and fully air-gapped environments. Its attestation services are based on the open-source Cloud Native Computing Foundation Trustee project or can be provided through Fortanix Inc.’s Confidential AI offering.
The system also logs attestation events, key releases and enclave lifecycle activity in the Vast DataBase data warehouse. These records provide an audit trail showing which workloads ran and under what policies without revealing the protected data or model weights.
Initial model and software partners include Cohere Inc., CrowdStrike Holdings Inc., Deepgram Inc., The San Francisco AI Factory Inc., Fundamental Research Labs Inc. and TwelveLabs Inc. Cisco Systems Inc. and Super Micro Computer Inc. are among the hardware partners that will offer integrated systems.
Vast said the model allows a developer’s base weights and a customer’s fine-tuned weights to operate together while remaining under separate ownership and key control. That could help enterprises create customized models without disclosing their proprietary training or operational data to the base-model provider.
“Both of those can interoperate within this multitenant enclave where we can support the trust requirements of both organizations simultaneously,” Denworth said.
Vast is initially concentrating on organizations with particularly strict security and data residency requirements. Denworth identified large banks, intelligence and defense agencies and pharmaceutical companies as early target customers.
“In all three cases, they have said that this solves major pains for them in that they’re not allowed to send certain data products up to different services that they want to use,” he said. “It’s basically the most regulated and air-gapped customers of the world.”
The company also argues that DataEnclave could change the economics of enterprise AI. Customers could run proprietary models on infrastructure they own or select a regional AI cloud, reducing model developers’ need to finance the underlying computing capacity.
For Vast, the capability will be included in the existing AI Operating System rather than sold as a separate product. “We don’t charge anything extra for this,” Denworth said. “It’s just part of the AI operating system stack.”
DataEnclave is available in preview and is scheduled to ship in the first quarter of 2027 through Vast and participating hardware partners, including Cisco and Supermicro.

articles.title: Von neuen Airpods überflüssig gemacht? Apple legt KI-Gadget auf Eis.
articles.text:
KI-Gadget von Apple soll aufs Abstellgleis geraten: Was dazu bekannt ist
Apple legt laut einem Bericht US-Wirtschaftsmagazin Bloomberg die Entwicklung eines KI-Wearable auf Eis. Es handelt sich demnach um einen tragbaren Pin, über den das Portal The Information zuerst im Januar dieses Jahres berichtet hatte.
Wearable von der Größe eines Airtag
Nutzer:innen sollten sich das Gadget, das aus Glas und Aluminium bestehen sollte, entweder an die Kleidung pinnen oder um den Hals hängen können.
Der Durchmesser des Gadgets sollten dem des Airtag entsprechen, aber etwas dicker sein als dieser. Apples 2021 vorgestellter Tracker, mit dem man die Geldbörse oder die Autoschlüssel wiederfinden kann, ist etwa so groß wie eine Zwei-Euro-Münze.
Das sollte der eingestampfte KI-Pin von Apple leisten
In dem Pin waren laut den Plänen von Apple zwei Kameras integriert, ein Standardlinse und ein Weitwinkelobjektiv. Drei Mikrofone sollten Umgebungsgeräusche einfangen.
Die Kameras und die Mikros sollten Informationen über die Umgebung der User:innen an Siri und die KI-Bilderkennung Visual Intelligence weiterleiten. Die Nutzer:innen könnten dann Fragen zu ihrer Umwelt stellen, die Siri über die am Pinn eingebauten Lautsprecher beantwortet. Das Ganze sollte völlig freihändig funktionieren.
Machen neue Airpods den KI-Anhänger überflüssig?
Hauseigene Konkurrenz könnte den eingestampften KI-Pin überflüssig gemacht haben. So sollen die geplanten neuen Airpods von Apple ebenfalls Kameras enthalten, über die sich Nutzer:innen über ihre Umgebung informieren können.
Außerdem sollen laut Bloomberg auch smarte Brillen intern Vorfahrt haben. Ein eigenes Gerät um den Hals hängen oder an den Kragen zu pinnen wäre damit nicht mehr nötig.
Apple konzentriert sich auf Fitnessband
Laut Bloomberg verlagert Apple seinen Fokus von dem Pin weg auf andere Wearables. Hauptsächlich soll es sich dabei um ein Fitnessband ohne Display handeln.
Damit macht Apple etwa dem Armband von Whoop Konkurrenz, das seinen Nutzer:innen Fitnessdaten direkt auf eine Smartphone-App schickt. User:innen der Apple Watch tragen stattdessen ein im Verhältnis zu Whoop klobiges Display am Handgelenk, das viel Akkuleistung frisst. Wie beim Whoop soll es sich beim Apple-Fitnesstracker um ein Stoffband mit Sensor handeln.

articles.title: EU and EIB launch launch institutional investor pact to tackle Europe’s scale-up funding gap | EU-Startups
articles.text:
The European Commission and the European Investment Bank (EIB) Group have launched the European Institutional Investors Pact (EIIP), a new voluntary framework aimed at channelling more long-term institutional capital into Europe’s technology and scale-up ecosystem.
The Pact was unveiled at the TechEU Equity Summit in Luxembourg, with thirteen institutional investors already signalling their intention to invest in Europe’s innovation economy. The commitments are largely expected to come through two existing vehicles: the €15 billion European Tech Champions Initiative (ETCI) 2.0 and the €5 billion Scaleup Europe Fund.
“Talent, ideas and ambition – Europe has all of these. Now we are making sure our innovative companies can grow, scale and lead on the global stage – from Europe. By bringing together public and private partners, the goal is to unlock long-term capital for our technology. This is about turning European innovation into European industrial and economic strength,” said Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission.
The EIIP was developed jointly by the European Commission and the EIB Group as part of the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy. It rests on two complementary pillars: a Policy Dialogue Forum and an Investment Platform.
The Policy Dialogue Forum is led by the Commission, through which institutional investors can engage on regulatory and EU investment policy developments. The Investment Platform, on the other hand, is led by the EIB Group and will give investors access to opportunities across Europe’s venture capital and growth equity ecosystem by sharing investment pipelines, market intelligence, peer exchange and ecosystem insights.
The platform will be built in close cooperation with EU member states and aligned with existing national initiatives, with an eye to facilitating engagement and providing clearer pathways to exit.
The broader goal of the EIIP is to make it easier for pension funds, insurers, banks, and other institutional investors to invest in European venture and growth equity funds, helping fast-growing companies raise the capital they need to scale without having to look outside the bloc.
For years, the European startup ecosystem has struggled to raise late-stage and growth capital, and it has been especially adverse for startups raising rounds above €100 million. With EIIP, the Commission and the EIB aim to address this funding gap and strengthen Europe’s competitiveness in the innovation landscape.
Nadia Calviño, President of the EIB Group, said, “Our goal is clear: to provide Europe’s institutional investors with a single, credible entry point into innovation financing. In today’s world, this partnership between EU institutions and the private sector sends a powerful message of European unity, ambition and determination.”
The 13 investors that have already expressed intent to join the EIIP are targeting large EU-based funds focused on later-stage and growth equity financing, including ETCI 2.0, the Scaleup Europe Fund, and European Investment Fund-backed vehicles under InvestEU.
“What many companies still lack is access to sufficient late-stage capital. With the European Institutional Investors Pact, we are helping connect Europe’s deep pools of long-term capital with its most promising innovators so they can scale up and stay in Europe,” added Ekaterina Zaharieva, Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation.

articles.title: Airbus is using a Steam Deck to drive a Mars rover prototype
articles.text:
Recap: A Steam Deck is being used in testing for the ExoMars rover, giving Airbus engineers a handheld way to control a prototype vehicle in a Mars-like test environment. The experiment shows that Valve's gaming device can also serve as a practical controller for robotics work. For Airbus, it is one example of how accessible PC hardware can be repurposed for specialized testing.
The setup appears in a video from YouTuber Tom Scott, who visited Airbus facilities in the UK to see work on the rover. The project is focused on developing a vehicle that can travel across Mars with a high degree of autonomy. Because signals take too long to travel between Earth and Mars, the rover will need to make manfairbus y navigation decisions on its own using onboard 3D cameras.
That is the eventual goal. During testing on Earth, engineers still need direct control over the rover. In the video, a senior Airbus engineer first uses a laptop to tell a prototype to move forward. Scott later operates another rover with a Steam Deck running custom software. The handheld's sticks, buttons and triggers give him real-time control of the machine.
The video does not explain what software is installed on the Steam Deck or how it is connected to the rover, but it does show why the device can work well in a setting like this. The Steam Deck is essentially a small Linux PC with a built-in display and a full set of physical controls. That makes it more adaptable than a conventional game console and more portable than a laptop-and-controller setup.
The ExoMars use is another example of Valve hardware being put to work outside gaming. Disney operators have also been seen using Steam Decks to control BDX droids at Galaxy's Edge. In both cases, the device appears to be serving as a flexible control interface rather than as part of the robot's main computing system.
Valve's hardware is well suited to that kind of experimentation because it is relatively open. Steam Deck owners can install other programs and operating systems, and the same general approach applies to the company's Steam Machine and Steam Frame devices. Developers are not limited to games sold through the Steam store.
Valve engineer Yazan Aldehayyat made that point in an interview about the Steam Machine. "I don't think it's a coincidence that a good PC is also a good gaming device. At the end of the day, good hardware is good hardware. So in a lot of ways, the challenges you're trying to solve are, a lot of them are pretty much the same."
Valve does not tightly control what owners do with its hardware, which means a Steam Deck can be bought for uses that have nothing to do with Steam games. It can become a robotics controller, a portable development device or a general-purpose Linux computer.
For Airbus, the Steam Deck is not a substitute for the ExoMars rover's autonomous systems. The final rover will have to navigate without live steering from Earth. Its cameras and onboard software will be responsible for identifying terrain and choosing routes across the Martian surface.
The handheld is useful during the development stage, when engineers need to move prototypes, test controls and observe how the rover responds. A physical controller can be quicker and easier to use than a keyboard.

articles.title: The Beats 360 are fun headphones that you can mix and match
articles.text:
For the past couple of weeks, I’ve been using the Beats 360 for my flights and commutes, and I’m impressed by Beats’ newest and flashiest headphones ever.
The audio device is made to be used all the time, whether you’re at the gym or you’re out and about looking fancy. I really appreciate the customizable headphones; you’re able to swap out ear cups and headband cushion, so you can mix and match to your liking.
At first, I was a bit skeptical because I thought swapping would be a pain in the ass. In the past, when companies say that something is easy to swap out, I’ve found it usually isn’t quite so easy. But what I like about the Beats 360 is that they’re kind of idiot proof, and this is what I need: idiot-proof customization options, and I’m pleased.
With a twist, the cups pop off the headphones, and another twist helps you put new colours in. At the top, the headband has little holes on the underside that make it easy to clip the cushion into it. They’re so easy to remove that another tech creator just snatched an earcup when I was wearing the headphones around my neck.
Now, swappable cups alone wouldn’t be exciting, except Beats lets you mix and match colours, and that’s pretty dope. The headphones come in Black, Cloud, Sky and Pink, and of course these all have matching pieces, but there’s also ‘Spark,’ which is like a neon yellow, and Navy, giving you tons of colours to mix and match. There are also leather options in Black and Cloud as well for a night out on the town. My favourite combination is the Black headset with Spark.
The Beats 360 are IPX4 and come with ‘Performance Knit’ cups that allow you to sweat in the earbuds without damaging them. And if your workout is intense, you can easily swap out the cups or the headband cushion. I’m a pretty sweaty dude, so I was able to see that the cups dealt pretty well with sweat.
The Beats 360 feel okay on your head. They’re comfortable after you start wearing them for a while. At least I found the top band a bit tight on my head, but after wearing them for 20 minutes, this feeling goes away. The Performance Knit cushions also use plush memory foam, which might explain why it starts to feel better after some time. Maybe the shape of my head is weird because I found the AirPods Max headphones more comfortable, which people tend to complain about. But the degree of comfort isn’t that bad at all. For instance, I wore them on a seven-hour flight straight, and even fell asleep while wearing them.
The Beats 360 sound great; Beats said they improved the active noise cancellation from the Beats Studio. It’s pretty good at shutting out most noise without needing to raise the volume too loud. Airplane and subway sounds disappear completely; however, the high-pitched sound of a baby crying made it through. The baby was an aisle over on a two-aisle plane, but it wasn’t like I could 100 per cent tell what I was hearing at first. I just thought it was a sound in the background of my show. I was watching Secret Lives of Mormon Wives; all these women have babies, but when I removed the headphones, it was like, “Oh, this baby isn’t on my show, and is pretty loud.”
The Beats 360 offers rich sound with immersive audio. I played music and watched media for hours, and it all sounds great. It also has Adaptive EQ, which adjusts acoustic frequencies based on the fit. Plus, there’s Personalized Spatial Audio with head tracking and Dolby Atmos, with a built-in accelerometer and gyroscope for head tracking.
When I was testing audio, I picked songs like Middle Child by J.Cole, Another One Bites the Dust by Queen, Humble by Kendrick Lamar, and We Are Young, which are pretty different songs, but also the same ones I used to test Apple’s AirPods Max 2. It’s pretty interesting comparing the two headphones; both sound good and are immersive. Strangely, I think the Beats 360 are even louder than the AirPods Max 2, but loudness isn’t everything.
I found that Middle Child had a bit of a punch to the bass that was a little bit overwhelming (though I was playing the music at the loudest volume to compare), which isn’t something I hear with the AirPods Max 2. Other songs like Another One Bites the Dust and Humble sounded very similar on the two headsets; voices are clear and precise, so you can hear harmonies very well. For instance, there’s a very quiet harmony in We Are Young that’s slightly delayed, like an echo, that I can hear pretty well between both headsets.
However, the experience between the two headphones for We Are Young is interesting. I think the instrumentals are stronger on the AirPods Max 2, as it feels like We Are Young is a huge production, whereas on the Beats 360, you can hear a lot, but it sounds a bit lacking. But again, I definitely needed to keep the volume on max to hear the difference.
One thing I found a little weird: when you take off the headphones, your media doesn’t auto-pause. Also, the Beats 360 work on both Android and iOS, but you need to download the Beats app on Android, while on iOS, it just works and you can control the headphones via your settings, similar to any AirPods.
I enjoyed the Beats 360 headphones, but definitely my favourite thing was the customizable cushions and the variety of colours they come in. Although I noted that there weren’t any red options, which feels like a miss considering it’s Beats. The Beats 360 costs $479.95, and the cushion kit costs $74.95. However, until October 31, you can grab different cushion kits for $14.99, which I think is a sick introductory offer that I might take advantage of — I love mixing and matching.

articles.title: Hacking group ShinyHunters claims it breached the FBI, stole agents' and applicants' data | TechCrunch
articles.text:
ShinyHunters, a prolific cybercriminal group known for large-scale data theft and extortion, says it has breached the FBI and stolen data on thousands of agents and applicants. The hackers made the claim on their dark web leak site, which TechCrunch reviewed, saying they had stolen “sensitive data on almost all FBI agents and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job.”
404 Media first reported on the breach after receiving a sample of the stolen names, home addresses, and phone numbers of FBI agents and their spouses, and verifying a portion of the stolen data against public records. The hackers say their hack is “not financially motivated,” and are demanding that the FBI remove a report that they say contains false allegations about the group.
The independent publication said the hackers breached an Oracle PeopleSoft server, often used by human resources and recruiters to store job applicants’ personal information, then pivoted to breach an Amazon-hosted government cloud storing the agents and applicants’ data.
ShinyHunters told the publication that they took terabytes of data but did not say what they would do with the information if the FBI does not take down its published report. The stolen data could present a major counterintelligence threat, in which hackers and overseas spies use the information to coerce or extort FBI agents and their families into cooperating with a foreign government.
The hackers reportedly defaced the FBI’s jobs site, which showed at the time of publication that the portal was “currently down for maintenance.” The site also said that the FBI’s special agent applicant portal was also down.
An FBI spokesperson told TechCrunch: “The FBI is aware of claims regarding unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov and is currently investigating.” When reached by TechCrunch, the ShinyHunters hackers did not say how many people had their information taken, but said that they are “very confident we have data on mostly all of FBI,” and that “a substantial amount of applicants data [is] involved as well.”
This is the second known breach of an FBI system this year after unidentified hackers broke into one of the agency’s systems for managing real-time wiretaps and foreign intelligence-gathering warrants, which could have identified targets of the agency’s surveillance. Separately, FBI director Kash Patel also had his personal email account hacked and leaked by an Iran-backed hacking group called Handala in retaliation for U.S.-led strikes against Iran.
Updated with comment from FBI and ShinyHunters.

articles.title: Apple quiere plantarle cara a Whoop con una pulsera que no tiene pantalla
articles.text:
Apple está trabajando en una nueva pulsera de acondicionamiento físico que competirá directamente con Whoop. Según reporta el periodista Mark Gurman, los de Cupertino llevan meses desarrollando diversos prototipos, por lo que su llegada sería inminente. El proyecto ha sido respaldado por el mismo Tim Cook, antiguo CEO que cedió la dirección de la compañía a John Ternus.
De acuerdo con Bloomberg, la Apple Band sería una pulsera fitness sin pantalla muy parecida a lo que ya ofrece Whoop. Aunque el proyecto se encuentra en sus primeros pasos, el equipo ya pasó de la fase de ideas al desarrollo de prototipos funcionales. En esta fase, conocida internamente como investigación tecnológica, los ingenieros de Cupertino evalúan el desempeño de los prototipos para saber si pueden materializarse en un dispositivo final.
En términos de diseño, la banda está fabricada en tela fina e incluye un módulo con sensores. A diferencia del Apple Watch, esta pulsera no incluye pantalla y se enfoca solo en lo esencial, por lo que no competirán entre sí. El reloj inteligente cuenta con muchas funciones que ayudan al acondicionamiento físico, pero Apple busca algo más discreto, sin distracciones, y que pueda usarse en el día a día como la Whoop.
Aunque Tim Cook y Eddy Cue apoyan esta pulsera de fitness, no existe garantía de que se convertirá en un producto. Si la empresa decide seguir adelante, la Apple Band no se lanzará antes de 2028. Los de Cupertino tienen que evaluar más a fondo el desempeño y saber si se puede integrar con sus servicios, así como también sortear otros problemas como los que ocurren con la cadena de producción por culpa de la IA.
Apple no quiere depender solo del Apple Watch
Una pulsera inteligente hace sentido para Apple, sobre todo si consideramos el avance de Whoop en este campo. A diferencia del Apple Watch, que incluye todas las funciones y seguimiento de acondicionamiento físico, una pulsera con sensores como la de Whoop funciona a través de una suscripción. Aquí el usuario paga una tarifa mensual por comprar el dispositivo a menor coste y con acceso total a la plataforma.
Este esquema de suscripción garantizaría una entrada de dinero constante para Apple, algo que no obtiene cuando alguien compra el Apple Watch. Debido a que se trata de una membresía, la compañía "amarra" al usuario por un año o el tiempo que elija para pagar el dispositivo. Este mismo modelo lo aplica Oura, el anillo inteligente que registra tus métricas de sueño, ritmo cardíaco y otros valores de salud.
Una evidencia que anticipa la llegada de esta pulsera es que Apple ya comenzó a incorporar funciones al estilo Whoop en su app de Salud. Entre las novedades encontramos un seguimiento más preciso de tu frecuencia cardiaca y un modo que analiza tu nivel de preparación física para el día a día. Además, la app estrenó una nueva interfaz de usuario más limpia y accesible, inspirada en lo que ofrecen sus principales rivales.
Con la apuesta por la pulsera inteligente, Apple ha puesto el freno a otro ambicioso proyecto con IA. Gurman menciona que la compañía pausó el desarrollo de un colgante inteligente equipado con cámara e impulsado por la nueva Siri. Este wearable podría visualizar tu entorno y responder preguntas de un modo parecido a un asistente inteligente como el que vimos en la película Her.
Por el momento no se sabe si este proyecto retomará su desarrollo o si quedará archivado, sobre todo después del fiasco del AI Pin de Humane.

articles.title: Google Adds Cycle-Level Kernel Profiling to XProf
articles.text:
Google has added a Kernel Profiling suite to XProf. This is its open-source profiler for TPU workloads. Now, developers can see cycle-level details in custom Pallas kernels. Before, these kernels appeared as single opaque blocks in trace captures. On TPU v7 (Ironwood), XProf samples hardware performance counters during runtime. In a tiled matmul example, Google found a memory stall. They cut kernel time from 125.5µs to 88µs, about 30%, by adding triple buffering.
According to Yogesh SY of Google's AI Infra team, the gap comes from how profilers treat custom compilation paths. Kernels made with Pallas, Mosaic, or Triton skip standard XLA passes. This can distort the compile-time static cost models. As a result, metrics like "optimal FLOPs" and goodput efficiency may be inaccurate or not work at all. A static tool can flag an MXU instruction block as fully utilized while the unit sits idle waiting on HBM, because static analysis ignores time.
The suite works at three levels. Developers pass these flags for compiler inspection: --xla_enable_custom_call_region_trace=true and --xla_xprof_register_llo_debug_info=true. After this, the Graph Viewer displays a "Custom Call Text" panel. It shows the lowered MLIR for each custom call.
This lets engineers check whether operations are fused and memory tiles are structured as intended. The Trace Viewer shows Low-Level Operations (LLO) bundle data for static execution analysis. This data includes machine instructions per clock cycle. It presents time-aligned tracks for the MXU, scalar and vector ALUs, vector fills, loads, spills, stores, and the cross-lane unit (XLU). For runtime telemetry, XProf samples hardware counters periodically, with a 1µs resolution floor driven by a host-level timer.
A new external event-triggered mode removes that floor. The sampler captures TPU trace instructions and boundary triggers. These include the entry and exit of custom call scopes. This enables sub-microsecond capture and improved attribution. Developers can configure up to 28 counters per core across up to four SparseCores, a 4x28 matrix. Collection is enabled through jax.profiler.ProfileOptions, using tpu_enable_periodic_counter_sampling and tpu_tc_perf_counter_sampling_options with is_external_trigger:true. For periodic mode, interval_us replaces the trigger flag.
In the matmul case study, a memory-bound variant showed large spikes in sync_wait counters. Overlapping HBM loads with MXU compute through triple buffering reduced those events and produced the 125.5µs to 88µs improvement. The figure comes from a single Google-authored demo kernel, not a broad benchmark, so it shows the workflow rather than the gains to expect elsewhere.
The post also sets out a "hierarchy of trust" for metrics. Values read directly from hardware registers, such as HBM utilization and TPO metrics, count as ground truth for custom kernels, while XLA cost-model estimates need caution. A new Perf Counters View lists over 16,000 raw counters in tabular form. Trace track height reflects the maximum raw counter value in an interval, not a normalized percentage. For example, an increment of 100 cycles over a 500ns window on a roughly 2.0 GHz core equals 10% utilization of that unit.
XProf is part of the OpenXLA project and integrates with JAX profiling. The post does not state a release status or version for the Kernel Profiling suite.
The counter sampling is documented for TPU v7 (Ironwood), so teams on earlier TPU generations should not assume the same coverage. Anyone tuning Pallas kernels can start with the Pallas Matmul with Perf Counters notebook in the XProf repository and the OpenXLA kernel profiling instructions. The limited 4x28 counter budget requires teams to pick counters for each investigation. The setup aims to safeguard workload performance. Engineers should also stop treating XLA-derived efficiency numbers as reliable for custom kernels and anchor optimization on register-level counters instead.

articles.title: Make Your Interface Work For Your AI SoC—A 10 Step Program: Verification With Simulation
articles.text:
Best practices for reducing integration risk, shortening verification schedules, and improving productivity when deploying third-party interface IP in AI and heterogeneous SoC architectures.
As AI SoCs integrate increasingly complex combinations of processors, accelerators, memory subsystems, and high-speed interfaces, verification challenges extend well beyond functional correctness. Modern designs must validate system integration, software interactions, interoperability, and performance across highly configurable third-party IP environments. This white paper explores how simulation-based verification helps engineering teams identify integration issues early and accelerate development cycles.
The paper examines the evolving role of Verification IP (VIP), Test Groups, and SoC Verification Kits (SVKs) in modern semiconductor verification flows. Readers will learn how these solutions provide protocol expertise, reusable verification content, and pre-integrated test environments that reduce integration risk, improve verification efficiency, and enable consistent validation from early RTL development through system-level verification.

articles.title: Five35 Ventures completes 1st portfolio exit, generates 3.5x return from Complete Farmer investment - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Five35 Ventures, an Africa-focused, gender-lens investment vehicle backed by the Mastercard Foundation Africa Growth Fund, has completed its first portfolio exit, generating a 3.5x multiple on invested capital in Ghanaian agri-tech company Complete Farmer.
The Africa Growth Fund is a US$200 million fund-of-funds designed to strengthen African-led, women-led investment vehicles and enable them to invest in businesses with the potential to contribute to inclusive growth and job creation.
Rather than investing directly in individual companies, the fund works through investment vehicles such as Five35 Ventures, supporting the managers and strategies that can channel capital to promising businesses across the continent.
Five35 Ventures invested in Complete Farmer, which connects farmers to markets while providing access to agricultural inputs and technical support, in April 2022, and exited in March 2026. During the investment period, the company’s valuation increased from US$6 million to US$49 million, resulting in a 3.5x return for Five35 Ventures, and a 38 per internal rate of return over four years.
The firm said the exit was a meaningful milestone and proof point of the commercial potential of both Five35 Ventures’ and the Africa Growth Fund’s investment strategy. Five35 Ventures’ gender-lens approach looks beyond ownership and leadership to consider how women participate in and benefit from the businesses it backs, whether as employees, suppliers, customers or participants in the wider value chain.
“At Five35, we look for businesses in which commercial growth and inclusive impact reinforce one another. Complete Farmer shows how technology can strengthen African food systems, improve farmers’ access to markets and create meaningful economic opportunities for women,” said Hema Vallabh, general partner at Five35 Ventures.
“Achieving this result through our first exit is an important validation of our investment strategy. As we continue backing Africa’s next generation of technology-enabled businesses, this exit strengthens our conviction that gender-lens investing is not a concessionary strategy, it is a disciplined way of identifying overlooked markets, stronger business models and new sources of sustainable value.”

articles.title: Nokia 1100 es el celular más vendido de la historia: cuánto cuesta hoy y por qué regresó en 2026
articles.text:
Un Nokia 1100 usado se ofrece desde 25 hasta 40 dólares en publicaciones de segunda mano en eBay, según su estado. El modelo, lanzado en 2003, fue el celular más vendido de la historia tras alcanzar 250 millones de unidades en seis años, según un estudio de Visual Capitalist basado en datos de Yahoo Finance y Omdia.
El Nokia 1100 volvió a estar en el centro de la conversación por el lanzamiento del Nokia 300 Charge, un celular básico de HMD Global que recupera parte de la propuesta del dispositivo original: batería de larga duración, diseño resistente y funciones centradas en lo esencial.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué fue tan popular el Nokia 1100
La autonomía fue uno de sus principales atributos. Su batería extraíble de ion de litio BL-5C tenía una capacidad de 850 mAh y un voltaje de 3,7 V: ofrecía hasta 400 horas en modo de espera y unas 4,5 horas de conversación continua.
Con un uso moderado, una sola carga podía durar más de una semana. La pantalla monocromática y el sistema operativo básico reducían el consumo de energía frente a los teléfonos actuales.
También incluía linterna, despertador, recordatorios, calculadora y juegos preinstalados como Snake, conocido como viborita o culebrita. Su carcasa robusta, los bordes antideslizantes y el teclado protegido por una alfombrilla de silicona ayudaban a que el equipo resistiera el uso cotidiano.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué características tiene el Nokia 300 Charge
El Nokia 300 Charge incorpora una batería extraíble de 3.700 mAh que, según HMD Global, ofrece más de 40 días en modo de espera con una sola carga. El dispositivo no tiene acceso a internet, cámaras de alta resolución ni un ecosistema de aplicaciones.
El equipo cuenta con una pantalla de 2,4 pulgadas, con resolución de 320 x 240 píxeles, y utiliza un procesador Unisoc SC6531E. Tiene 4 MB de RAM, 4 MB de almacenamiento interno y admite tarjetas microSD de hasta 32 GB.
Su conectividad se limita a redes 2G GSM 900/1800, por lo que depende de que esa tecnología continúe disponible en cada región. Además, integra una linterna LED, jack de 3,5 mm para radio FM y carga inversa por USB-C de 10 W mediante un botón físico lateral. Por ahora, solo está disponible en Filipinas.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuál fue el segundo celular más vendido
Según una recopilación publicada por Statista, basada en datos de Visual Capitalist, Yahoo Finance y Omdia, los otros celulares más vendidos han sido:
1. Nokia 1100 (2003): 250 millones de unidades.
2. Nokia 1110 (2005): 248 millones de unidades.
3. iPhone 6 y 6 Plus (2014): 222 millones de unidades.
4. Nokia 105: 200 millones de unidades.
5. iPhone 6s y 6s Plus: 174 millones de unidades.
6. iPhone 5s: 165 millones de unidades.
7. Nokia 3220: 161 millones de unidades.
8. iPhone 7 y 7 Plus: 160 millones de unidades.
Cómo fue el lanzamiento del primer iPhone
El primer iPhone fue presentado por Steve Jobs el 9 de enero de 2007 durante la conferencia Macworld, en San Francisco. Apple lo definió como la combinación de tres productos en un solo dispositivo: un teléfono móvil, un iPod con pantalla ancha y controles táctiles, y una herramienta de comunicación por internet con correo electrónico, navegador, buscador y mapas.
PUBLICIDAD
Durante la presentación, Jobs explicó que el equipo se controlaba con los dedos mediante una pantalla multitáctil. El modelo también incorporaba un teclado virtual, una función que reemplazaba los teclados físicos habituales en los celulares de la época.
El lanzamiento comercial ocurrió el 29 de junio de 2007 en Estados Unidos. Apple puso a la venta dos versiones: una con 4 GB de almacenamiento por USD 499 y otra con 8 GB por USD 599. Los equipos se distribuyeron en tiendas Apple, en la tienda online de la compañía y en locales seleccionados de AT&T.
El primer iPhone requería un contrato de servicio de dos años con AT&T para su activación. Además, podía sincronizar contactos, música, videos y otros contenidos mediante iTunes en una computadora Mac o PC.

articles.title: After Tatas, succession test at another family-linked company
articles.text:
Succession test at Hikal; Nothing spins off CMF as majority Indian-owned company
At Hikal’s AGM on September 23, shareholders will vote on Sameer Hiremath’s five-year term as CMD. The Hiremath and Kalyani sides hold nearly identical 34% stakes, while proxy advisers are split over the move.
Dear Reader,
Weeks after the Tata Sons boardroom dispute put questions of succession, shareholder power, and board authority in focus, another family-linked corporate contest is heading to a key vote.
Hikal shareholders will vote on Wednesday on Sameer Hiremath’s five-year term as chairman and managing director, with the Hiremath and Kalyani sides holding near-identical stakes of about 34% each. The vote comes amid a decades-old ownership dispute, while proxy advisers are split on his elevation.
Meanwhile, India’s startup IPO pipeline is getting busier, and ecommerce and mobility are joining the party. Snapdeal parent AceVector is set to hit the public markets this week, while used-car marketplace Spinny has filed confidential IPO papers, reportedly looking to raise up to Rs 3,000 crore. Two very different consumer businesses, but both signal how India’s startup story is moving deeper into the public markets.
The expansion story is playing out overseas too. PhonePe is taking its payments overseas by securing in-principle approval from the UAE central bank for two payment licences. The fintech plans to integrate with the UAE’s Aani and Jaywan payment rails once it receives final regulatory approval.
And then there’s AI, where the debate is getting louder. DeepSeek is set to brief the UN Security Council this week on AI risks as world leaders gather in New York for the UN General Assembly. The meeting comes amid growing calls from AI leaders for a coordinated slowdown in developing increasingly powerful systems over concerns about human control.
But not everyone sees a doomsday scenario. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has dismissed predictions that AI could become “superhuman” and cause human extinction within the next few years, calling such claims exaggerated. He also criticised former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon’s warnings about AI risks as “irresponsible.”
In other news, Nothing is spinning off its CMF sub-brand into a standalone, majority-Indian-owned company headquartered in India, with its own local team and R&D operations. The move signals a shift from simply assembling devices in India to building more design, technology and IP locally.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- MP Shashank Mani on NEET, India’s growth, and entrepreneurship
- Empowering young women leaders in rural Himachal
Here’s your trivia for today: In which year did Apple introduce the Lightning cable to standardise its chargers? (Scroll down for the answer)
Interview
MP Shashank Mani on NEET, India’s growth, and entrepreneurship
The 2026 NEET crisis has reopened a larger question about how India measures success, and what comes after the exam. In a conversation with Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, Shashank Mani Tripathi, BJP MP from Deoria and Founder of Jagriti Yatra, connects education, entrepreneurship, and India’s demographic opportunity.
Key takeaways:
- Tripathi argues that failure in an examination should not define a young person’s potential, calling for greater emphasis on skilling, sports and entrepreneurship alongside formal education.
- He points to defence and space, agriculture, women-led enterprise and small-town urbanisation as areas with room for entrepreneurial growth.
- Through Amrit Prayas and his proposed “Banyan Revolution”, Tripathi is working to build enterprise hubs beyond major cities, with plans spanning Deoria, Kanyakumari, Ganjam and Nagpur.
Social Impact
Empowering young women leaders in rural Himachal
In rural Himachal, Enlightened India Foundation is helping girls move from the classroom to the community. Its approach combines education, digital safety and civic engagement to build confidence—and create young women leaders.
Key takeaways:
- The foundation runs learning sessions in subjects such as maths, English, science and coding, alongside sports and life skills programmes.
- The foundation has reached 3,500 children across 46 villages, with girls making up 70% of those reached. Five village-level women leaders now run programmes in their communities.
- EIF’s women leaders conduct surveys, document issues such as poor infrastructure and digital-safety risks, and take their findings to government departments and local authorities.
News & updates
- Cricket: India’s women’s cricket team clinched its second successive Asian Games gold, beating Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final. Led by Harmanpreet Kaur, India scored 216, setting Sri Lanka a record target of 217.
- Indian founders: Founders who grew up in India account for an estimated $560 billion in founder-share-attributed value across current and former unicorns abroad, according to Prosus and Dealroom.
In which year did Apple introduce the Lightning cable to standardise its chargers?

articles.title: Beats releases its first customisable headphones with improved audio performance - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Hip audio brand Beats has released its first customizable over-ear headphones with interchangeable ear and headband cushions while still offering its best audio performance.
Priced at $499.95 and available from September 24, the Beats 360 headphones come in four core colours: Black, Cloud, Pink and Sky, along with matching performance knit earcups and headband cushions.
There are also Performance Knit and UltraPlush cushions available to purchase separately for $14.95 in a range of colours and offer exceptional comfort, added stability, and durability.
And of course they have an impressive sound thanks to an all-new acoustic platform and proprietary drivers, which offer Beats’ most advanced audio performance ever.
Beats has also improved Active Noise Cancellation with up to 1.75x more ANC than Beats Studio Pro.
It also has Transparency Mode and Adaptive EQ.
The Beats 360 over-ear headphones have a redesigned fit and finish with a refined architecture and IPX4 sweat and water resistance.
Under the hood is the custom Beats chip, which has native support for Apple features like Find My and audio sharing.
It also has Android Fast Pair and Find Hub compatibility.
On the battery side the Beats 360 will run for up to 32 hours, with Fast Fuel offering one hour of playback from a quick 5-minute charge.
Beats 360 will be available to order now from apple.com/au.

articles.title: 403 millions d’euros : Google écope d'une amende pour avoir exploité vos données de localisation
articles.text:
L’autorité irlandaise chargée de superviser Google au niveau européen a condamné l’entreprise américaine à une amende de 403 millions d’euros pour plusieurs manquements liés à l’utilisation des données de géolocalisation de ses utilisateurs. Il s’agit de la quatrième plus importante amende jamais infligée par cette autorité. En juillet dernier, Google avait déjà écopé d’une amende record de 890 millions d’euros, infligée cette fois-ci par la Commission européenne.
Google condamné à une amende de 403 millions d’euros
La Commission irlandaise de protection des données (DPC) a condamné Google à une amende de 403 millions d’euros pour sa gestion des données de géolocalisation de ses utilisateurs. Il s’agit de la quatrième plus importante amende jamais infligée par l’autorité irlandaise chargée de superviser Google au niveau européen. Pour être plus précis, la DPC estime que l’entreprise américaine a fait preuve de plusieurs manquements liés à l’utilisation des données de géolocalisation de ses utilisateurs et a ainsi enfreint les règles européennes (RGPD).
Graham Doyle, commissaire adjoint de la DPC, explique : « En raison des manquements de Google à cet égard, des individus auraient pu ignorer que leur géolocalisation était utilisée, par exemple, pour les influencer avec des publicités ou pour déduire leurs centres d’intérêt, et pouvaient perdre le contrôle de leurs données à caractère personnel ». Google aurait donc utilisé les données de géolocalisation de certains de ses utilisateurs à des fins publicitaires, sans que ceux-ci ne soient suffisamment informés.
L’entreprise américaine plaide la mise en conformité
Cette affaire a été ouverte en 2020 à la suite de plaintes déposées par plusieurs associations de consommateurs européennes. Les faits reprochés à Google se sont déroulés entre 2018 et 2020. Google ne réfute pas les accusations, mais explique s’être conformé à la réglementation européenne dès 2019. L’entreprise américaine a déclaré : « Cette affaire porte sur des règles historiques qui ont depuis été mises à jour. À partir de 2019, nous avons considérablement fait évoluer nos pratiques et lancé des outils robustes qui simplifient la gestion des données de localisation ».
Quoi qu’il en soit, Google est définitivement dans le viseur de l’Union européenne. En juillet dernier, l’UE avait condamné l’entreprise américaine à une amende record de 890 millions d’euros pour violation du Digital Markets Act. À cela s’ajoute maintenant une nouvelle amende de 403 millions d’euros.

articles.title: YouTube : cette vieille astuce légale et gratuite permet toujours de se débarrasser des pubs
articles.text:
YouTube : cette vieille astuce légale et gratuite permet toujours de se débarrasser des pubs
Saviez-vous qu'une astuce vieille de plusieurs années pour profiter de YouTube sans publicité fonctionne toujours ? Et que celle-ci est gratuite, légale, et ne repose pas sur un bloqueur de publicité ?
Depuis plusieurs années, Google fait son maximum pour que les utilisateurs de YouTube succombent à un abonnement Premium. Au-delà de réserver certaines fonctionnalités aux abonnés, la guerre contre les bloqueurs de publicité, toujours plus envahissante, fait toujours rage. Il est ainsi régulièrement difficile de trouver une solution qui fonctionne correctement, qui ne laisse pas passer des annonces ou qui n'empêche pas le bon fonctionnement de la plateforme.
Pour les utilisateurs qui en ont assez de devoir changer de navigateur (certains proposent des bloqueurs intégrés), d'extensions, d'applications tierces ou encore de DNS régulièrement, il existe une autre méthode.
YouTube a un mode sans pub pour les développeurs
Déjà évoquée il y a plusieurs années et étrangement toujours fonctionnelle, cette astuce se destine initialement aux développeurs pour leur permettre d'intégrer confortablement des vidéos sur leur site en passant par le mode confidentialité avancé de YouTube. Ce dernier désactive de nombreux scripts et fonctions de la plateforme, empêche la collecte de cookies et bloque la publicité pour profiter d'une expérience fluide et sans gêne.
Le plus beau, c'est qu'aucune connaissance de développeur n'est nécessaire pour en profiter : dans l'URL de la vidéo en cours, il suffit d'ajouter un tiret ( - ) entre le "t" et le "u" de YouTube, ce qui donne : www.yout-ube.com/blablabla. Cela fonctionne aussi avec les live streams et les Shorts, mais aussi avec les URL mobiles (m.yout-ube.com) et de YouTube Music (music.yout-ube.com).
Après avoir appuyé sur Entrée, l'utilisateur est alors redirigé vers la page youtube-nocookie.com, où la vidéo s'affiche désormais en plein écran, sans publicité et sans recommandations. Si l'URL yout-ube.com n'est pas officielle et propriété de Google (la sécurité des utilisateurs est évoquée ici), elle ne fait que rediriger vers un outil lui tout à fait officiel de la firme.
Une méthode efficace, mais avec des contraintes
Comme vous l'aurez probablement déjà deviné, cette méthode a cependant un inconvénient : elle ne fonctionne que sur la version web de YouTube, et donc principalement sur ordinateur et dans certains navigateurs sur mobile. Pas question de pouvoir modifier l'URL depuis l'application sur TV ou smartphone, application qui se lance automatiquement quand une URL YouTube est détectée.
Enfin, certains se posent probablement à raison la question d'automatiser ce processus. Voilà qui tombe bien, puisqu'un développeur a créé deux scripts à installer via l'extension User JavaScript and CSS pour cela. Une fois tout cela installé, plus besoin de modifier l'URL à la main, chaque vidéo s'ouvrira dans un nouvel onglet avec l'interface simplifiée et sans publicité.

articles.title: En fin de cycle, la Nintendo Switch avec Mario Kart 8 Deluxe passe sous les 200€
articles.text:
La Nintendo Switch est une console hybride entre la console de salon et la console portable. Pour ceux qui sont passés à côté en dix ans, elle est désormais disponible pour 199,99 euros.
La Nintendo Switch approche de sa fin. Pour écouler ses stocks, Nintendo sort le grand jeu puisqu’elle passe la console sous les 200 euros. Pour convaincre encore plus de monde, la marque offre Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. Même en 2026, la Nintendo Switch reste intéressante puisque le catalogue de jeux est complet, mais il faut bien avoir en tête qu’il ne va plus être renouvelé.
Sortie en 2017 pour 330 euros, la Nintendo Switch est maintenant disponible pour 199,99 euros
Pourquoi choisir la Nintendo Switch ?
- Des performances hybrides : C’était la promesse de Nintendo : offrir une console de salon qui soit aussi portable. La marque japonaise réussit sa mission avec une console qui peut se jouer sur un téléviseur ou dans les transports en commun
- Un design compact : La Nintendo Switch se glisse facilement dans un sac à dos et sa béquille au dos permet de poser l’écran sur une surface plane et de jouer avec les joy-cons en main.
- Mario Kart 8 Deluxe : Il s’agit de l’un des meilleurs titres sortis sur la console et permet de passer de bonnes soirées entre amis.
Le meilleur des deux mondes
Après la Wii U, Nintendo a sorti sa Nintendo Switch en 2017 avec une promesse : proposer un produit qui est une console portable, mais aussi une console de salon. Ainsi, la Nintendo Switch se présente avec un dock pour jouer sur un téléviseur en 1080p.
Si vous partez en déplacement, la console peut s’emporter pour jouer en 720p. Même dans ce format portable, la console reste hybride. Elle peut se jouer comme une PSP pour pouvoir jouer au fond de votre lit. Néanmoins, à l’arrière de la console, il y a une béquille pour poser l’écran sur une petite table et jouer directement avec les Joy-Con dans les mains.
Deux bémols sont à noter sur la partie portable : la luminosité n’est pas éblouissante et les reflets sont nombreux. Deuxième point : l’autonomie est restreinte et ne dépassera que légèrement les cinq heures.
Une Nintendo Switch en 2026, vraiment ?
La Nintendo Switch va bientôt souffler sa dixième bougie. Depuis, plusieurs itérations sont sorties avec une version Lite et OLED. La Nintendo Switch 2 a même vu le jour en juin 2025. Une question vient alors logiquement se poser : pourquoi choisir la Nintendo Switch ? Deux éléments permettent de répondre. D’abord, il y a le prix. Grâce à cette offre, la console passe sous les 200 euros et devient vraiment attractive puisque la version OLED dépasse toujours les 300 euros.
L'’autre point fort, c’est Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. Il s’agit de l’un des meilleurs titres sortis sur la console. Ce jeu convient à toute la famille, dont les enfants qui pourraient s’occuper pendant plusieurs heures à rouler sur les nombreux circuits disponibles. Ce n’est pas le seul classique de la console puisque vous pourrez toujours essayer Zelda : Breath of the Wild.
Cependant, ce prix n'est pas un cadeau de Nintendo. La marque cherche à vider ses stocks puisque la console est en fin de vie. Preuve en est, les derniers titres de la firme nipponne ne sortent plus sur la première version de cette Nintendo Switch.
✅ Les points forts
- Le format hybride entre console portable et console de salon
- Point fort concret et factuel
- Mario Kart 8 Deluxe offert
❌ Les limites
- Pas d’écran OLED
- Une console en fin de cycle
Sortie en 2017 pour 330 euros, la Nintendo Switch est maintenant disponible pour 199,99 euros
La Nintendo Switch s’adresse ainsi aux collectionneurs, mais aussi à ceux qui cherchent une première console pour leurs enfants à un prix abordable. Malgré le poids des années, la Nintendo Switch reste encore performante surtout avec Mario Kart 8 Deluxe offert. En outre, la console permet d’accéder à de nombreux titres, dont les récents remakes des premiers jeux Pokémon.

articles.title: Adobe Patches Critical Flaws in Connect, AEM Forms
articles.text:
Adobe on Tuesday rolled out patches for 36 vulnerabilities across its products, including critical-severity flaws in Connect and Experience Manager (AEM) Forms.
The Adobe Connect update resolves nine security defects, including six critical issues that could be exploited for arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation.
Tracked as CVE-2026-75682, CVE-2026-75684, CVE-2026-75686, CVE-2026-75689, CVE-2026-75697, and CVE-2026-75698, they are described as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and improper input validation flaws.
The update also fixes high-severity path traversal, improper certificate validation, and XSS weaknesses that could lead to arbitrary file system read, security feature bypass, and arbitrary code execution.
Adobe patched six vulnerabilities in AEM Forms, including three critical-severity flaws leading to code execution and privilege escalation.
Described as incorrect authorization, improper input validation, and server-side request forgery (SSRF), the critical issues are tracked as CVE-2026-75745, CVE-2026-81995, and CVE-2026-82000.
The AEM Forms patches also fix three high-severity SSRF, XSS, and cross-site request forgery (CSRF) bugs leading to privilege escalation, code execution, and security feature bypass.
Both security updates have a priority 2 rating, meaning that users should apply them within the next 30 days.
On Tuesday, Adobe also announced fixes for multiple high- and medium-severity vulnerabilities in InDesign, Content Credentials SDK, Bridge, Substance 3D Modeler, and Premiere Pro.
Successful exploitation of these security defects could lead to application denial-of-service (DoS), security feature bypass, arbitrary code execution, and memory exposure.
Adobe says it is not aware of any of these security flaws being exploited in the wild. Additional information is available on the company’s security bulletins page.

articles.title: Ryuk ransomware member sentenced to 24 months in prison
articles.text:
An Armenian man was sentenced to 24 months in prison and 3 years of supervised release for hacking U.S. companies and encrypting their systems in Ryuk ransomware attacks.
35-year-old Karen Serobovich Vardanyan (also known online as "Maneeken" or "Karl Lagerfeld"), who specialized in gaining initial access to corporate networks, pleaded guilty in July after being extradited from Kyiv, Ukraine, following his April 2025 arrest.
According to court documents, Vardanyan hacked into the networks of multiple U.S. organizations in Ryuk ransomware attacks between March 2019 and approximately June 2020.
In one of these attacks, Vardanyan and his accomplices breached a Michigan company that paid 200 BTC (worth over $1.1 million at the time). Prosecutors also said the cybercriminals breached a school in Texas and a technology company in Wilsonville, Oregon.
"Vardanyan and his co-conspirators illegally accessed computer networks of victim companies and deployed ransomware on hundreds of compromised servers and workstations," the U.S. Department of Justice said in July.
"Vardanyan and his co-conspirators are alleged to have received approximately 1,610 bitcoins in ransom payments from the victim companies, which was valued at over $15 million at the time of payment."
Ryuk was a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation active between August 2018 and mid-2020 that became notorious after launching a massive wave of attacks targeting the healthcare sector during the COVID-19 pandemic.
At its peak, the Ryuk ransomware group hacked around 20 victims every week, collecting more than $150 million in ransoms.
Following Ryuk's shutdown in 2020, the Wizard Spider cybercrime gang behind it switched to Conti ransomware, which quickly became one of the most prolific hacker groups.
However, Conti also disbanded in 2022 after its internal chats and source code were leaked in May 2022, and it splintered into multiple smaller units that infiltrated existing ransomware gangs or launched new operations.

articles.title: Rank wants to pool Nigeria’s savings into a wealth engine
articles.text:
Saving money in Nigeria has become easier, but turning those savings into wealth remains harder. Rank, a Nigerian integrated financial services and wealth management platform, wants to close that gap by pooling people’s savings so they can access investments and financial services that may be out of reach individually.
Its model is simple: combine small savings into larger pools of capital that can invest in assets and opportunities typically available to wealthier investors. The pitch comes as formal saving grows in Nigeria, with 38% of adults—69% of those with a transactional account—saving formally, according to Enhancing Financial Innovation & Access (EFInA)’s 2023 survey.
Rank sees saving as only the first step. By pooling its users’ money, it creates larger pools of capital that can access investments that may be out of reach for individuals. The company does this through financial communities that pool contributions, create scale, and give members access to investments, credit, and other financial services.
“Rank is a wealth management company, and what we are trying to do is change what wealth management is for young people,” Femi Iromini, CEO and co-founder, told TechCabal in an interview.
“The intention of saving is meant to lead to financial freedom one day or wealth creation. And after 10 years, what we are seeing is more like a savings fatigue where people have saved for years, but then the path to wealth creation is still blocked.”
The problem with saving alone
Investment is, in part, a volume game. The more capital an investor controls, the more opportunities, pricing power, and negotiating leverage they can potentially access.
“We have worked with high-net-worth individuals (HNIs) and seen a couple of things that actually give them the leverage to create wealth. The first is volume; the second is access to information; and the third is leverage. Now the three of them are connected because volume is where you have the leverage,” Iromini said.
Iromini defines HNIs as those with at least ₦100 million ($75,199.28) to invest. Most young Nigerians cannot put that much money aside, as they are trying to build savings from limited incomes already being squeezed by rising living costs. According to PiggyVest’s 2025 savings report, only one in 20 Nigerians earns more than ₦1 million ($751.99) monthly.
A young Nigerian earning ₦1 million ($751.99) monthly and saving half their income—₦500,000 ($375.99)—would need 16 years and eight months to save ₦100 million ($75,199.28), assuming no returns on their savings.
How much faster can compounding get you to ₦100m?
