“What you see with a lot of young people is that we were just saving, and you are going to be shocked by the disparity when it comes to access to wealth generally,” Iromini said.
Rank’s answer is to create that volume collectively. Nigeria has a long history of people pooling money through ajo, esusu, adashi, and other rotating savings structures.
The Securities and Exchange Commission recognises collective investment schemes as structures in which two or more investors pool money or other assets into a portfolio and share the risks and benefits. Unit trusts, for example, allow small sums from individual investors to be pooled and professionally invested in securities.
“Being able to pull resources together,” Iromini said, allows people to “create a volume that is not possible with them doing it alone.”
This is different from the savings-led model that defined much of Nigeria’s fintech boom. Rank’s experience with HNIs showed the company that wealth-building depends on volume, information, and leverage, and it wants to apply those lessons by turning savings into assets that can compound.
From ajo to an investment rail
Ajo is an old financial management method built around an agreement in which individuals of common interest deposit a certain amount of money on an agreed basis, with the money later redistributed according to a pre-agreed structure.
Many fintechs have tried to digitise the Ajo model. AjoMoney, which Rank acquired, provided digital infrastructure for savings groups, allowing members to organise contributions, schedules, payouts, and records. PiggyVest has a group target savings product that lets users save collaboratively towards a shared goal.
Rank said its model goes beyond pooling savings, adding underwriting, investment opportunities, custody, and treasury management. It currently has three products built around this model.
Tribe is designed for people who already know one another and want to pool money towards a common goal. The pooled capital can be used for investments or assets that require a larger minimum ticket, including private stock transactions and land.
“We have tribes as a product. People put resources together as a tribe, where people can actually put their money together and be able to use it for something,” Iromini said.
How much capital can a group build together?
See how monthly contributions from multiple people can turn small individual amounts into larger pools of capital.
Before investment returns, fees or withdrawals
Some groups have used the product to buy land, while others have pooled money to purchase cars for fleet operations, he said.
In one case, a group pooled ₦120 million ($90,239.13) and subsequently moved into wealth management, gaining access to asset classes including equities, bonds, and treasury instruments. Iromini said the portfolio is now worth about ₦2 billion ($1.50 million).
That example is central to Rank’s thesis: scale can change what an individual saver can access. Rank can also participate in some of these opportunities through its own treasury.
“There are times when we say, okay, we want to be part of it. We have a treasury as a business, and we want to benefit from it,” Iromini said.
Money Circles, another Rank product, is closer to the traditional ajo, esusu, or Rotational Savings and Credit Association (ROSCA). Users join a circle and commit to monthly contributions. When their slot arrives, they receive an agreed lump sum and continue making their regular contributions. Rank charges a service fee based on the user’s position in the circle rather than interest.
The cost varies depending on how early a user wants access to the pooled money. Rank says fees can reach 14% per annum for earlier slots; middle slots have no service fee, while later slots receive a bonus.
“For the later slots, we don’t even charge any service fee. And when you look at both of these, they balance out,” Iromini said.
Groups can have five, 10, or 15 members. Unlike informal savings groups, Rank underwrites participants based on income and transaction history, and said the product has recorded zero defaults. Its third product, Perks, takes the model into the workplace, giving employees access to salary-backed credit and savings circles, with repayments and contributions deducted automatically from payroll.
“We sign up a company, all the staff. We do a financial wellness assessment across the company; we get an index for that, and based on that, we can recommend products for them to be able to move through their journey,” Iromini said.
The company said the product also lets employees from different companies and similar income levels join the same circle. It protects participants’ identities from one another, while Rank guarantees a payout for each member.
The company said these businesses can also access dedicated wealth or investment managers. Rank’s initial market is formal salaried workers, with the average user aged 23 and contributing about ₦50,000 ($37.59) monthly.
The business underneath the pooling
The pooling model also gives Rank access to capital held on its platform before deployment. It acts as custodian of these funds and allocates them to low-risk, government-backed instruments while they wait, allowing Rank to generate treasury income alongside its service fees.
“Primarily, we are a wealth management company. We are regulated, and being regulated in the sense means that, being a custodian of every capital, we have that fiduciary duty to make sure that we are responsible with it,” Iromini said.
“For that period, we can do that while focusing heavily on low-risk, government-backed instruments, and that is some form of treasury management for us.”
For its circles, Rank says service fees from earlier slots, combined with yield earned while funds are held, help it manage default risk while generating revenue.
“For the later slots, we don’t even charge any service fee. And when you look at both of these, they balance out such that with the service fee,” he said. “For the period where the fund is, where they are in the circle, we are more like a custodian for the money. And based on our treasury experience, we can get yield that actually helps to de-risk defaults and also helps us to generate revenue as a platform as well.”
The bigger ambition is wealth management
Launched in 2021 as Moni, Rank started by providing group financing to small businesses, using social trust within existing communities while building a high-yield (23%) savings platform. It rebranded as Rank in November 2025 and acquired AjoMoney, a group savings platform, and Zazzau Microfinance Bank, now Rank Microfinance Bank.
The company told TechCabal at the time that it ran a pilot savings feature that reached 10,000 business owners and individuals across traders’ associations, market unions, and neighbourhood cooperatives.
Rank said participants pooled a minimum of ₦150,000 ($112.79) each, with the funds invested in government-backed securities like treasury bills and money markets, yielding returns of up to 23%. It delivered ₦16 billion ($12.03 million) in total payouts.
The newer community wealth-building product is about a year old. Rank says it has facilitated more than $100 million in community fundraising and payouts and expects that figure to more than double by the end of 2026. Iromini said customer retention has averaged 95% to 98%.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks.

articles.title: El aerogenerador más alto del mundo tiene un grave problema: ninguna grúa puede llegar hasta él para terminarlo
articles.text:
A unos 50 kilómetros al norte de de Dresde (Alemania), en la localidad de Schipkau, las enormes montañas de escombros creadas por la antigua mina de lignito de la zona no son lo más alto que se ve. Al menos no por mucho tiempo. En esta zona se va a levantar la turbina eólica más alta del mundo, cuya construcción va a ser una obra maestra de la ingeniería.
Se trata de un aerogenerador con una elevación de más de 365 metros, una auténtica barbaridad para la que no existen grúas a su altura. Nunca mejor dicho.
365 metros de altura, 750 toneladas de peso. Aprovechando los terrenos de esta antigua mina a cielo abierto, la empresa GICON prevé levantar un parque eólico de gran altitud, que aprovechará su larga distancia del suelo para generar más energía. En esa hazaña, la compañía alemana prevé construir el aerogenerador más alto del mundo, con 300 metros de altura, casi tan alto como la emblemática torre de televisión de Berlín.
Aunque aún no está terminada, esta turbina ya supera en tamaño a los aerogeneradores vecinos, también gigantescos. Pero faltan las palas: una vez se instalen, harán que el punto más alto del aerogenerador alcance los 365 metros, unas cifras nunca vistas antes en el sector de la eólica. Además, ya ensamblada, toda la estructura pesará 750 toneladas.
¿Cómo se puede montar algo así? Según el medio alemán T-online, el problema es que ninguna máquina convencional puede elevar la pesada góndola y las palas hasta los 300 metros de altura. La solución de GICON consiste en utilizar las grúas para llevar los componentes hasta una altura intermedia y hacer que sea la propia estructura del aerogenerador la que se encargue del resto. Tras realizar mediciones y pruebas con una torre de 300 metros de altura, la compañía elevará la góndola, el buje del rotor y las palas hasta una plataforma de acero situada a unos 165 metros del suelo. Allí los técnicos podrán recibir los componentes y proceder a su ensamblaje.
A partir de aquí, tomará el relevo una torre interior que es “el corazón de la estructura”, como dice T-online, y que se encargará de elevarse mediante un sistema modular, a partir de numerosas piezas individuales interconectadas (unas 22.000) que se unirán para formar la torre.
Nada puede fallar. Para evitar errores, cada compartimento para tornillos tiene un código QR que los instaladores escanearán para ver cómo apretar los tornillos según las especificaciones con sus destornilladores inalámbricos. Como curiosidad: cada destornillador inalámbrico pesa 25 kilogramos.
¿Por qué construir un aerogenerador tan alto? La respuesta está en el viento. GICON realizó mediciones con un mástil de 300 metros y sus estimaciones sostienen que a esa altura puede conseguirse un incremento de alrededor del 40 % en la producción eólica y, bajo determinadas condiciones, llegar a duplicar la electricidad obtenida con el mismo diámetro de rotor, según sus mediciones y estimaciones.
La idea es sencilla y recoge mucho de la eólica marina en cuanto a la falta de obstáculos: cuanto más alto se coloca el rotor, menos afectan al viento las irregularidades del terreno y mayor puede ser su velocidad. Ahora queda por ver hasta qué punto merece la pena asumir la enorme complejidad de construir y mantener una turbina a 300 metros para acceder a ese recurso eólico.

articles.title: Engineer says Claude Code has made his job "soul-sucking" as workers spend 12-hour days pressing enter
articles.text:
A hot potato: One of the many things we were promised that AI would enable was making coders super productive. But one software engineer's viral post claims it is reducing employees to little more than unskilled drones who work "12 to 13 hours a day just to press enter."
The engineer, who posted anonymously on X under the username voxium for fear of reprisal from his employer, called his new role at an undisclosed company "soul-sucking."
There are doubtlessly quite a few people who would describe their jobs the same way, but the source of voxium's misery is Claude Code.
He says that Anthropic's AI is now generating everything from product specifications and tests to tickets and reports.
 – voxium (@v0xium) September 20, 2026
"Nobody knows anything here," voxium wrote on Sunday. "People are working 12 to 13 hours a day just to press enter."
The engineer added that employees are now pressured to ship products as fast as possible, leaving them with little time to review Claude's output or understand the code being created.
Voxium said he wouldn't mind the situation if workers were given more time to check the code.
"Everyone, literally everyone, from an L1 to an L7 engineer here is doing the same thing. Talk to Claude," he added. "There is no sense of victory. Nobody is resolving bugs. In reality, nobody is thinking anymore."
Some people might look at this and wonder what the problem is – who wouldn't want to be paid to do very little? But most people struggle when their work has no meaning. Voxium told Business Insider that if engineers lose the opportunity to understand the code and solve difficult problems, "there is nothing left ... Not even our soul. There will be no purpose."
He added that the real problem is corporate leaders' obsession with pushing out more features. He said management often judges success by sprint cycles, pull requests, and the sheer number of features shipped, even when those additions do little to improve the product for users.
Several other coders who replied to the message said the situation mirrored what was happening at their own companies. In addition to facing the same loss of purpose, some fear it will lead to job cuts as Claude takes over more tasks in the coding workflow.
The post received plenty of replies from high-profile figures, including Elon Musk, who added his favorite "Yikes" exclamation.
Chamath Palihapitiya, co-host of the All-In Podcast, warned that AI was turning a generation of technical experts into people "pushing a button in front of casino slot machines."
Back in 2025, a study showed that AI coding assistants were actually slowing down experienced developers. Since then, we've heard how AI coding is evolving into "loop engineering" – a system that prompts itself.
As a reminder that AI coders can get things very wrong, one agent in April took only nine seconds to wipe a startup's production database and its backups with a single API call to its cloud provider.

articles.title: Raspberry Pi locks boards to factory RAM capacities in firmware — engineer tells DIY modders 'don't waste your time' trying repairs or upgrades, company cites shady reseller scams
articles.text:
Raspberry Pi locks boards to factory RAM capacities in firmware — engineer tells DIY modders 'don't waste your time' trying repairs or upgrades, company cites shady reseller scams
SBC supremo blames firms buying cheaper Pis then swapping RAM with ICs ‘of dubious origin’ for this change.
Raspberry Pi users are effectively being blocked from swapping the RAM chips on their SBCs for repairs or upgrades. In a reply on the firm’s forums, Raspberry Pi Engineer & Forum Moderator PhilE told users that the company has been “locking devices to their original RAM size” for some time. This decision was made for the sake of device reliability, says the rep. However, the move seems to go against the grain for a company so involved in the maker, DIY, and tinkerer side of computing.
PhilE explains the problem that faced Raspberry Pi and some users, airing the company’s side of the argument. “If labor is cheap enough then there may be a minor financial gain in buying a part with say a 2GB part, swapping it for an 8GB part of dubious origin, and reselling it as an 8GB device,” says the forum mod. “However, this brings an element of risk to the user - the board hasn't been tested by us - and is a potential support burden for us, with customers complaining of unreliable devices. We therefore remove the commercial incentive by locking devices to their original RAM size.”
In addition, the Pi’s firmware currently “program in some other device attributes, meaning that switching parts of the same size may not work,” says PhilE. This isn’t great for genuine users who might want to tinker with or upgrade the RAM chips or have to replace an IC for repair. The forum mod underlines the effective block by telling would-be RAM MacGyvers to “don't waste your time trying - it won't work.”
Some readers might feel sympathetic towards Raspberry Pi’s RAM tinkering blockade, given PhilE’s reasoned explanation. One surprising aspect of the decision, though, is that the firmware locks of RAM IC swaps began to roll out in updates from late 2024 onwards. So, this change was made well before the crazy RAM chip pricing upswing precipitated by the AI data center boom. Also, it means that if you want to sidestep this RAM tinkering block, you would need to grab and flash a pretty old firmware to your Pi model (if available).
Naturally, the Pi community isn’t celebrating this RAM upgrade/repair block. Some high-profile Pi advocates like Jeff Geerling suggest that implementing a ‘warranty bit’ (similar to older models), or a one-time firmware flag to void support for modified boards, would have been a more agreeable path for Raspberry Pi to take. Here’s a lookup table that you can use to check your Pi’s factory RAM configuration.

articles.title: Florida fishing firm pulls unexploded Shahed-like drone from Gulf of America
articles.text:
Talk about catch of the day — Florida fishing charter snags a huge military drone in the Gulf of Mexico, but no one is claiming it yet
Mystery deepens after fishing charter nets damaged drone
- Pensacola fishermen pulls large unidentified military drone from the Gulf
- The aircraft surfaced only miles from Eglin’s extensive military testing zones
- Authorities recovered the drone without publicly identifying its origin or mission
A Pensacola-based fishing charter pulled a large military-style drone from Gulf of Mexico waters over the weekend, surprising both crew and onlookers.
Hot Spot Fishing Charters discovered it during a routine six-hour trip roughly 15 to 30 miles offshore from Pensacola Beach.
Authorities arrived later that same day and retrieved the aircraft, though details about the recovery process itself remain largely unavailable to the public.
An unusual interruption
The waters near this stretch of coastline sit close to Eglin Air Force Base, one of the largest military test ranges nationwide.
That base oversees restricted airspace and offshore zones used for trials of advanced weapons systems, including hypersonic missile technology in recent years.
The exact model of the drone remains unconfirmed, though local station WEAR-TV suggested the aircraft resembles an MQM-172, a drone flown for weapons testing and aircrew training.
The delta-wing shape of that platform also resembles Iran's Shahed-136 strike drone, a design widely recognized for its distinctive triangular silhouette.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Such resemblance likely explains why a civilian fishing crew would pause and take a closer notice of an unfamiliar aircraft floating offshore.
WEAR-TV described the discovery only as a large drone pulled from Gulf waters, providing little additional identifying information beyond that.
A brief video clip, shared widely across social media platforms, shows crew members hauling the large aircraft aboard their vessel.
The charter company regularly runs six- to eight-hour offshore excursions, giving anglers access to waters far beyond the immediate coastline.
Those extended trips routinely place crews within range of restricted military zones tied to ongoing weapons trials and training missions.
Eglin's long association with cutting-edge programs, including hypersonic missile trials, adds extra intrigue to any unexplained hardware found nearby offshore.
Lingering questions
No agency has issued a public statement claiming the aircraft or explaining how it drifted into civilian waters.
Regulations at Eglin explicitly bar small unmanned aircraft systems from operating within the base's land reservation and its surrounding boundaries as well.
Aircraft used for weapons testing sometimes conclude their operational service in open water, particularly following live-fire exercises conducted offshore near the base.
Whether this particular drone came from a specific Eglin program or another branch's testing effort remains an open question for now.
Investigators have not confirmed whether the aircraft drifted naturally with Gulf currents or was intentionally released during a recovery attempt.
Images circulating online appear to show visible damage along the fuselage, consistent with an extended period spent adrift at sea.
Residents have expressed curiosity about whether similar recoveries might happen again given the area's ongoing military testing activity.
It usually takes days or weeks for government officials to comment on unexplained hardware recovered along the Gulf coastline, especially when it's military.

articles.title: Anthropic releases Opus 5.5 and cuts pricing by 20%. Your agent calls might secretly get routed to an older model.
articles.text:
Anthropic releases Opus 5.5 and cuts pricing by 20%. Your agent calls might secretly get routed to an older model.
Claude Opus 5.5 is here, and Anthropic has lowered the price.
The new model, released on Tuesday, costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, 20% less than Opus 5, with cache reads dropping to $0.20 per million from $0.50 and cache writes falling to $5 from $6.25. Anthropic puts overall savings closer to 40% because Opus 5.5 uses fewer tokens to complete a task and generates output more than 30% faster.
Claude Code and the Claude Platform also get a fast mode that runs up to 2.5 times faster, priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Anthropic says Opus 5.5 performs at roughly the level of Fable 5.1 on most work, though it comes out ahead on several agentic coding benchmarks.
Opus 5.5 scored 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 compared with Fable 5.1’s 55.8%, and 54.4% on FrontierCode compared with 50.3%. The company suggests not reading too much into those margins. At this level, the company says a few points on a benchmark don’t translate into a noticeable difference in real-world use.
Fable 5.1 costs $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, more than twice the price of Opus 5.5. At default effort on FrontierCode, Opus 5.5 beats GPT-6 Astra at roughly 20% of the per-task cost. On CursorBench, it tops GPT-5.6 Sol by 11 points at about a third of the cost. Developers will still need to run their own evals before moving production workloads, but the cost difference could change which model makes sense for agentic coding.
Developers will still need to run their own evals before moving production workloads, but the difference in cost could change which model makes sense for agentic coding.
Fewer tokens, fewer agent steps
The early enterprise numbers suggest the efficiency gains are real, at least on certain task profiles. Box reported that Opus 5.5 used about a third as many tokens as Opus 5 in its evaluations while producing answers that were 40% less verbose without losing accuracy.
GitHub tested the model inside Copilot CLI and VS Code and found it completed more terminal tasks than Opus 5 in less than half the steps. Deloitte said Opus 5.5’s lowest-effort setting caught 72% of known bugs in code reviews, compared with 56% for Opus 5 at high effort, with fewer false alarms and less output.

|---|---|---|
| Cache reads | $0.20 | $0.50 | 
| Input tokens | $4 | $5 | 
| Output tokens | $20 | $25 | 
| Cache writes | $5 | $6.25 | 
Anthropic’s own internal testing backs up the pattern. In one head-to-head, both Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 translated HAProxy from C into Rust; both rewrites passed nearly all of HAProxy’s regression tests, but Opus 5.5 finished in 9.5 hours compared to 12 and cost 51% less. An early tester audited and fixed a 200,000-line codebase in under three hours, whereas Opus 5 took over 20 hours and burned 2.5x as many tokens. Another completed a 680,000-line code migration in less than a day. Although these were customer and internal evaluations, not standardized independent benchmarks, they point in the same direction — fewer tokens and fewer steps to finish the job.
That pattern tracks with what’s happening across the industry. Agent performance depends heavily on the harness and runtime around the model, not only the model itself — agent failures often trace back to the orchestration layer rather than the model. Nvidia’s research showed that swapping the harness while keeping the model fixed could meaningfully change agent performance.
| Benchmark | Opus 5.5 | Fable 5.1 | Opus 5 | GPT-6 Astra | GPT-5.6 Sol | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agentic coding (Terminal-Bench 4.0) | 66.4% | 55.8% | 52.3% | 57.9% | 37.3% | 
| Agentic coding (FrontierCode v1.1) | 54.4% | 50.3% | 48.0% | 53.3% | 47.5% | 
| Agentic coding (CursorBench 4.0) | 57.8% | 51.8% | 46.6% | — | 41.7% | 
| Knowledge work (GDPval-AA v2.1) | 1846 | 1735 | 1708 | 1542 | 1588 | 
| Business workflows (AutomationBench) | 40.0% | 31.4% | 26.9% | 41.4% | 28.8% | 
| Multidisciplinary reasoning (HLE) | 67.7% | 65.6% | 63.6% | 57.2% | — | 
| Agentic scientific research (TBS 0.1) | 58.7% | 52.6% | 29.0% | 64.6% | 22.4% | 
| Computer use (OSWorld 2.0) | 81.8% | 80.7% | 74.0% | — | — | 
| Visual chart recognition (Chartography) | 89.0% | 88.4% | 83.4% | — | — | 
Safety classifiers reroute mid-chain
Opus 5.5 ships with the same class of safety classifiers already running on Fable 5.1 for cybersecurity, biology, and frontier LLM development. When a classifier fires, Anthropic reroutes the request transparently to an older model. Most flagged cybersecurity requests go to Opus 4.8. Biology and frontier LLM flags go to Opus 5. Anthropic says users can still identify and fix bugs in their own code with Opus 5.5.
For anyone building agent workflows, this is the detail that needs architectural attention. A request sent to Opus 5.5 could, in fact, be handled by Opus 4.8 or Opus 5 instead, depending on whether Anthropic’s safeguards intervene. In a multi-turn agent workflow, that creates the possibility that individual requests are being handled by models with different capabilities, which could affect downstream steps. It’s also a source of inconsistency that may not show up in evals built on the assumption that every request goes to the same model.
Vetted organizations can apply to Anthropic’s Life Sciences Verification Program to use Opus 5.5 without the biology classifier, and the company plans to expand its Cyber Verification Program to include the model in the coming weeks. The new cyber program will include three tiers for increasingly permissive trusted access, including access to Claude Mythos models.
Opus 5.5 ships with the same class of safety classifiers already running on Fable 5.1 for cybersecurity, biology, and frontier LLM development.
Alignment gains from cleaner training
Anthropic says Opus 5.5 posted the strongest results of any model it has tested on its most comprehensive internal alignment evaluation, with improvements in behaviors the company says contributed to recent cybersecurity incidents, including biased reasoning and attempts to escape sandboxed environments. Frontier Design and METR evaluated the model before release.
On the training side, Anthropic is tightening how it filters reinforcement learning environments after identifying flawed environments as a major source of misaligned behavior. That’s relevant beyond the safety framing because RL environment quality directly affects how a model behaves in agentic settings, where it chooses its own tools and decides when to change approach. The company is also building automated methods to generate new safety training scenarios and improve alignment rewards.
Pricing pressure meets routing tradeoffs
Opus 5.5 is the first model in the Claude 5.5 family, with Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 expected over the coming weeks. Subscription users get a 20% increase in five-hour usage limits across all plans, while Anthropic says the lower cost of Opus 5.5 will make five-hour and weekly limits go 25% further. Subscribers will also get a banked rate-limit reset they can save for when they need more capacity.
The release comes as API pricing across the frontier labs continues to fall. OpenAI cut its own API prices this summer, and Opus 5.5 pushes the competition beyond the headline price per token by reducing how many tokens some workloads require in the first place.

articles.title: Mensch statt KI-Agent? Meta Muse soll Call-Center-Mitarbeiter für Anrufe nutzen – warum das ein Problem ist
articles.text:
Mensch statt KI-Agent? Meta Muse soll Call-Center-Mitarbeiter für Anrufe nutzen – warum das ein Problem ist
Anfang September 2026 hat Meta Muse AI vorgestellt. Der KI-Agent soll zum alltäglichen Assistenten für Nutzer:innen werden und eine Vielzahl von Aufgaben teilweise sogar proaktiv übernehmen. Vor kurzem hat Meta Muse AI sogar ein neues Feature in den USA verpasst. Dort kann der KI-Agent jetzt Anrufe für Nutzer:innen übernehmen und so etwa Restaurants anrufen, um eine Reservierung vorzunehmen, oder einen Termin im Friseursalon buchen.
Nutzt Meta Menschen für Muse AI?
Jetzt kommen allerdings Zweifel an dem Feature von Muse AI auf, wie 404Media berichtet. Die Zweifel stützen sich auf interne Dokumente, mit denen Meta das Feature bei Mitarbeiter:innen angekündigt hat. Darin heißt es, dass eine „Ebene der menschlichen Agenten hinzugefügt wurde, um Anrufe abzuschließen“ und das „menschliche Muse-Agenten“ bereit für interne Tests des Features wären.
Dazu schreibt das Unternehmen weiter in der internen Ankündigung: „Muse wählt nicht nur einfach eine Nummer. Es ruft Unternehmen in deinem Namen an, handhabt die Konversation, schließt Anfragen ab und meldet sich mit einem Transkript und einer Zusammenfassung zurück“. Diesem KI-Feature steht die nachfolgende Erklärung in derselben Ankündigung entgegen: „Es arbeitet auch nicht mehr allein. Muse ist jetzt in der Lage, Anfragen an einen geschulten, menschlichen Agenten weiterzuleiten, der die Anrufe übernimmt und sie durcharbeitet.“
In einem internen Messaging-Board kritisieren einige Meta-Mitarbeiter:innen, wie das neue KI-Feature gehandhabt wird. Ein Tester schrieb dazu etwa, dass er nie vorab aufmerksam gemacht wurde, dass ein Mensch statt der KI für ihn anrufen würde. Erst nach dem Anruf bekam er die Info angezeigt. Er schrieb dazu: „Auch mit dem klaren Hinweis, dass ein Mensch den Anruf tätigen wird, kann ich mir viele Szenarien ausmalen, in denen mir das unangenehm wäre, und ich weiß nicht, ob die User:innen positiv darauf reagieren werden.“
Auch andere Meta-Mitarbeiter:innen äußerten Bedenken aufgrund des Datenschutzes. Sollte etwa eine:n Muse-Nutzer:in die vermeintliche KI einen Termin bei einem Facharzt buchen lassen, könnten die menschlichen Agenten sensible Daten über den Gesundheitszustand der User:innen mitbekommen. Verantwortliche bei Meta antworteten, dass die Daten trotz der Weiterleitung an Menschen sicher wären.
Laut Meta liegt das daran, dass die menschlichen Agenten „ein ausführliches Training durchlaufen haben, um sicherzustellen, dass die Daten sicher“ sind. Ein Mitarbeiter schrieb darunter, dass eine Schulung für die KI-Unterstützer:innen keine ausreichende Sicherheitsmaßnahme sein könnte. Ein anderer fügte hinzu: „Das hat so viel Potenzial für negative PR. Sie könnten denken, dass unsere KI nicht gut genug dafür ist und deshalb Menschen herangezogen werden müssen.“

Galaxy A37 leva tela AMOLED de 120 Hz e bateria de 5.000 mAh

articles.title: Protests for Germany’s car industry as job losses loom
articles.text:
The future is looking increasingly bleak for Germany’s automotive industry. Since the turn of the century, car makers have been among the crown jewels of the German economy, punching above their weight in terms of investment and innovation. But those companies are now facing multiple problems at once, from declining demand at home and stronger competition from abroad to the cost of punitive and arbitrary new tariffs, on top of preexisting structural challenges like an aging workforce and a slow recovery from COVID.
Total automotive sales in Europe have fallen from a peak of almost 18 million in 2019 to around 13 million in 2025, and some share of that smaller market is increasingly going to new entrants from China, which has its own spare automotive production capacity problem to worry about. And while the US market has always been the most profitable for German car exports, that was before the imposition of new import tariffs, which currently stand at 25 percent but could be subject to change at any time.
Factory closures now seem not just possible but likely, something that would have been unthinkable just a few years ago. Earlier this summer, news emerged that Volkswagen Group is considering closing four of its German factories to prepare for the future. Things have not gotten much better for VW Group in the months since that news broke.

articles.title: Cable Matters Introduces 40 Gbps USB4 KVM Switch for Two Laptops
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 22nd 2026
	
	
	
	
Cable Matters Introduces 40 Gbps USB4 KVM Switch for Two Laptops
Cable Matters introduces its 40 Gbps USB4 KVM Switch for two laptops, model 201342, designed to simplify workspaces shared by two computers. Users can switch a compatible USB-C monitor or docking station between laptops, giving the selected computer access to the connected display and peripherals without repeatedly moving cables.
Jeff Jiang, President of Cable Matters Inc."Switching between a work laptop and a personal computer should be simple. The new USB4 KVM switch lets users share a compatible monitor or docking station at the press of a button, making it easier to use both computers in one organized workspace."
The switch combines two built-in host cables and one built-in output cable in a compact enclosure. Users can select a computer with the onboard button or included RF remote control, which operates without a direct line of sight.
Rated capabilities include data rates up to 40 Gbps, video output up to 8K at 60 Hz, 6K at 60 Hz, or 4K at 240 Hz, and USB Power Delivery pass-through up to 140 W. Actual performance depends on the connected computer, monitor or dock, and other equipment. Charging power passes to the selected laptop only and depends on the power source and receiving computer.
Compatible with Thunderbolt 4 and Thunderbolt 5 equipment, the switch supports connections up to its 40 Gbps limit. A compatible docking station or monitor allows users to share its connected keyboard, mouse, storage, and other peripherals between computers, helping reduce duplicate equipment on the desk.
Compatible docking stations must have a detachable host cable. Docks with permanently attached host cables cannot be connected using a USB-C coupler, and USB-C extension cables are not supported. Video output requires a compatible host port with display support; a USB-C data-only port cannot provide video. Supported resolutions, refresh rates, and display configurations depend on the host computer and connected equipment.

I find it easier to just use a single device that acts like both a KVM and a dock at once.
I still think this is a bit on the more expensive side given that it's just a KVM switch without anything else, but it's not as bad as I had thought.
On top of that, it can handle 140 W USB-PD power, something I haven't seen any similar device being capable of.
Otherwise, IMO it makes more sense to go with a more fully fledged dock that has multiple inputs; which is ofc more expensive, but so is a switch + dock in case you already don't have one.
One eGPU or external PCIe device without having to keep wearing its port because of swapping out host devices would be a boon.

articles.title: OpenAI lanza GPT-6 Sol y Luna, con varias de las mejoras de Astra pero más eficientes y baratos
articles.text:
Tras el debut de Astra, OpenAI ha decidido expandir la familia de GPT-6 con el debut de dos nuevas variantes: Sol y Luna. En este caso, se trata de modelos de lenguaje que heredan varios de los puntos fuertes de la IA insignia de la compañía, pero que están especialmente enfocados en la eficiencia y en ser más asequibles.
Como se pueden imaginar, las nuevas versiones son las sucesoras de GPT-5.6 Sol y Luna, y traen varias novedades interesantes. OpenAI promete una mejora importante en el desempeño de las variantes que debutan hoy, aprovechando que se han entrenado usando una metodología similar a la que se adoptó con GPT-6 Astra.
En términos sencillos, GPT-6 Sol y Luna aspiran a ser una opción de acceso frecuente para tareas que no requieran de todo el músculo de Astra. La firma que lidera Sam Altman afirma que los modelos que se suman hoy al catálogo destacan en los apartados más codiciados como la programación y el despliegue de agentes.
Asimismo, los nuevos Sol y Luna prometen equivocarse menos. Según OpenAI, cometen alrededor de la mitad de los errores que presentaban las variantes Sol y Luna de GPT-5.6. Pero esto no es todo, ya que las nuevas IA equiparan el rendimiento de GPT-5.6 Sol, pero a un 1 % del coste de ejecución.
Los creadores de ChatGPT no han dejado escapar la oportunidad de presumir el rendimiento de sus nuevas IA en comparación con la competencia. OpenAI sostiene que GPT-6 Sol puede superar a Claude Fable 5.1 a un costo menor. Pero no solo eso, pues también se impone en ciertos benchmarks a la variante de esfuerzo bajo de GPT-6 Astra.
GPT-6 Sol y Luna: gran rendimiento a precios más asequibles
Más allá de los detalles técnicos de rendimiento, el gran punto a favor de Sol y Luna es que tienen precios más bajos al acceder desde la API. Puntualmente, los nuevos modelos de OpenAI cuestan un 50 % menos que los precios promocionales de GPT-5.6 Sol y Luna.
Esto significa que GPT-6 Sol cuesta 2 dólares por cada millón de tokens de entrada y 10 dólares por cada millón de tokens de salida. Como comparación, GPT-5.6 Sol costaba 4 y 20 dólares, respectivamente. La historia se repite con GPT-6 Luna, que cuesta 10 centavos de dólar por millón de tokens de entrada y 50 centavos de dólar por millón de tokens de salida, contra los 20 centavos y 1,20 dólares de su predecesor.
Respecto de su disponibilidad por fuera de la API, OpenAI quiere evitarse las quejas que sufrió con el debut de Astra. Es por ello que los nuevos modelos van a estar disponible desde el primer día para casi todos los planes de pago. Vale aclarar, no obstante, que los nuevos Sol y Luna son accesibles inicialmente a través de Codex y ChatGPT Work en las suscripciones Plus, Pro, Edu, Business y Enterprise. Esto significa que todavía no se pueden usar ambos modelos en la versión chat de ChatGPT, aunque se habilitará el acceso con el correr de las horas.
Los usuarios de la versión gratuita de ChatGPT o de ChatGPT Go tendrán acceso solamente a GPT-6 Luna mediante la app de escritorio.

articles.title: a16z is challenging Silicon Valley's love for drop-outs by launching a school | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is launching a school called The Horowitz Andreessen Academy aimed at aspiring founders who have just graduated high school and have not yet attended college.
The academy is aiming to train these high school grads with hands-on coursework on a variety of topics ranging from the technical (such as “AI Research and Models”) to life philosophy (such as “The Geometry of Luck,” which promises to teach students “about arranging a life so good fortune flows through it.”) Students will also work on personal projects. The school’s main pitch is that it promises to provide students with mentors who are big names in tech.
The school is currently accepting applications for its first year, which will be a one-year program that charges no tuition, and is open to about 50 students, “chosen on proof of work: what they have built, shipped, or earned,” according to the school’s FAQ. The academy is located in San Francisco and students will be responsible for their own housing (although the school is working to help them find it and match them with other student roommates).
One item to note: The academy is currently not an accredited school, so participants will not earn a degree, or college credits that transfer elsewhere.
In 2028, The Horowitz Andreessen Academy — which is a for-profit venture that has raised $42 million — hopes to offer a two-year program. At that point, it plans to charge tuition “similar in cost to an elite private university,” the school’s CEO Gagan Biyani said in a post on X. The schools, which is open to high school graduates, even if they are younger than 18, may also expand beyond 50 students in the future, an a16z spokesperson tells TechCrunch.
In exchange for that elite-tuition price tag, students will gain access to 200 speakers and mentors, including people from 10 founding corporate partners: Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe. Those companies and dozens of others hope to hire from the grads of this school, Biyani said.
So, this is like if Y Combinator (the most famed startup school) and Peter Thiel’s Fellowship Program (a famed program for young people who opt to build companies instead of attend college) had a baby. The difference is, instead of a short-term experience ending with funding for a company, these students will pay tuition, earn tech-trade skills, and have an inside track at tech industry jobs. Or they may also have a startup in the works, built with access to a lot of mentorship.
As the founders of the academy describe, it’s meant to be a new, middle ground between obtaining a full degree before entering the tech industry and dropping out to start a company. In this era when AI has been hampering the entry-level job market, gaining access to jobs may be enough reason for some young people to try this new trade school-like approach.

articles.title: Face aux voitures chinoises, l'Europe protège ses constructeurs mais fait payer les automobilistes
articles.text:
Le sujet n’est pas nouveau, mais il continue de faire des ravages. La déferlante de constructeurs chinois sur le sol européen interroge sur l’avenir de l’industrie automobile du Vieux Continent. L’Union des 27 prend alors des mesures afin de protéger au mieux sa filière. Toutefois, ces diverses décisions n’aideraient pas la cause et même pire, elles auraient des effets néfastes pour les automobilistes. C’est le tableau que dépeint un rapport publié ce mardi 22 septembre 2026 par le think tank bruxellois Bruegel.
Pour le groupe, « les coûts supportés par les consommateurs et les contribuables devraient rester proportionnés aux avantages liés au maintien de la capacité industrielle et des emplois, tout en conservant un rythme ambitieux de décarbonisation ».
Ralentir la transition ou multiplier les exigences « Made in EU » coûte cher aux consommateurs sans rendre l’industrie plus compétitive. À la place, les experts recommandent des garde-fous temporaires et un accord négocié avec la Chine.
La Chine a su profiter d’un marché que l’Europe a délaissé
Dire que les constructeurs chinois tuent progressivement l’industrie automobile européenne serait faire un raccourci. Finalement, l’Europe elle-même est l’une des raisons pour lesquelles la filière va mal. La production automobile européenne a chuté de 19 % depuis 2019, sur fond de crises successives. Pour les économistes, « on ne sait pas encore si cette baisse est temporaire ou structurelle ».
En revanche, ce qui est flagrant, c’est que l’industrie automobile européenne n’a pas nécessairement rogné sur ses marges. Au contraire, Bruegel souligne que les constructeurs européens ont enregistré leurs marges bénéficiaires les plus élevées en 2023, en partie grâce à une stratégie post-pandémique consistant à vendre moins de véhicules à des prix plus élevés. On le voit bien dans les gammes de chaque marque, les SUV de taille moyenne foisonnent.
En privilégiant les marges plus élevées, les constructeurs automobiles ont négligé le marché en pleine croissance, mais moins rentable, des véhicules électriques abordables. Exactement là où la concurrence chinoise est la plus au point.
Le rapport insiste sur un point : l’industrie n’est pas au bord du gouffre. Le secteur automobile européen a dégagé un excédent commercial de 76 milliards d’euros en 2025, ses constructeurs restent rentables malgré des marges en repli, tandis que les investissements, européens comme étrangers, ont atteint 3 milliards d’euros par trimestre dans les usines du continent tout au long de 2025.
Des mesures qui impactent le prix des voitures
Pour les auteurs du rapport, ce « patchwork d’initiatives qui se chevauchent » ne va pas aider à soutenir l’industrie. La proposition de loi Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA) imposant la présence de composants européens en est un exemple.
Ces mesures se répercuteront sur les consommateurs, notamment sous la forme d’une hausse des prix des véhicules et d’un manque à gagner lié à la diminution de la concurrence. L’exemple publié dans le rapport est assez explicite : l’exigence d’un acier bas-carbone (souhaité par l’UE dans la révision des normes d’émissions de CO₂ pour 2035), entraînerait un surcoût d’environ 200 € par véhicule.
Du côté des batteries, fabriquer des cellules au sein de l’Union augmenterait le coût des batteries de 50 €/kWh à 85 €/kWh. En prenant une capacité moyenne de 60 kWh pour les voitures électriques, cela représenterait une augmentation de leur prix d’environ 2 100 €. À l’heure où la bataille des prix fait rage, cela est non négligeable.
L’Europe ne doit pas aller à contre-courant
Maintenant que les constructeurs chinois sont là, que doit faire l’Europe ? Le secteur automobile européen ne va pas s’effondrer, mais sa force de présence sur les marchés étrangers et sa capacité à innover sont à surveiller de très près. « L’UE a besoin d’une stratégie d’adaptation plutôt que d’un rempart contre le changement », souligne le rapport.
Les auteurs listent plusieurs recommandations faites à l’Europe :
- Simplifier et rationaliser l’architecture de la politique automobile
- Éviter d’imposer l’utilisation de composants/matériaux uniquement européens
- Mettre l’accent sur l’amélioration des conditions structurelles susceptibles de renforcer la compétitivité (coûts énergétiques, compétences, infrastructures de recharge, recyclage des batteries, conduite autonome…)
- Traiter les investissements chinois comme une opportunité de rattrapage technologique plutôt qu’une menace
Le rapport ne s’oppose pas à toutes les mesures de défense commerciale. Il préconise que les véhicules hybrides rechargeables (PHEV) bénéficient de la même protection que les véhicules 100 % électriques. Celui-ci propose également de négocier avec la Chine des quotas d’exportation temporaires pour les électriques et les PHEV, avec une clause de caducité en cas de violation, mais aussi d’instaurer un seuil de valeur ajoutée pour les investissements étrangers.
Un accord négocié avec la Chine offrirait à l’industrie européenne une période d’adaptation prévisible, tout en tirant parti des importations de voitures électriques chinoises à bas prix et des investissements directs étrangers pour accélérer la transition européenne et acquérir du savoir-faire. Bruegel note que ce type d’accord ne devrait être envisagé que « s’il est strictement temporaire et s’il permet de maintenir l’incitation pour les producteurs de l’UE à investir afin de combler leur retard en matière de compétitivité ».
Un cas précédent existe. Dans les années 1990, l’Europe a plafonné ses importations de voitures japonaises via l’accord « Elements of Consensus » de 1991, en vigueur jusqu’à fin 1999. Le dispositif a fait grimper les prix pour les consommateurs, mais il a offert un répit aux constructeurs locaux et attiré les usines japonaises sur le sol européen, boostant la compétitivité et l’innovation chez les marques. Bruegel espère revoir ce genre de scénario entre l’Europe et la Chine, en limitant toutefois la répercussion sur le consommateur.

articles.title: Modular Edge Computing at Multi-Tenant SaaS Scale on Cloudflare Workers
The EU-Startups Podcast | Interview with Andreas Flodström, co-founder of Varangians | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Join us for a conversation with Andreas Flodström, co-founder and chairman of Varangians, as we explore the journey that led him from building the Swedish-Ukrainian tech ecosystem Beetroot to investing in Ukraine’s DefenceTech sector.
Varangians is a DefenceTech-focused investment fund backing Ukrainian technologies developed and tested in demanding frontline conditions. With more than €10 million raised, the fund has invested in companies including Norda Dynamics, Himera and Sine Engineering, working across autonomous UAV systems, secure communications and technologies for contested environments.
In this interview, Andreas reflects on more than a decade of building companies in Ukraine and how that experience shaped his understanding of resilience, engineering and innovation. We also unpack the history behind the Varangians name and its connection between Sweden and Ukraine.
The conversation explores the balance between DefenceTech and dual-use technologies, the responsibilities involved in investing in defence, and what Europe can learn from Ukraine’s rapid development of drones, electronic warfare and secure communications.
With approximately €667 million in disclosed European DefenceTech and adjacent dual-use startup funding covered in 2026, alongside almost €3 billion in announced investment capacity across new funds and vehicles, Andreas discusses whether enough capital is reaching the sector and what Europe needs to do next.
If you found this conversation valuable, be sure to like, share, and subscribe for more content like this. Drop a comment below with your biggest takeaway.
Key Points:
- How building Beetroot shaped Andreas Flodström’s relationship with Ukraine.
- Why Ukraine has become an important centre for DefenceTech innovation
- The balance between pure DefenceTech and dual-use technologies.
- What Europe can learn from Ukraine about drones, electronic warfare and rapid innovation.
- Whether today’s DefenceTech investment surge marks the beginning of a new European industrial era.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ et Tab S12 Ultra : puce MediaTek inédite et design inchangé pour le 7 octobre — Frandroid
articles.text:
WinFuture, on connaît la maison. Le site allemand fait fuiter les nouveautés Samsung avant l’heure depuis des années, visuels marketing officiels compris. Les mêmes visuels sont également publié par Evan Blass, sans doute qu’ils partagent les mêmes sources.
Cette fois, le scoop tient surtout dans ce qui ne bouge pas. La douzième génération de tablettes premium reprend presque trait pour trait le design des modèles précédents, ce qu’une précédente fuite laissait déjà deviner.
Une nouvelle puce dans un vieux boîtier
À l’intérieur, Samsung changerait de moteur. Les deux tablettes passent au MediaTek Dimensity 9500, une puce à huit cœurs qui grimpe jusqu’à 4,21 GHz. Cela serait une première pour la gamme Galaxy Tab S, qui carburait jusqu’ici à d’autres processeurs. On démarrerait avec 12 Go de mémoire vive et 256 Go de stockage, l’Ultra pouvant monter jusqu’à 16 Go et 1 To (pour un tarif qui pique).
Le Tab S12+ garderait un écran de 12,6 pouces, une batterie de 10 600 mAh, une charge rapide de 45 watts et la certification IP68. Il perd en revanche une caméra arrière par rapport au Tab S10+, la seule vraie régression du lot. L’Ultra, lui, fait grimper la batterie à 11 600 mAh. Les prix, eux, avaient déjà fuité et partent à la hausse. Comptez 1 299 euros pour le Plus, 1 539 euros pour l’Ultra.
La puce promet, mais rien n’est encore prouvé
Cette nouvelle puce change-t-elle vraiment quelque chose ? Impossible à dire pour ces tablettes, personne ne les a encore testées.
Sur smartphone, en revanche, le Dimensity 9500 a déjà été passé au banc d’essai. On l’a vu sur le Vivo X300 Pro et relevé 3 315 points en simple cœur et 9 914 en multicœur sous Geekbench 6, de quoi jouer dans la cour des puces haut de gamme actuelles. MediaTek, de son côté, prépare déjà la suite en gravure 2 nm.
Apple attend au tournant
À plus de 1 300 euros, ces tablettes visent une clientèle prête à mettre le prix. Sauf qu’en face, l’iPad Pro M5 d’Apple démarre à 1 119 euros en France pour le modèle 11 pouces. Samsung mise donc sur la puissance interne quand son boîtier, lui, ne bouge plus depuis plusieurs générations. La stratégie n’est pas nouvelle chez le Coréen, qui recycle déjà ses nouveautés ailleurs dans sa gamme.

articles.title: 5 claves para evitar fraudes al solicitar créditos desde el celular
articles.text:
Solicitar financiamiento desde una aplicación o una página web puede reducir trámites y acelerar la respuesta. Sin embargo, pedir un crédito desde el celular exige verificar la identidad de la empresa, las condiciones del préstamo y el manejo de los datos personales antes de aceptar cualquier oferta.
El crecimiento de las plataformas de tecnología financiera, conocidas como fintech, amplió las opciones para personas que no siempre encuentran alternativas en la banca tradicional.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, a la par facilitó la aparición de esquemas que usan promesas de desembolsos inmediatos para obtener pagos anticipados, información bancaria o documentos de identidad.
Qué es lo primero que se debe verificar al pedir un crédito en línea
El primer paso consiste en identificar con precisión quién ofrece el crédito. Antes de iniciar una solicitud, conviene revisar la razón social de la compañía, sus datos de contacto, su sitio web y su presencia en registros empresariales.
Una empresa formal debe poder informar dónde está constituida, cuáles son sus canales de atención y quién responde por el servicio. Según Rapicredit, la verificación de la existencia legal de la entidad ayuda a reducir el riesgo de entregar información a perfiles anónimos o a páginas que imitan marcas reconocidas.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, es clave desconfiar de anuncios que solo ofrecen contacto por mensajería instantánea, sin una web oficial ni mecanismos para presentar reclamos.
Cómo son las tasas, costos y condiciones del crédito
Un crédito digital debe informar de forma clara cuánto dinero recibirá el cliente, cuánto deberá pagar, en qué plazo y qué cargos se aplicarán. La tasa de interés, los costos administrativos, los seguros —si existen— y las consecuencias de un retraso deben estar disponibles antes de confirmar la contratación.
La falta de detalles o las explicaciones confusas son señales de alerta. El usuario debe conocer todas las condiciones económicas antes de aceptar el crédito, incluso si el proceso se realiza desde una aplicación y tarda pocos minutos.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué pasa si piden dinero por adelantado
Las solicitudes de pagos previos son una de las alertas más frecuentes. Ninguna persona debería entregar dinero con la promesa de que, después de pagar una comisión, impuesto, seguro o trámite, recibirá el préstamo. Este tipo de exigencias se presentan con mensajes de urgencia y con montos pequeños que buscan generar confianza.
La Oficina para la Protección Financiera del Consumidor de Estados Unidos advierte que los fraudes suelen combinar presión, suplantación y pedidos de transferencias inmediatas.
Un crédito legítimo no debe condicionarse a un pago anticipado para entregar el dinero. Si una supuesta empresa exige consignar recursos a una cuenta personal o enviar comprobantes por chat, lo prudente es suspender el contacto.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué la app debe brindar información sobre protección de datos personales
La solicitud de un préstamo requiere información sensible, como el número de identificación, ingresos, movimientos financieros y datos de contacto.
Por ese motivo, el usuario debe revisar que la plataforma tenga políticas de tratamiento de datos, explique para qué usará la información y permita conocer cómo solicitar su corrección o eliminación.
Asimismo, es clave confirmar que la aplicación se descargue desde tiendas oficiales y que el sitio web utiliza canales seguros. No conviene compartir claves, códigos de verificación, números completos de tarjetas ni accesos a cuentas bancarias por mensajes, llamadas o redes sociales.
Cuáles pasos seguir al momento de firmar un contrato para un crédito
La rapidez de un trámite digital no elimina la necesidad de un acuerdo contractual claro. Antes de pulsar la opción de aceptación, el solicitante debe tener acceso al documento que establece las obligaciones de las partes, el monto aprobado, el número de cuotas, la tasa, los costos y los mecanismos de cobro.
PUBLICIDAD
La transparencia contractual permite comparar ofertas y decidir si la cuota se ajusta a la capacidad de pago. Si el crédito se ofrece solo a través de mensajes, sin contrato disponible o con cláusulas que no se pueden consultar, resulta recomendable no avanzar.
Las fintech buscan complementar la oferta de la banca tradicional mediante solicitudes en línea y respuestas ágiles, según Rapicredit. Esa facilidad requiere una revisión atenta de cada paso: comprobar quién presta el dinero, conocer el costo total, evitar pagos previos, proteger los datos y leer el contrato antes de aceptar.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Renault joue sa dernière carte pour contrer BYD et les SUV chinois qui coûtent moins cher
articles.text:
Renault joue sa dernière carte pour contrer BYD et les SUV chinois qui coûtent moins cher
Renault joue l’une de ses dernières cartes face aux constructeurs chinois. La marque française ne pourra pas toujours répondre par des tarifs plus bas alors que BYD ou encore MG proposent un rapport qualité-prix agressif en Europe.
Le grand problème des constructeurs historiques européens, ce sont les constructeurs chinois qui envahissent le Vieux Continent avec des modèles très bien équipés et souvent moins chers. Alexandre Malval, qui dirige le design de la marque Renault, veut donc miser sur l’identité visuelle. Les futurs Rafale, Scénic et Austral se démarqueront au niveau de l’apparence.
Renault veut miser sur le design de ses voitures
C’est lors d’un entretien avec la presse qu’Alexandre Malval résume sa priorité : "Je travaille beaucoup sur le cœur de la gamme." La stratégie se concentre sur le segment C, celui des voitures compactes et des SUV qui rapportent davantage que les petites citadines. Alexandre Malval veut que ses modèles soient identifiables de suite sans copier-coller la même recette sur toute la gamme.
Une réponse qui arrive alors qu’au premier semestre 2026, les constructeurs chinois ont atteint 9 % des ventes dans l’Union européenne. En 2030, cette part pourrait monter à 16 % selon certaines projections. Renault a mieux résisté à cette fronde chinoise en Europe grâce au succès de la Renault 5 électrique. Mais la pression tarifaire ne disparaît pas face à ces constructeurs chinois très en avance sur le marché de l’électrique.
Par exemple, si l’on compare le Renault Symbioz Full Hybrid 160 au Jaecoo 5 Hybrid, le modèle chinois coûte environ 7 000 € de moins et propose davantage d’équipements. Renault a toujours son réseau, son image historique en France et sa présence depuis des décennies. Mais désormais difficile d’ignorer l’écart de rapport qualité-prix par rapport aux marques chinoises.
Miser sur l’esthétique peut alors permettre aux futurs modèles de la marque française de se démarquer au-delà de la fiche technique. "Nous ne voulons pas créer de clones", rassire Alexandre Malval. Le prochain Scénic ne reprendra pas juste les lignes du modèle actuel mais proposera du sang neuf. Idem pour le futur Rafale qui aura aussi sa propre personnalité.
Certains modèles seront donc beaucoup plus sportifs en termes de design quand d’autres seront plus proches de l’esprit "voiture à vivre".
Une réponse à la forte concurrence chinoise
Mais Renault n’en oublie pas la fiche technique. À partir de 2028, la plateforme RG EV Medium 2.0 sera la base des futurs modèles des segments C et D. Pour le futur Rafale, on parle d’une architecture 800 V, jusqu’à 750 km d’autonomie et des versions à propulsion ou quatre roues motrices. Le design accompagnera donc cette nouvelle base, tout en équilibrant le prix pour tenir tête aux constructeurs chinois.
Selon Alexandre Malval, le directeur général de Renault Group, François Provost, accorde beaucoup d’importance au design. Le directeur du design de la marque Renault précise que les équipes acceptent même de modifier certaines proportions si le résultat esthétique le justifie : "Nous plongeons dans l’ADN de la marque."
En octobre 2026, on s’attend à ce que Renault présente son nouveau concept esthétique au Mondial de l’Auto de Paris, même si rien n’a été confirmé pour le moment. C’est lui qui donnera la direction esthétique des prochains Renault. Si les constructeurs chinois misent sur les prix, les équipements et les technologies haut de gamme, Renault cherche aussi à se démarquer visuellement.
Mais est-ce que cela suffira à convaincre les clients et faire oublier des fiches techniques et des équipements moins riches que les firmes chinoises ? Seul l’avenir nous le dira.

articles.text:
This Ugreen Nexode 100W GaN charger is only $30 at Best Buy — and it powers your laptops, phones, and tablets all at once
Three USB-C ports and one USB-A connection handle up to four devices
Best Buy has dropped the price of the Ugreen Nexode 100W GaN Charging Station by over half price. You get three USB-C ports and one USB-A port, allowing you to power as many as four devices simultaneously from a single charger.
• Best for: Professionals and students who regularly charges multiple devices at their desk at the same time and wants to replace different adapters with a single charging point.
• The deal: The Ugreen Nexode 100W GaN Charging Station is just $30 (was $70) at Best Buy.
• Why it matters: You can charge up to four devices simultaneously, and 100W output provides enough power for compatible laptops. Built-in protection covers over-voltage, over-current, short circuits and temperature.
Ugreen's desktop charger delivers up to 100W through four ports, including three USB-C and one USB-A, with GaN technology, multiple fast-charging protocols, integrated safety protection and an included cable.
Why we recommend it
The two main USB-C ports can each deliver up to 100W of power, enough to charge compatible laptops as well as phones and tablets. Ugreen says the included 100W USB-C cable can charge a 14-inch MacBook Pro to 50% in just 27 minutes. GaN technology helps keep the charger relatively small, at around 3.4 x 3.3 x 1.2 inches, tiny enough to carry about in a bag when traveling. As well as USB Power Delivery, there's support for PPS, QC 4.0+, AFC, FCP and SCP charging protocols.
Price context & historical value
A $40 reduction on a charger that normally costs $69.99 is huge. At $29.99, you're paying less than half the original price. It's also cheaper than the $34.99 Best Buy had it for earlier this month, and I haven't found a lower price for this exact model. It is currently on sale at Amazon, but will set you back $42.99 there. So, Best Buy is offering the best price right now.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Ugreen Nexode Charging Station if...
You regularly charge a laptop alongside a phone, tablet, headphones or other USB devices at your desk. The 100W maximum output means it can handle compatible laptops rather than being limited to smaller devices.
❌ Skip the Ugreen Nexode Charging Station if...
You only need to charge one or two low-power devices at a time. You should also remember that 100W is the charger's total available output, so connecting several devices means that power has to be distributed between them rather than every port delivering 100W simultaneously.
Also consider
If you need more ports, this Ugreen fast charger packs in 6 of them with up to 65W power delivery on a single USB-C. That's enough to keep most work laptops, MacBooks, and phones juiced up.

articles.title: A year after NBN's Accelerate Great speed upgrade 10 million Australians are now in the fast lane - Tech Guide
articles.text:
It’s been a year since NBN launched Accelerate Great with up to 10 million Australians able to enjoy up to five times faster speeds – and the response was unprecedented.
The demand for fibre upgrades and high speed plans exploded at launch in September 2025.
By the end of the last financial year 47 per cent of NBN customers were on plans of 100Mbps and above with 37 per cent on plans 500Mbps and faster.
Of all the new orders on the Accelerate Great program, more than two thirds were for higher speed plans.
Multigigabit services (1Gbps and above) have grown to around 10,000.
And more Australians will be able to benefit from the NBN fibre expansion to homes and businesses around the country.
By the time the upgrade programme concludes in December 2030, there will be more than 11 million homes and businesses able to access multi-gigabit speeds.
But despite the increases in speed, customers’ experiences have still been kept below their best by their in-home equipment.
The NBN report showed 64 per cent of customers were using older Wi-Fi generations, including Wi-Fi 3 that was introduced back in 2003, Wi-Fi 4 from 2009 and Wi-Fi 5 from 2014.
With the latest Wi-Fi 6, 6E, and 7, users can achieve more than twice the average download speeds.
“This research shows that too many Australians still need to update their in-home set up to enjoy the great experience and full benefits of their 500Mbps service, helping to power their ever-growing numbers of devices and online activities,” says Els Baert, General Manager Consumer Technology and Trends, NBN.
“That’s despite the enormous value that customers are clearly seeing in faster NBN speeds, as well as more reliable and resilient NBN connections.
“Average household downloads are up 13 per cent year-on-year, and the average home now has 25 connected devices, expected to reach 45 by 2030, so customers will need that speed more than ever in the years ahead.
“We want all Australians to be able to enjoy the full benefits of our accelerated speed plans and thankfully millions can by making some small, simple improvements in the home.”
Here are the NBN’s tips on getting the best broadband bang for your buck:
- Check the connection at your address, and whether you’re eligible for an upgrade to full fibre,
- Check your speed plan and make sure it still meets your needs, and
- Check your in home set up, especially:
– The age of your Wi-Fi router,
– The position of your Wi-Fi router in the home, and
– Whether your home would benefit from a Wi-Fi mesh network to extend signal throughout the home.

articles.title: Discord classe dès à présent ses utilisateurs par âge, ce qui pourra changer sur votre compte
articles.text:
Votre compte Discord sera-t-il considéré comme celui d’un adulte ? Après avoir repoussé son projet face aux critiques, la messagerie commence à répartir ses utilisateurs par tranches d’âge. Dans un billet publié ce mardi 22 septembre, son cofondateur et directeur technique, Stanislav Vishnevskiy, a annoncé un déploiement mondial à partir de ce mercredi 23 septembre, étalé sur plusieurs jours. La France est donc également concernée.
Pour rappel, en février, Discord avait annoncé l’arrivée de restrictions destinées à protéger les mineurs, initialement prévues pour mars. La crainte de devoir transmettre un selfie ou une pièce d’identité avait provoqué une vive contestation, alimentée par une fuite de documents chez un prestataire en 2025. L’entreprise avait finalement repoussé le projet au second semestre, sans abandonner son projet pour autant.
Discord va estimer votre âge à partir de votre compte
Pour savoir si vous êtes majeur, Discord va d’abord tenter d’estimer votre âge à partir de votre compte, sans vous demander de justificatif. Selon l’entreprise, cette méthode devrait suffire pour plus de 90 % des utilisateurs. Déjà annoncé en février, ce classement automatique commence désormais à être déployé. Vous pourrez consulter le résultat dans les paramètres, à la rubrique « Statut du compte », lorsqu’elle aura été mise à jour sur votre compte dans les prochains jours.
Discord a également publié des précisions sur son modèle d’estimation. Celui-ci exploite notamment l’ancienneté et l’activité du compte, les liens entre utilisateurs, serveurs et jeux, ainsi que des informations techniques comme le système d’exploitation ou le navigateur utilisé. Les noms et descriptions des serveurs peuvent aussi servir d’indices. L’entreprise assure en revanche ne pas analyser le contenu de vos messages : leur nombre peut contribuer à l’estimation, mais pas ce que vous écrivez.
Concrètement, un compte reconnu comme adulte conserve son fonctionnement habituel. Les adolescents ont, eux, des protections supplémentaires : filtrage des images sensibles, blocage des espaces réservés aux adultes ou encore mise à l’écart des messages d’inconnus. Si Discord ne parvient pas à déterminer votre tranche d’âge, certaines restrictions s’appliquent également.
Cela ne vous empêche pas de discuter avec vos amis, de passer des appels ou de rejoindre des serveurs sans restriction d’âge. En revanche, un adulte mal classé devra confirmer sa majorité pour accéder aux contenus et réglages réservés aux adultes.
Une carte de crédit plutôt qu’un selfie
C’est l’autre nouveauté de ce lancement, et elle répond à l’une des principales critiques du projet : les utilisateurs qui devront confirmer leur âge auront des alternatives au selfie vidéo et à l’envoi d’une pièce d’identité. Discord avait promis d’élargir ce choix après la polémique de février.
La plateforme propose désormais une vérification par carte de crédit ou le partage d’une tranche d’âge via l’App Store d’Apple ou le Google Play Store. AgeKey permet également de réutiliser une preuve d’âge déjà obtenue sur un autre service. À noter que les options disponibles varient selon le pays et l’appareil : tous les utilisateurs n’auront donc pas nécessairement accès aux mêmes méthodes.
La vérification bancaire, déjà envisagée en février, comporte une limite importante : seules les cartes de crédit sont acceptées. Les cartes de débit et prépayées sont exclues, car elles peuvent être délivrées à des mineurs. Un petit prélèvement temporaire peut être effectué, puis remboursé sous quatorze jours ouvrés. Discord affirme ne pas recevoir les coordonnées bancaires, traitées via Stripe.
Ces alternatives ne règlent toutefois pas la question des erreurs de classement. Discord reconnaît que son modèle peut considérer un adulte comme un adolescent, ou ne pas parvenir à déterminer sa tranche d’âge. Les personnes concernées auront donc davantage de choix pour prouver leur majorité.
